name: Midnight: Add Spirit Board

children.key: While walking through the spaceport you notice an old woman performing some kind of fortune telling or seance. She looks at you and says, "Captain <last>, the dead call to you. Would you hear them?"

She smiles, "The spirits demand to be heard by you. I dare not deny them." She has a board lying on the table adorned with letters and numbers. Sitting atop the board is a large metal ring. "Come, sit." She motions to the chair opposite her.
"Good. <first>, do as I do." She rests the tips of her fingers on the metal ring."

You look down at the metal circle. It is just large enough to encircle the letters and numbers on the board. After resting your fingers on it, you notice the woman's eyes are closed. "Clear your thoughts. Let it guide you."

As as you your eyes close, you feel the ring start to move. Instinctively, you move your hands to keep up. After several moments of what seems like random movements over the board, it stops. Opening your eyes, you see the letter 'R' sitting inside the metal ring.
The old woman speaks, "Remember this and close your eyes when you are ready to continue."
The process is repeated several times...
The woman stares directly into your eyes. "The spirits have spoken."
You ask her what the message means, but she remains silent, staring into your eyes...
You pull out your gun. She remains silent, staring into your eyes...

Before you can do anything else, you feel a sharp pain in your chest! There's a bloody blade sticking out from there. Someone must have stabbed you through the back while you were distracted by the fortune teller. You crumple to the ground, your strength rapidly fading away. Death claims you, the message spelled out on the board no longer relevant.

You leap up from your chair and run towards the <ship>'s landing pad. A few shots stray past, narrowly missing you. The old lady was clearly a distraction for someone who wants you dead. An interceptor makes a strafing run on your ship, but you activate the shields in time. Skipping the routine pre-flight safety checks, you launch before they make another pass.
As you leave, the old lady calls out to you, "Even if you ignore the dead, death will still catch you."

name: Midnight Popcorn: Deep Archaeology 1
description: Drop this archaeologist off on <destination>, before making a trip to Midgard in the Deep to collect some samples.

values: Drop this archaeologist off on <destination>, before making a trip to Midgard in the Deep to collect some samples.

children.key: As you are walking through the spaceport, a man in an expensive suit approaches you. "Pardon me, Captain," he says. "I wonder if you would be willing to talk privately about a very lucrative job opportunity."
"Sure, let's return to my ship and talk there."
"Not illegal," he says, "but it could help to uncover a secret with enormous ramifications. A secret that certain people do not want known."
"Okay," you say, "let's return to my ship, and I'll hear you out."

You lead him back to your ship. "I'm an archaeologist," he explains, "studying the early history of the space era. And in particular, a set of persistent folk tales about contact with alien species. Many of these tales have to do with the region of the galaxy we call the Deep. I need someone to travel to Midgard and retrieve some samples from an ancient site there."
"What sort of samples? Will this get me in trouble?"

"Well, let's just say I've made myself somewhat unpopular in the Deep," he says. "Asking too many questions. If I were seen walking around on Midgard, they would probably ask me to leave immediately."
You say, "And, is the work you're asking me to do going to make me equally unpopular?"
"Not if you are circumspect," he says. "I need two samples from a certain village. One is simple: wood from a living or recently deceased tree. Any tree will do."

He pauses for a minute, then continues. "The other is more... sensitive. There is a historical site on Midgard, an ancient church. Not something they publish in the official tourist guides, mind you. I need a small sample of the wood that the church is built with. A small splinter would suffice."
"Sure, if it's in the interest of science, I can do that."
"You're asking me to vandalize a historical site?"

"I need only the tiniest of samples," he says, "maybe a splinter of wood that is already peeling off, or from a place where the wood is worn and cracked. And what we discover from that sample could be of immense importance."
"Sorry, that sounds a bit too shady to me."

"Thank you," he says. "Trust me, this could give us some very important information. I'll need you to drop me off on Vinci first, to meet with some scientists. We can then meet up back on Vinci once you have the samples."

values: You land on <planet>, but realize that your escort carrying the archaeologist hasn't entered the system yet. Better depart and wait for it.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Midnight Popcorn: Deep Archaeology 1

name: Midnight Popcorn: Remnant: Learn Sign 1
description: Travel to <destination> for more lessons on how to speak using Remnant sign language.

values: Travel to <destination> for more lessons on how to speak using Remnant sign language.

children.key: As you make your way through the spaceport, you become increasingly aware of how quiet it is. Looking around, you note that it doesn't seem any less busy than usual, just that only a handful of people are paying attention to you. As a result, they have reverted to their normal gestures instead of singing. It feels oddly isolating, and eerie, to realize that there are hundreds of conversations going on around you, yet you can't understand a single one.
Looking around the spaceport, you eventually find someone at what looks like an information desk.
"I would like to learn your sign language."
(Sing a short verse about not understanding people because my hands are still.)
She looks at you with a confused expression, her hands making a few quick gestures. After a moment she points at the hand scanner embedded in the desk.
She looks surprised, but then recovers and sings a verse about how hands can learn, but must be cautious, and gestures at the hand scanner embedded in the desk.

As you place your hand on the scanner, you feel a quick tingle as it scans your hand, then a pinprick as it extracts a drop of blood. The lady behind the desk looks at her screen. She nods, taps on the screen a few times, then retrieves a data pad from beneath the desk.
She hands the pad to you, and sings a brief verse about perseverance and hope.

Back on your ship you flip the pad on. The data pad appears to be loaded with a number of historic musicals and operas where the meaning of the lyrics has been replicated with gestures as subtitles. It is interspersed with what appear to be Remnant children's videos slowly explaining gestures and pausing to give you the opportunity to practice.

You spend a few hours going through the lessons. It takes a while to start vaguely understanding the signs, but you eventually learn how to sign a number of basic phrases. Eventually, the pad goes black and a note pops up on the screen informing you that additional lessons are available from the director's desk on Aventine.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Midnight Popcorn: Remnant: Learn Sign 1

name: Midnight Popcorn: There Might Be Riots 1
description: Give the band "There Might Be Riots" a ride to <destination>.

values: Give the band "There Might Be Riots" a ride to <destination>.

children.key: A woman in a well-tailored suit approaches you. "Captain <last>?" You nod. "Are you available for a transport job?" she asks.

"My name is Becca," she says. "I'm a stage manager for a band, and the transport we had under contract bailed out on us. Any chance you could take <fare> and <tons> of cargo to <destination>? Given the circumstances, we can pay quite well."
"Sorry, I'm not headed in that direction right now."

"Great," she says, "I'll tell the boys to start loading their gear into your ship." About a half an hour later the road crew begins carting instruments and amplifiers into your cargo hold. Soon after that, you hear the roar of a crowd in the distance and another group of men comes running into your ship. "We're with the band," they say. "Quick, shut the hatch." Half a minute later, a mob of people has surrounded your ship and a few of them are even climbing on top of it. It takes you a second to realize they're not angry or bent on destruction - they're just a group of crazy fans.

"Happens everywhere we go," says one of the musicians, calmly, as he watches a video feed of the mob on one of your monitors. He tells you that he's Ulrich, the lead singer. Then he introduces the rest of the singers and musicians.
"Pleased to meet you all. What's the name of your band?"
"Oh," Ulrich says, "we call ourselves, 'There Might Be Riots.'"
Eventually, the spaceport police arrive and disperse the crowd, and the band settles in for their trip to <destination>.

values: You arrive on <planet>, but realize that your escort carrying the band and their supplies has not arrived yet. Better depart and wait for your escorts to enter the system.
Dropped the famous band "There Might Be Riots" off on Wayfarer. They drew quite the crowd, and paid very well.

children.key: You drop off the band "There Might Be Riots" on <destination>. Along the way, you got to hear some of their music, which is mostly characterized by frenzied instrumentals, a very energetic brass section, and bizarre lyrics. One day while you were in transit, they nearly drove you insane by playing their catchy but nonsensical song "Henhouse In Your Soul" for four hours straight, but other than that they have been good passengers, and their stage manager gives you an incredibly generous payment of <payment>.

"We've already got a gig lined up for tonight," says Ulrich. "Want to come? We'll give you free tickets." Given how well they just paid you, it might be worth going just to build a relationship with the band, even if not for the music itself.
"Sorry, I've got other things to do."

The band is even louder in concert than they were when practicing in the confines of your ship. About thirty minutes into the concert, the energy of the crowd and the surreal lyrics finally begin to soak in, and rather than seeming meaningless their music feels fraught with meaning that hovers just beyond your grasp.

Finally the band announces that their last song will be "Sad Archie." You've never heard of it, but the fans scream in approval. It's a slow, ballad-like song about a man named Archie who lives forever and is sad because the friends he makes all grow old and die. Archie has a pet dragon, and he builds a beautiful house for the dragon, but the dragon dies young. Archie is so sad seeing the dragon's house empty and gathering dust that he rents it out to some friends, but they fight with each other and trash the place. The story makes no sense, but some of the fans are wiping away tears as the song ends.

Becca, who is sitting next to you in the VIP section, says, "We learned years ago that we need to end every concert with a sad song. Otherwise the fans leave with way too much energy and start destroying public property."
The concert ends, and you say goodbye to the band. They say they'll be in touch if they ever need a ride again.

"<first>!" says Ulrich, when they see you. "What luck! We're doing a concert tonight on landing pad ninety-four, part of our 'Trouble on the Tarmac Tour.' We're going to need a lift to <planet> right after the concert. Or possibly in the middle of it. Can you help us out?"
"Okay. But why the hurry to leave?"
"Please," he says, "I'm serious. You'll be saving our skins. Whatever else you've got, it's not this important."
"Okay, I'll do it. Why's it so urgent?"
"Sorry, I really don't want to work with you guys anymore."
"You'll see," he says. "You should park your ship right behind us in case the natives get restless and we need to skedaddle."

With some trepidation, you sit by the hatchway of your ship and watch as the band sets up directly outside it and the concert begins. Nothing seems out of the ordinary until the band introduces a song called "Gluttony," and you can feel a sudden tension fill the air. The Syndicate security guards, who until now have been standing at the periphery of the landing pad, begin to disperse themselves throughout the crowd.

It's a song about a man who will die if he ever stops eating, so he eats more and more and grows bigger and bigger. A second after you realize that the whole thing is a thinly veiled critique of the Syndicate, a group up front unrolls a banner that reads "End Wage Slavery!" and begins shouting and chanting slogans. As the band plays on, there is some sort of scuffle at the back of the crowd, and then you see stun guns begin to flash, and rising plumes of what you would guess is tear gas.
As the demonstrators are driven away, a group of guards approach you. "What is your connection to these musicians?" they ask.
"I'm just their transport. They're paying me to carry them to their next destination."
"They're friends of mine. Why? They haven't done anything illegal, that I can see."

"Be careful what friends you choose," says the guard, "or you might find that no one in this sector will offer you any jobs. Now, get them packed up and get out of here." You have no choice but to leave the planet immediately...
"Then I suggest you do your job and transport them. Immediately." The guards leave. As soon as the band is packed up, you leave the planet...

children.key: A disabled Shuttle is sending a request for help. The transmissions suddenly stop...
(The default key for boarding disabled ships is "B".)

You open the hatch and find an old man in grease stained overalls on the other side. "Thank goodness! A pirate attacked the shuttle and plundered most of the outfits. I've been trying to keep the ship from falling apart but I don't think it can be saved. My name is James. If you could give me a lift to <destination>, I'd really appreciate it."
"That's kind of a rude question," he says, "but I'll pay you ten thousand credits. I'm not really in a position to negotiate at the moment..."
"Great," he says. "My name is James, by the way."
"I'm looking forward to traveling with you, Captain <last>," says James.
"<first> <last>?" he stops for a moment. "I've heard that name before. Reminds me of someone famous, I think," says James. "Anyways, I'm looking forward to traveling with you."

As you're helping him wheel his luggage aboard and showing him his bunk, he says, "Before we leave, you may as well salvage whatever cargo the pirates left behind. I don't mind if you sell it on <planet>."
After a few days, you've finally arrived at another inhabited system. Your real journey starts here...

James makes some observations of the <ship>. "Is this a Tarazed Modified Hawk? A lot of the parts aren't original, but it's rare to find one that doesn't require a co-pilot. Most Modified Hawks are counterfeits."
"Well, I don't plan to get too attached to this one. I'll be flying something much nicer before long."

He smiles. "I'm sure you will. But there's something nice to having a ship you can pilot all by yourself. Believe me, once you have to start managing crew and paying salaries, or keeping track of a whole fleet, you'll miss these days when everything was simple."
"Had," he says. "Sold off my fleet a few days ago, and I already miss it. That Shuttle was my last ship. But it was time. Time for me to retire." His voice trails off.

Your landing on <planet> is a bit rough, but you manage to make it safely. James says, "Was this your first trip through hyperspace? Congrats! I'm impressed that you didn't throw up; most folks do, the first time."

"Yeah, and then spent half an hour in orbit cleaning my cabin while hoping the passengers wouldn't come out of their bunk room and see the mess. Not my proudest moment. Anyway, here's your pay." He hands you <payment>.

Then his face lights up. "Say, any chance I could hitch a ride with you, maybe show you the ropes, give you some pointers? I could pay you, of course. If you're okay with giving me a lift for a while longer, sell off any cargo you salvaged and then meet me in the spaceport. I'll see if I can rustle up any interesting work for you to do."
(Click the "Spaceport" button to continue this mission.)

Armen continues. "Which is where you come in. Recently, we've come into contact with someone claiming to have information on pirate activity in the Core. If they're telling the truth, their knowledge could open the way for preemptive strikes against the pirates, freeing ships to be deployed elsewhere. However, the informant's existence has leaked, and a hired ship named the Spear of Heimdall is trying to cover up this loose end. "It'll outspeed anything short of a fighter."
"Not fast enough. You'll have to find someone else for the job."
"Good," he says. "I'll have the informant on your ship by sundown."

After <person> leaves, James says to you, "Now, get one thing clear. This is not your David and Goliath moment. The <enemy>'s shields are <magnitude> times as strong as yours, and if it's able to bring its weapons to bear, we'll be dead in two seconds. So, the moment we're in the sky, we head straight for hyperspace. Don't even wait around to see if the <enemy> is coming or not. Got it?"

"It just isn't feasible," he says. "If a ship has turrets, your <model> can't get close enough to hit it with your guns without being damaged, and then it's just a matter of whose weapons and shields are stronger. If it has anti-missile turrets, you can't count on hanging back and bombarding it with missiles from long distances, or at least not with weapons that can fit in a <model>. So, don't risk it.
"It's like rock paper scissors; recognize what your enemy's strengths and weaknesses are, as well as your own."

James looks disppointed. He whispers to you, "Alright, but a final word of free advice: Get a real Pilot's License as soon as you can. Don't think I didn't notice that fake one. If the Republic catches you with it too often the fees will eat you alive..." With that, he lets you go.

"Are there any good trade routes you can give me?"
"I'm ready to go out on my own."

"Stay near Sol and around the Paradise Worlds. The Navy stays there the most, so even if a pirate does show up, they won't last long. The Deep is also a pretty safe place, as they have their own security forces. Once you start moving farther south, things get riskier. The worlds down there don't bring in as much tax revenue as the Paradise Worlds do, so the Navy tends to ignore them. You'll find some local militia to back you up, but they're nothing compared to one of the Navy's Cruisers.

"If you do end up in pirate space, then sometimes the best defense is no defense at all. Pirates will prioritize fighting armed threats over unarmed transports, so if you don't install any weapons, you might be able to sneak away."

"I've spoken with the Quarg a few times, but what captain hasn't? You'll find them down south by Tarazed. I haven't met any other aliens," he pauses for a moment, "as far as I'm aware, that is, but I'm sure they're out there if you go looking hard enough. I've explored all of Republic space in my many years, but there are far more systems out there that we don't even know how to reach."

"One of the most reliable trade routes is to bring food from the Dirt Belt to Earth or the other urban worlds around it. There are billions of mouths to feed on those worlds, and the Dirt Belt sells food for cheap, so it's a great place to get started. Just remember though that if you use the same trade route for too long, you might end up causing the prices to stabilize. The Dirt Belt can only produce food and people can only eat it so fast, so change up your trade routes if you notice the return getting worse."

"Getting good jobs is more about having the space to accept the good jobs than it is finding them, but if you're looking for jobs that pay well for little effort, then you'll want to watch out around the holidays. There's always a big celebration on Earth every April 22nd, Earth Day, so pay attention to the job board in the months leading up to that. The people down in the Rim have some month-long celebration every August that you should look out for too."

He takes on a serious tone, "A final word of free advice: Get a real Pilot's License as soon as you can. Don't think I didn't notice that fake one. If the Republic catches you with it too often the fees will eat you alive..."

James hands you a credit chip worth <payment>, and says, "Best of luck to you, Captain. Don't hesitate to look me up if you're ever in the area. And remember to check the spaceports wherever you land. You never know who you'll find wandering around there."

children.key: You end up finding James in the spaceport bar, talking to a man in a Navy uniform. "Nice to see you, <first>," he says. "I've been talking to Lieutenant Armen over here, and I think we have a job on our hands."
"You haven't drafted me into the Navy, have you?"
"Actually, I want to go out on my own now."
Armen grins. "You would have a lot more to do if you were joining the Navy."
James says, "The Navy protects merchants from pirates, keeping the Paradise Worlds safe. However, they also deal with the transport of confidential documents and equipment."

Armen continues. "Which is where you come in. "Recently, one of our logistics ships was attacked and damaged by a merchant warship named the Eye of Odin. We now believe that ship to be a pirate vessel in disguise, specifically targeting the cargo onboard. We're looking for a replacement ship capable of avoiding the threat while we track down the warlord. How fast would you say the <ship> is?"
"It'll outspeed anything short of a fighter."
"Not fast enough. You'll have to find someone else for the job."
"Good," he says. "I'll have the cargo loaded onto your ship by sundown."

After <person> leaves, James says to you, "Now, get one thing clear. This is not your David and Goliath moment. The <enemy>'s shields are <magnitude> times as strong as yours, and if it's able to bring its weapons to bear, we'll be dead in two seconds. So, the moment we're in the sky, we head straight for hyperspace. Don't even wait around to see if the <enemy> is coming or not. Got it?"

"It just isn't feasible," he says. "In case you forgot, the <model> has no gunports or turret mounts for installing weapons. So, don't risk it. It's like rock paper scissors; recognize what your enemy's strengths and weaknesses are, as well as your own."

When you meet up with James in the spaceport, he says, "Hi there, <first>! I found you another mission, but it looks like you'll need <capacity> in order to take it on. So, you'll either have to cancel another mission, or come back here later to continue this one. Sorry!"

children.key: The spaceport on <origin> is small enough that it doesn't take long to find James. He's talking with a man wearing what looks like a doctor's lab coat. "Captain <last>!" says James. "Glad you could join us. It turns out there's been a flu outbreak on <planet>, and they're asking every captain with space to spare to carry some vaccines and other medical supplies that are urgently needed over there. That means it needs to be there no later than <day>. If we take a direct route, there should be no trouble making the delivery on time. What do you say?"
"Sorry, I think I'm going to head in the other direction."
"Great!" says James. "They'll be loading up your ship shortly."

You drop off the shipment of <commodity> on <planet>, and collect your payment of <payment>. "Hauling freight," says James. "Not the most glamorous job, or the most interesting, but you're always guaranteed steady income. And once you know the galaxy a bit better, instead of taking missions you can find your own trade routes to follow. The only trouble is, build up a fleet with lots of cargo space and not enough defenses and the pirates begin to take notice."
"Did you have a lot of trouble with pirates when you were a captain?"
"But what if I want to earn money more quickly than I can by trading?"

"Some. That's why you can't just go traipsing around the galaxy in a fleet of unarmed star barges; every pirate within a week's travel will hear you're coming through and come after you. In the long term, having a few heavy freighters with good defenses is more cost-effective than losing a star barge or two to the pirates on every journey."

"If you can line them up right," says James, "rush deliveries can be your best source of income as a freighter captain. And keep your eye out for missions with large amounts of cargo, too, because your <model>'s hold is definitely big enough to handle them. And if you've got any cargo space to spare and you know what the prices are going to be at your destination, be sure to stock up on something you can sell for a profit."
"What would you recommend if I want to do more than just carry cargo?"
"Did you do that for your whole career?"

He pauses for a moment to think, then says, "Unless you want to do something really risky like hunting pirates, your best bet is to work with the Navy, or the Syndicate, or one of the local militias. Any of those would be a decent choice, although they've each got their own problems. If any of them offer you a mission, go ahead and take it; that's a good way to build connections and get to know the lay of the land."

"Well," he says, "Back when I was a bit older than you, I piloted a Firebird for a while, escorting merchant convoys up and down the Rim. I used to hope we'd get attacked; I'd disable the pirate ships and rob them blind. Turnabout is fair play, after all.

"Then one day I got a bit too greedy and thought I'd try to capture a pirate ship or two, to add more firepower to my fleet. We boarded their ship, and I sent my crew through the airlock to kill off the pirates. And it turns out the pirates had grenades. Four of my men were dead before I even realized what was happening. We had to retreat, and then limp back to port without even enough crew left uninjured to pilot the ship right. After that I decided to stick to less risky jobs."
He glances toward the spaceport and says, "Anyway, if you want to make one more trip with me, you know where to find me."

children.key: You find James standing on a landing pad underneath a large freighter, chatting with a man you assume is the captain. "There you are!" he says. "Captain Eldred here says his two ships have been having trouble with pirates ever since they left the Rim ten days ago, and he's looking for an escort to get them safely to Gemstone. Are you interested?"
"No, sounds a bit too risky for me."

"Great," he says. "Whenever we're ready to leave the planet, they'll take off behind us and follow us to <planet>." As you begin walking away together, he adds in a quieter voice, "Normally a fresh pilot like you with no combat reputation would never be offered a mission like this, so try not to mess things up. Remember that we don't have to kill the pirates, all we have to do is make sure the convoy isn't destroyed. But freighters are slow, so you can't just go skipping through hyperspace as fast as you want; you need to stick around and make sure they're behind you."

The captain of the <npc> hands you <payment> and thanks you for your escort services. From the expression on <their> face, you'd guess that <they're> feeling lucky to still be alive after entrusting the safety of <their> fleet to a rookie pilot like yourself.

After <they are> gone, James turns to you and says, "Not too bad for your first escort mission. I recognize that look on your face - it's the same one I had after my first job like this back when I was a beginner. If I recall, my first priority after touching down was replacing some of the ship's guns with missile launchers so I'd actually have a chance against pirates. It's a scandal how they sell interceptors with nothing but short-ranged energy weapons these days; trying to use them in combat on such a small ship is practically suicide. Keep your distance with some missiles and you can almost never go wrong.
"Anyway, I'll stop rambling. If you've still got a hankering for some dangerous missions, come and find me in the spaceport before you leave." He picks up his suitcase and heads outside.
(As before, click the "Spaceport" button to continue this mission. The next mission will involve carrying cargo, so it will only show up if you have 10 tons of space free.)

"Sorry <first>," he says, "I haven't found any good opportunities." The sheer number of people here is almost overwhelming. Homeless men wrapped in old army blankets beg money from well-dressed businessmen. Soldiers in Navy uniforms walk by in groups of ten or twenty, all marching in unison. Starship captains haggle with merchants over trade goods and jobs. Flashes of light come from various landing bays as welders make repairs.

Before you can respond, a man in nondescript clothing appears out of nowhere and offers <payment> for discreet, no-questions-asked passage to <destination>. Though he says very little, you get the distinct sense that his presence on this planet and motivation to be elsewhere may not be entirely legal.
James casts you an uncertain look. "It's your choice if you want to take on this job."
"If you're willing to pay, I'm willing to fly."
"Get lost. I'm not letting you on my ship."

The stranger growls, pulls out a gun and fires a shot. Fortunately, he has terrible aim. A woman nearby screams and a squad of Navy soldiers converges on your position. They subdue him before he can harm anyone and momentarily detain you for witness testimony. Somehow, you've lost sight of James in all the confusion. It appears you'll be on your own from here on out.

After your new client heads off to the landing pads, James pulls you aside. "Since you're going through with this, head straight to <planet> and don't linger anywhere long enough to let the Navy scan the <ship>. I'm not certain your new passenger is on any wanted lists, but if he is you don't want to be on the hook for any legal penalties."

Unfortunately, planetary security recognized your passenger is a wanted fugitive. After the criminal is hauled away, James breaths a sigh of relief. "I'm glad that's over with," he says. "Different planets have varying levels of security and this determines your odds of being scanned. Installing scan interference or scan concealment outfits can help improve your chances of smuggling someone or something in." He shakes his head. "Shady jobs like this can be rewarding, but as you've seen the legal penalties for being caught outweigh the rewards and you should always be on the lookout for backstabbers who would be willing to double cross you."

description: You've been accused of stealing the Conundrum and its Jump Drive! Flee to <destination> until things calm down.

children.key: You land the Conundrum and a crew of dockworkers begin refueling it. James raids the nearest vending machine and returns with an armload of snacks. "Whew, It's good to be back!" James hands you a bag of chips when an alert notifies you of a hail.

The manager greets you. "Welcome back <last>. A Syndicate Security team has been dispatched to arrest you and James for stealing the Conundrum and its valuable prototype. The Syndicate guarantees a swift trial. Do not attempt to resist."
James skoffs. "Your trial may be swift, but it won't necessarily be fair. <first>, we need to get out of here!"
How could it come to this? Will the trial be fair or are you being setup? The dock workers have disengaged the fuel pumps and a Syndicate Security team is walking over to your landing pad...
"<first>! They're coming! We need to go! NOW!" At this point, James is shouting...

Syndicate security takes you and James into custody. The trial is indeed swift. You are both sentenced to fifty years in prison with no possibility of parole. Your life as a pilot is over. For an old man like James, it's a death sentence.

values: After making it back, we were accused of stealing the Conundrum and its Jump Drive. I'll have to avoid the Syndicate while I'm high on their priority list for wanted fugitives.

children.key: James says, "You should head west, into the Dirt Belt. <destination> should be a good backwater planet to lay low on until things calm down.

values: After arriving at New Boston, James and I parted ways. He'll be posing as a retired starship captain. I should probably come up with my own cover story. This planet seems as good as any to call home...
An old man who accompanied you on your first job as a starship captain.

children.key: After landing, James says "Thanks for getting us out of there. This is a good time for us to part ways. I'll be able to take care of myself. How about you? Is there anything you'd like to ask me about being an independent pilot?"
"How long will I have to avoid the Syndicate?"
"Where should I go if I want to avoid pirates?"
"Are there any good trade routes you can give me?"

"Stay near Sol and around the Paradise Worlds. The Navy stays there the most, so even if a pirate does show up, they won't last long. The Deep is also a pretty safe place, as they have their own security forces. Once you start moving farther south, things get riskier. The worlds down there don't bring in as much tax revenue as the Paradise Worlds do, so the Navy tends to ignore them. You'll find some local militia to back you up, but they're nothing compared to one of the Navy's Cruisers.

"I've spoken with the Quarg a few times, but what captain hasn't? You'll find them down south by Tarazed. I haven't met any other aliens," he pauses for a moment, "as far as I'm aware, that is, but I'm sure they're out there if you go looking hard enough. I've explored all of Republic space in my many years, but there are far more systems out there that we don't even know how to reach.

"One of the most reliable trade routes is to bring food from the Dirt Belt to Earth or the other urban worlds around it. There are billions of mouths to feed on those worlds, and the Dirt Belt sells food for cheap, so it's a great place to get started. Just remember though that if you use the same trade route for too long, you might end up causing the prices to stabilize. The Dirt Belt can only produce food and people can only eat it so fast, so change up your trade routes if you notice the return getting worse.

"Getting good jobs is more about having the space to accept the good jobs than it is finding them, but if you're looking for jobs that pay well for little effort, then you'll want to watch out around the holidays. There's always a big celebration on Earth every April 22nd, Earth Day, so pay attention to the job board in the months leading up to that. The people down in the Rim have some month-long celebration every August that you should look out for too.
"Anything else you want to ask me?"

"Unless you do something to improve your reputation with them, they'll consider you a person of interest. Avoid getting into fights with their fleets. That will just make things worse. Helping merchants in distress and fighting pirates might put you back on their good side."

"Best of luck to you, Captain." He hands you a credit chip worth <payment>, and says, "Here's a little something to help now that you're on your own. Remember to check the spaceports wherever you land. You never know who you'll find wandering around there."
He turns back to you and smiles. "As of today, I'm just a retired star ship captain." He gives one last wave and disembarks.

Before leaving, I retrieved my trusty sidearm from storage: the Guncraft, an heirloom that's been passed down my family for generations and carefully kept in perfect working order. name: Guncraft VIII
description: The captain of the <npc> murdered Ceska and stole your Guncraft. Find that ship somewhere in Syndicate space and take back what's yours! Return to <destination> afterwards.

values: The captain of the <npc> murdered Ceska and stole your Guncraft. Find that ship somewhere in Syndicate space and take back what's yours! Return to <destination> afterwards.

children.key: As you enter a gun shop the shop keeper squeals, "Oh my gosh, Captain <first> <last> is in my shop! Word's gotten around that you not only have a fully functional Guncraft, but you've been letting gunsmiths make mods for it." She seems genuinely delighted to see you, or at least see your Guncraft. She stares at the weapon longingly...
"Did you want to try making a modification to it?"
"Before you ask, no. You can't touch it."

She pouts. "I'll do it for free! Please let me have a stab at it!" She seems genuinely interested in making a mod for the Guncraft. But gives you the impression that she might not be as experienced as the previous gunsmiths you've worked with...
"Alright, you can make a mod for it."
"Too bad..." She sulks at the counter and you leave to look for a different store.

"Wait, for realz?" She's astonished. "I should warn you, I have some radical ideas in mind that be like totally illegal. Like, yeah this is a pirate world, but not just kinda illegal but like really really illegal. For realz would totes blow your mind illegal. You know?" Words seemed to have finally stopped flowing from her mouth and she is waiting for a response.

"I'm saying that the mod I have in mind would totally make your Guncraft an illegal item. Like, you could get fined and stuff if the authorities catch you with it. Are you okay with that?" That's a little more clear than what she said earlier.
"I'm okay with that. Do your best to bring out its potential."
"I changed my mind. I don't want to make my Guncraft illegal. That's final."

She nods, a bit more somber this time. Adjustments to your Guncraft have probably gotten as far as they can possibly go without crossing the line into making it a weapon to draw the ire of law enforcement. You finish the business you originally came here for and leave.
"Alright!" She whoops and hollars while jumping up and down. She holds out her hands and you carefully hand over the Guncraft...
Before handing it over, you ask for her name.
"Ceska," she replies. "Named after my mother's fave gun, the CZ75. If you thought the Guncraft was rare... Anyway, I should totes have this ready for you by tomorrow afternoon."

Impatient to wait for the afternoon, you return the following morning to find the door to Ceska's shop slightly ajar. Looking inside, you see her lying in a pool of her own blood, a gunshot wound to the chest area being the source.

"Oh... <first>... Sorry, I... I had planned to sell your Guncraft to the captain of... of the Silent Assassin... But he betrayed..." Her breathing is shallow. You notice the flesh around the gunshot wound necrotizing rapidly. "My mod at work... Atomic Bullets... If the wound doesn't get you... the radioactive poisoning will..." Tears well up in her eyes. "For realz..." She dies right there, sobbing quietly until she takes her final breath. Whether you feel sorry for her or angry at her, one thing is certain: You need to get your gun back.
After snooping around <planet>'s spaceport, you get a lead: the <npc> usually operates in Syndicate space. It's not much, but it's a start.

values: A gunsmith named after her mother's favorite gun. She was killed by the captain of the Silent Assassin after she modified the Guncraft VIII to fire Atomic Bullets.
Recovered the Guncraft VIII from the Silent Assassin. With Ceska's modifications, it has become a terrifying weapon. One that is unlikely to go unnoticed by governments across the galaxy.

children.key: After a fierce battle, you take possession of the Guncraft VIII. With Ceska's modifications, it has become a terrifying weapon. One that is unlikely to go unnoticed by governments across the galaxy. Its power is yours to wield, if you dare.

You visit Ceska's shop and find a man behind the counter. "Oh! The Guncraft wielder! I heard you were here the day my assistant was killed. Thanks for not robbing me blind while I was away. That was some messy business though. You can't be too careful about who you deal with in this line of work."
He offers you some free ammo for your trouble...

name: Coalition Dissension: Heliarch Intrigues 1
description: Scan the <npc> at one of the Heliarch ringworlds and share the data collected with Chikee on <destination>.

values: Scan the <npc> at one of the Heliarch ringworlds and share the data collected with Chikee on <destination>.

children.key: You run into Chikee, the student who you helped on his path to joining the Heliarchs. He seems tired. "On the council I am not. Yet put forth a proposal for production of a new Kimek freighter, the Bramble. Able to convince someone on the council, I did. But opposition to the proposal, there is. Led by Temlamrem, a Saryd. Frustrating, the inner machinations of the Heliarchs. Not expected I did!"
Such is politics. You wish Chikee luck and return to your ship, where you find a data chip wedged into the entry hatch.

You carefully remove the chip and bring it aboard. It contains an audio message of an Arach speaking into a translation device. "On the <npc> does Temlamrem ride between the Heliarch rings. Scan his ship's outfits you should and with your friend share the data." The message ends there. Could Chikee have an ally behind the scenes? Or could this be some other kind of plot? What will you do?
You yank out the data chip, but it breaks in half! You won't be able to view the data that was contained on it...

values: Your scans revealed evidence of Temlamrem's involvement in corrupt Heliarch activities! Share the data with Chikee on <destination>.
[MISSION FAILED] Destroying the <npc> wasn't part of the plan! If life were a game, you could load a save file and try again.

children.key: You contact Chikee and share the scanner data with him. "Shocked I am at this evidence. Present this to the council I must. Finished, Temlamrem's position on the council is." Chikee accepts the scanner data and excuses himself.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Coalition Dissension: Heliarch Intrigues 1

name: Coalition Dissension: Heliarch Intrigues 2
description: Visit Chikee on <destination>.

children.key: The shipyard has a new ship on display: the Kimek Bramble. It isn't ready to be sold yet, but the shipyard is taking preorders.
When you get back to your ship, there's a data chip wedged into the entry hatch...

You carefully remove the chip and bring it aboard. It contains a video of a party where a drunk Chikee is doing... You're not sure what you're watching. Supposedly, whoever left it with you wants you to share this with Chikee.
You yank out the data chip, but it breaks in half! You won't be able to view the data that was contained on it...

You contact Chikee and share the video with him. "Embarrassed I am at this video. From when I was still a student this was. Not serious, this is. But a message someone is sending me." Chikee thanks you for telling him about the video and asks you to destroy any copies you have. He pays you <payment> as a token of good faith.

name: Coalition Dissension: Restricted Spaceport (Arach)

children.key: Access to the spaceport is blocked off by several crowd control barriers. An Arach wearing a Heliarch arm band is shooing away anyone who approaches the barrier.

The Arach looks at you with his eight eyes and gestures with his staff for you to keep your distance. "Beyond this point, civil unrest, there is. A group of suspected dissidents in the space port, there are. Barred from entry, all must be.
"Is there anything I can do to help?"

The Arach hesitates as the translation device communicates your question. Finally he answers, "Handle this, the Heliarch will. Remain out of harm's way, of you we ask." It seems there's no way for you to access the spaceport today.

name: Coalition Dissension: Spaceport Bomber (Arach)

children.key: As you walk into the spaceport, an Arach nearly knocks you down. He seems to be in a rush to leave.

The Arach turns to look at you and gurgles something in his strange guttural language. You notice that he has no translation device. Before you have a chance to respond he is rushing off, as fast he can, away from the spaceport.

While walking towards the shops, you find a plaza that offers a scenic view of the landing pads. You can see your own ship along with the others. Several Heliarch agents are swarming over one of the ships, an Arach Courier. They seem to be searching for something and are pointing some sort of sensor equipment at the ship.

Suddenly, the Arach Courier explodes! The Heliarch agents surrounding the ship are caught in the blast. Alarm sirens start blaring and the spaceport exits are quickly sealed off by Riot Containment Barriers.
As you rush to your ship, an Arach wearing a Heliarch armband orders you to stop.
(Wield the terrifying power of Midnight's Lost Orphan.)

You hasten your pace into a full run. The Arach takes aim and shoots you in the back! Your body spins from the impact and you find yourself sprawled on the ground. For some reason, you can't move your body and a cold chill settles over you. Soon, your vision fades to darkness and you leave this mortal realm...

You draw the Quantum Keyblade. Seeing this, the Arach takes aim and shoots! You activate Quantum Shifting and the energy blast passes through you harmlessly. Before she can fire again, you deactivated Quantum Shifting and...

You sever the appendages she used to hold her weapon. She falls to the ground, screaming! You can see more Heliarch agents approaching and flee to the <ship>. If they didn't suspect you before, they will now. Firing up the engines, you head into orbit.

You cause the appendages she held her weapon with to explode, splattering the area around her with blood. She falls to the ground, screaming! You can see more Heliarch agents approaching and flee to the <ship>. If they didn't suspect you before, they will now. Firing up the engines, you head into orbit.

The Arach approaches you and gestures back towards the direction of the plaza. "To the plaza you must go. Many questions we have for you. Resist you must not." She is holding one of their weapons, no mere Laser Rifle. A shot from this would probably put a very large hole in you.

Arriving at the plaza you notice that several Arachi, along with a few Kimek and Saryd, have been gathered there. You are ushered into the crowd and the Heliarch spread out around the edges, their weapons ready.
Soon several Arachs, along with a few Kimek and Saryd, gather at your location. The Heliarch herd you all into a cluster while they spread out around the edges, their weapons held ready.
One of the agents addresses the crowd. "Knowledge of this bombing does anyone here have? Of someone acting suspiciously does anyone wish to report?"
(Tell them about the Arach who rushed away from the spaceport.)

An Arach suddenly burbles something in its native language. Soon the Kimek begin to chitter and the Saryd whinny. Several gesture towards you. The Heliarch approach with their weapons readied. "Accused of this attack you are. Claim it is true many witnesses agree. Died in the explosion several Heliarch did. Death is the sentence that is judged."
(Wield the terrifying power of Midnight's Lost Orphan.)
The Heliarch fire their weapons, vaporizing you. All that remains is a pink mist dissipating into the wind...
You activate Quantum Shifting before the first volley hits. As their weapons charge up to fire again, you deactivate Quantum Shifting and...
You scramble to flee to the <ship>, but the Heliarch shoot you in the back, vaporizing you. All that remains is a pink mist dissipating into the wind...

You stab your blade deep into the abdomen of the closest Heliarch, an Arach. As the others take aim, you reactivate Quantum Shifting. Methodically, you repeat the process. After several of their agents lie dead on the ground, more arrive. They seem to be staggering their shots, to the point that you can no longer find a breather to safely deactivate Quantum Shifting. Finally, one of their weapon blasts slams into your back! Your body spins from the impact and you find yourself sprawled on the ground. For some reason, you can't move your body and a cold chill settles over you. Soon, your vision fades to darkness and you leave this mortal realm...

With a gesture, the energy blasts from their weapons reverse course and decapitate all of the Heliarch present! The crowd witnessing this flee in terror. You are free to return to the <ship>, but the Heliarch and the Coalition are now your enemy.

You step forward and tell the Heliarch about the Arach who almost knocked you down in his rush away from the spaceport. After recording your statement, they ask the crowd if anyone has more information on this Arach. After gathering a few more statements and confirming your identity, you and the others are released.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Coalition Dissension: Spaceport Bomber (Arach)

name: Coalition Dissension: Spaceport Bomber (Kimek)

children.key: You are about to enter a restaurant when a Kimek carrying a large briefcase bumps into you. He chitters at you angrily in the native language of his species before skittering off in a rush.

After entering the restaurant and ordering a meal, you try to enjoy your food despite the eating habits of the Kimek around you. The sounds of Kimek digesting their food are interrupted by the low roar and vibrations of a nearby explosion.

The building next door is on fire! Alarm sirens start blaring and the spaceport exits are quickly sealed off by Riot Containment Barriers. The Heliarch are directing fire suppression teams to put out the blaze while rescue workers retrieve the burnt remains of those who were caught in the blast. It seems this was a Heliarch facility and most of the victims are their agents. Once the fire is out, the Heliarch begin taking witness statements from everyone.
(Tell them about the Kimek carrying a briefcase.)
You tell the Heliarch agent about your experience in the restaurant, but she isn't interested in your opinion on Kimek dining habits.

You tell the Heliarch agent about the Kimek who bumped into you earlier while carrying a large briefcase. "Go in what direction he did?" As you think about it, you realize it was the same direction as the building that exploded.
After recording your statement and confirming your identity, the Heliarch grants you permission to leave the area sealed off by the Riot Containment Barriers.

description: Help an old Saryd visit <stopovers> before going to <destination> for retirement.

values: Help an old Saryd visit <stopovers> before going to <destination> for retirement.

children.key: You find an elderly Saryd waiting at the <ship>'s landing pad. "Transportation to <stopovers> I require. A final journey before retiring on <destination> I must undertake."
"Sedorum. For your assistance you I thank."

values: Sedorum thanks you for helping him reach <stopovers>. A small package is waiting for him at the spaceport. After bringing it aboard, he is ready for the final leg of his trip.

children.key: "Finally arrived we have!" While looking at the planet below, Sedorum asks, "<first>, seen our great Coalition you have. Of the society we built what think you?"
Sedorum guffaws. "Much to learn about us, you still have!" After calming down he quietly mutters, "What opinion you will have once learn more you do?"
Sedorum smiles. "Keeping the peace, the Heliarch always are. But to achieve that, a cost we must pay..."
Sedorum frowns. "Order we have, under the Heliarch's watch. But to maintain that, a price we pay..."

values: An old Saryd who retired on Shifting Sand in the Good Omen system on the edge of Saryd space.

children.key: After arriving, Sedorum hands you a pair of scrolls from the package he received on <stopovers>. "Retired I am. A use for these I no longer have. Please take as payment for you I thank." Studying them after Sedorum departs, you see they are maps of locations on Vibrant Water in the Lone Cloud system and Shadowed Valley in the Fallen Leaf system. Notes are written on them, but you are unable to discern what they mean.

name: Culminator Cache [Vibrant Water] 2
description: Flee to <destination> without killing any Coalition or Heliarch ships.

values: Flee to <destination> without killing any Coalition or Heliarch ships.

children.key: <origin> is one of the locations on the maps given to you by Sedorum. Do you want to explore the island depicted on it?

You fly out to the island and park on a wide stretch of beach. A thick jungle spreads out before you. After a few hours of hiking through the exotic foliage, you find the place where the map is marked with some notes. Several large crates are hidden in the bushes.
(Haul the crates back to your ship.)

The lid is difficult to crack open. With some effort, you start to pry it open by pounding a wedge into the seam. Unfortunately, the noise attracts a pack of local predators that sneak up on you! Although each one is no larger than a common house cat, there are too many of them. They seem to sense where your arteries are and each bite results in a spray of blood that splatters the area. This only excites the ravaging predators into a frenzy and you are quickly devoured.

The lid is difficult to crack open. With some effort, you start to pry it open by wedging the Quantum Keyblade into the seam. Unfortunately, the noise attracts a pack of local predators that sneak up on you! Although each one is no larger than a common house cat, there are too many of them to fight. When the first one leaps for your throat, you instinctively activate Quantum Shifting. The creatures viciously try to attack but are quickly confused when their bites fail to find your succulent flesh. After a few moments they give up in frustration and scatter into the underbrush...
Deactivating Quantum Shifting, you gasp for breath. You are uncertain if the predators will return.
(Haul the crates back to your ship.)
It takes multiple trips, but you manage to haul back half of the crates. Inside, you find a pair of weapon pods and what appears to be their ammunition. The sun is starting to set...

The sky gradually darkens as you trudge back through the jungle. Something seems odd. The local wildlife has gotten quiet. As your eyes adjust to the gloomy twilight, something leaps out from the brush and you feel a sharp pain in your neck! The creature's vicious attack cut into an artery, sending a spray of blood gushing out into the cool evening air. Suddenly, the jungle springs to life as more of these predators swarm out from the underbrush. There is no time to react as you are quickly devoured by them in a bloodthirsty frenzy.
You settle in for the night...

The following morning you awaken to the sound of engines flying overhead. A Heliarch patrol is surveilling the island and hails you. "For what on this island you do seek? Find in the jungle something you have?".
"Property of the Coalition these weapons are. Surrender them you will. Resist you shall not."
You hand over the crates you retrieved. The Heliarch thank you for your cooperation and dispatch a search party to confiscate the rest. You return to the spaceport empty handed.

You fire up your engines and launch the <ship>! A Heliarch Judicator is in orbit and moves to intercept! Your only hope of getting out of this with your reputation somewhat intact is to flee Coalition space without getting into a fire fight. Perhaps you can lay low on <destination> until things here cool down.
You fire up your engines and launch the <ship>! A Heliarch Judicator is in orbit and moves to intercept!

You abandon the remaining crates and head back to the spaceport for the evening. The following morning, the Heliarch announce that a weapons cache was discovered on the island. They are searching for whoever was hiding the weapons there...
You've escaped Coalition space. Hopefully your reputation with the Heliarch is salvagable...
You've escaped Coalition space. Unfortunately your reputation with the Heliarch probably isn't salvagable...

name: Culminator Cache [Shadowed Valley] 2

children.key: <origin> is one of the locations on the maps given to you by Sedorum. Do you want to explore the caverns depicted on it?

The caverns are located in a remote mountain range some distance from the spaceport. You find a spot near the caverns just large enough to park the <ship>, but it leaves a portion of the hull hanging precariously off the edge of a cliff. The caverns, like many on this world, are filled with strange crystals that reflect and refract the light you brought with you, casting everything in sight with a strange multi-colored hue.
You find the location marked on the map with several notes. There doesn't appear to be anything here but a large pool of water.

The water chills you to the bone. As you swim out you start to have trouble making your arms and legs move the way you want them to. It's uncertain whether this is the result of the freezing temperature or poison in the water. Either way, you are unable to keep your head above the surface and drown.

You aren't sure if the water is safe. Returning to your ship, you don a space suit before returning to the pool. Wading out into the depths, you find several crates hidden below the surface. Hauling them back to your ship, you find that they contain ammunition, but the weapon that uses them is not included.

name: Midnight Market: Trailblazer Auction

children.key: While walking through the spaceport, you notice a large crowd forming at one of the other landing pads. A Saryd style ship you haven't seen at any Coalition shipyard is parked there. You are particularly surprised to see Heliarch officials give no attention to the guns mounted on it.
(Take a closer look at what's going on.)

While walking through the spaceport, you notice a large crowd forming at one of the other landing pads. An old Saryd warship is parked there. You are particularly surprised to see Heliarch officials give no attention to the guns mounted on it.
(Take a closer look at what's going on.)
"30 million!" recites another Saryd from behind a podium set up in front of the crowd. "Is a bid there for 31?"
"31 million!" repeats the Saryd at the podium. "Will a bid of 32 anyone make?"
From what you are seeing, it looks like the ship is being auctioned off...
"32 million!" calls out the Saryd at the podium. "Is 33 a bid any proposes?"
"32 million, a bid twice does stand."
"32 million, thrice a bid goes unchallenged."

"32 million for the third time does stand!" proclaims the auctioneer. The Saryds stamp their hooves and hoot while the Arachi make celebratory clicking sounds with their mandibles and the Kimek buzz their vestigial wings. You realize this must be the Coalition equivalent of clapping. The Saryd auctioneer congratulates the Kimek on his purchase while a Heliarch official formalizes the transfer of ownership.
"Th... th... thirty three million, the human does bid! Will a challenge from anyone come forth?" stammers the auctioneer.
"33 million, twice a bid goes unopposed!"
"33 million, thrice the bid does stand."
"Congratulations to the human! The Trailblazer, to you it does go!" the auctioneer gestures towards you.

After a moment of silence, the Saryds stamp their hooves and hoot while the Arachi make audible clicking sounds with their mandibles and the Kimek buzz their vestigial wings. You realize this must be the Coalition equivalent of clapping. The auctioneer and a Heliarch official make their way towards you and begin the formal ownership transfer process.
Do you have any questions you would like to ask?
"Can you tell me more about the Trailblazer?"
"Why do the Heliarch allow guns on this ship?"
(No more questions. Time to fly your new ship!)
"No. Is rare, an auction like this. From the Heliarchs, special permission is required. At the shipyard, most ships are exchanged."
"From the times of war against the Quarg, this ship is! A true warship! Famous it is! Few in number remain. Many wealthy seek to own for status. For prestige."
There is a momentary pause of confusion. Then both the Saryd and the Heliarch official begin to laugh.
"Sorry human! Not real, these guns are. Decorative models only. For display," the Saryd nervously apologizes.
Other than the earlier laughter, the Heliarch official has nothing to say regarding the model guns...
After signing off on the transfer forms, you look upon your new ship. You make a mental note to take it to an outfitter as soon as possible to get a closer look at those guns...

values: I saw a Saryd Trailblazer sold at a Coalition auction. I was amazed that the Heliarch allowed the ship to be sold with its guns installed. There is still much for me to learn about the Coalition's legal system regarding civilian weapon ownership.

Won a Saryd Trailblazer at auction. This is supposedly a rare antique from the time of the Coalition's rebellion against the Quarg. Since the Coalition does not allow citizens to arm their ships, the previous owner outfitted it with model guns to give it an authentic appearance.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Midnight Market: Trailblazer Auction

name: Midnight Market: Trailblazer 1

values: The Saryd Trailblazer that was up for auction was stolen by someone piloting a Kestrel. I have to give the thief credit. Stealing a warship from under the Heliarch's nose is no small feat. Whoever the thief is must be either daring or crazy.

children.key: When you land you are surprised to find a group of Heliarch officials waiting for you. They question you about the time you witnessed a rare Trailblazer ship being auctioned off. Apparently, the ship was recently stolen by a human piloting what, from the description, is likely a Kestrel. It was last seen traveling through the Coalition systems bordering human space.

values: Looks like a convention of rogues, scoundrels, and villainy has gathered at Greenrock. More than usual, that is.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Midnight Market: Trailblazer 1

name: Midnight Market: Trailblazer 2

children.key: You land in a secluded area away from the spaceport and sneak in covertly over land.

When you arrive, you take cover in a nearby alley. Playing out before you is a familiar scene. The guns have been replaced with locally produced weapons, but you are certain that the Coalition ship on auction here is the same one you saw on auction before! This time, the auctioneer is human. He is a strong muscular man in the rough clothing of a pirate warlord. His accent hints that he might have been raised on New China.

The crowd of potential buyers is filled with pirate warlords, including a group from Scar's Legion in the north. A delegation representing the Oathbreakers stands out from the crowd with their disheveled Navy uniforms. You even see some bounty hunters present. Getting tangled up in this riff raff would not be a good idea.

The bidding in the auction is fierce, as one would expect. Any of these groups would benefit from adding an alien warship to their fleet. In the end, the Oathbreakers outbid everyone. There is some angry shouting and fighting until a few unruly pirates are dead. The rest of the crowd is smart enough to walk away. The auctioneer himself boards a Kestrel after receiving payment. Only the Oathbreakers remain with their prize.
(Prepare an ambush for when the Oathbreakers leave.)
You've decided that even with the other groups gone, you aren't ready to take on an Oathbreaker fleet and their new toy. You wait until they finally launch, then head back to your ship.
You've decided to ambush the Oathbreakers as soon as they enter orbit. You rush back to your ship and prepare to make a surprise attack.

name: Midnight Justicar First Contact 2

children.key: You are escorted to your assigned landing pad. After disembarking, a trio of mechanical drones are waiting to escort you to the courthouse. As you walk, you notice that the city is only populated by robots or androids. Eventually, you arrive at a building that is difficult to distinguish from the others. The drones lead you to a kiosk. A robot situated on the other side addresses you.
"Captain <first> <last> identified. Priority incident 9173648520. Do you dispute your penalty?"
"Objection. Evidence of crime was detected. You are guilty."
"Justicar Code of Conduct Statute 3180 Subsection 512 paragraph 7."
"Summary: Use of an unapproved method of hyperspace travel. The standard penalty is a fine of 1,000,000 credits."

"Justicar Code of Conduct Statute 0066 Subsection 137 paragraph 11 allows an alternative penalty. The convict is placed into cryosleep for lifetime service in an Incarceration Cell, storing and providing energy as needed. Do you consent to the alternative penalty?"

"Consent confirmed." Before you can say anything else you are dropped though a hole in the floor and flash frozen. Your body is placed into an Incarceration Cell and you spend the rest of your existence as a living battery for a Justicar ship.
You are allowed to leave the courthouse. The drones never leave your side. They allow you to take a guided tour of the spaceport before returning to your ship.

name: Geddonia's Folly (Corpse)

values: Geddonia was a highly advanced species older than the Drak. They were small spheres of light with telekinetic powers that lived in large crystalline structures. The only active remnant of their civilization is a doomsday device called the Worldcrusher.

children.key: Soon after entering the system, a voice speaks directly to your mind.

"Welcome to the remains of Geddonia. The beings who once lived here were already old when the Drak were young. The object patrolling the nearby system is the final monument to their civilization. If you decide to visit that system, take care to only observe it from a distance. The Worldcrusher can be very dangerous when viewed up close. Millions died luring it away from here to its present location. Sadly, by then it was already too late for the Geddonians."

"You may find this difficult to believe. But the Worldcrusher was not built as a weapon of war. One of their youths constructed it in an attempt to impress the elders in a competition of scientific prowess," replies the voice in your head.
"A science project? You're telling me a kid's science project caused the downfall of their entire civilization?" you ask.

"Yes. It was the Geddonian's folly that taught us the wisdom of limiting technological access to those who have the maturity to use it responsibly. Remember the Geddonians and learn from their downfall."

As the voice fades from your mind you see visions of aliens made of light living in large crystalline structures that shatter as their world is destroyed. The image the vision presents of the Geddonian's physical nature is completely beyond your own experience. The closest approximation you can relate to them is that each resembled a star smaller in size than a human. They possessed telekinetic powers to manipulate their environment. Somehow, you're certain that if you were to encounter one and gaze upon it with your own eyes, you would go blind from the intensity of the light.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Geddonia's Folly (Corpse)

name: First Contact: Geddonia

children.key: A telepathic voice speaks to you again. "Congratulations. You are one of a very few who have managed to force the Worldcrusher to phase into another quantum space time. None can predict when it will return."

"The Worldcrusher is a techonological marvel. The mind that spawned it was a pinnacle of genius unlikely to be reached again. The construct propels itself by quantum shifting on a sub atomic level. Whenever it exists, it simultaneously does not exist. And while it does not exist now, it continues to exist elsewhen. The paradox diffusion waves surrounding it are the result of reality attempting to resolve this conundrum to account for the displacement caused by the effect of..." The voice continues on, but you are starting to develop a headache and are unable to focus on the thoughts being forced upon you.

Eventually the voice fades and your consciousness briefly latches onto something. You have a vague memory of being lectured about a cat in a box that was both alive and dead at the same time, until the box was opened. Or something like that. Then the headache intensifies.

values: Captain Ayab is hunting an ancient subsidurial known as the Gray Eye. You're still not sure how you got roped into this...
A starship captain seeking revenge against the Gray Eye that destroyed his previous ship. With his new ship, the Ayab's Revenge, he is recruiting other starship captains to join his fleet.
Very old Subsidurials are known as Gray Eyes. They have thicker hides and can be temperamental, having learned how to deliver a powerful slap with their tail.

children.key: You're at a spaceport bar when a grizzeled old starship captain with a crazed expression on his face approaches your table.
"Name's Ayab. Captain Ayab. You're just the kind of fresh recruit I need to join my fleet on the hunt."
"Gray Eye!" The man screams loudly. "The accursed creature destroyed my first ship! But now I finally have a new ship and am building up my fleet! Soon it will know my revenge!"
"Welcome to my fleet, <last>! I'll see you up in orbit!" The man stomps off to terrorize other bar patrons. You're still not sure what just happened.

values: Captain Ayab will fight by your side until the horrible squid monsters have been defeated.

children.key: A grizzled old starship captain stumbles out of a spaceport bar and calls out to you. "Hey kid! Remember me? Captain Ayab!" This was the man who insisted on recruiting you into his fleet to hunt down a Gray Eye. His mood saddens. "It's terrible <first>! Terrible!"
"It's the squid, <first>! The squid!" He's shouting uncontrollably as other people back away in fear. "I got stuck in this space swarming with them! We have to kill them! All of them!"

"Space squid!" He shouts "Those tentacled monsters are a menace!". By now, the streets around you are abandoned, the locals having been scared off by his tirade. "But I'm glad you're here to join me, <first>."
"As part of my fleet you'll assist me in exterminating this wretched threat to humanity! It'll be more dangerous than our hunt for the Gray Eye, but I'm sure you're up to the task. See you in orbit!"

He's already rushing off to the landing pads before you can respond. You watch him board what appears to be an Argosy so heavily modified that it could be classified a Marauder. Maybe he'll be useful in the fight against the Pug...

values: The exposed mantle of Hell's Maw is home to a thriving colony of these creatures. While they are content to harmlessly scavenge for minerals, they can become dangerous when provoked. One of their tendrils is able to emit electrical bursts which can disrupt a ship's power systems.

children.key: You wait until the exposed core is facing away from the sun and pick a landing spot near the edge of the planet's broken crust. Even at night the ambient heat here is intense, with temperatures slightly above the recommended safety limits for your environmental suit. Your ship's scanners alert you to the presence of several large lifeforms moving about on the rocky terrain below. Their translucent bodies gives them the appearance of ghostly jellyfish. While observing them consume the exposed minerals from the planet's gaping wound, you see occasional flashes of light when they create some form of energy discharge. Between the presence of these creatures and other environmental hazards, it's probably not a good idea to disembark.

Plasma Parasites are a scourge plaguing the Coalition. They are attracted to starship engine emissions and will swarm over them. While they are not inherently hostile, they are prone to violently exploding from exposure to even minor weapons fire. Appearing only after the Coalition gained their independence, some believe them to be biological weapons unleashed by the Quarg.
First Contact: Plasma Parasite Log Patched

name: Gathering Specimens: Liquid Metal

children.key: Do you want to turn in the liquid metal specimen to the Syndicate? There might be a big reward. Or this could be an opportunity to get arrested for being in possession of stolen property...
You decide to keep the specimen instead of turning it in. Remember to keep it installed so it doesn't get mixed in with the regular cargo.
The Syndicate representative is very appreciative for the return of their stolen property and grants you 1,000,000 credits as a reward. They aren't asking any questions. As for you...
"What is the Syndicate going to do with this?"

"Syndicate patrols found the original HG-80 specimen while patrolling the Northern Passage. Patents have been filed with the Republic. It is by all rights, physical and intellectual, property of the Syndicate."
"As you can imagine, there are several commercial and industrial uses for this material. You're a pilot, right? Perhaps we'll contact you when we have a new hull to test out."
The Syndicate representative thanks you again for returning their property. Security escorts you safely outside...

name: Gathering Specimens: Liquid Metal Amalgam
description: The Syndicate has lost control of their Amalgam test ship Mythreal. It was last spotted heading towards the Paradise Planets. Locate and neutralize the ship before it can harm any more people.

values: The Syndicate has lost control of their Amalgam test ship Mythreal. It was last spotted heading towards the Paradise Planets. Locate and neutralize the ship before it can harm any more people.

children.key: You've won a bet and have been given the opportunity to eat Rock Scavenger for free at the spaceport bar and grill! Before you can take a bite, the communications device of everyone in the restaurant loudly beeps, vibrates, or otherwise alerts their owners that they have a message.

You check yours and are surprised to get a message from the Syndicate representative who you delivered the Liquid Metal sample to: "Greetings Captain <first> <last>. The liquid metal specimen was used to make the test model Amalgam ship, Mythreal. You are invited to help test the ship as previously discussed. If you are anywhere near the Paradise Planets, we advise you to head over there if you want to try and stop the Mythreal. Unlike our normal testing procedures, you are not forbidden from destroying or capturing this ship.
As you are mulling over the odd message, someone watching the news display mutters, "Ghost Ship." You look up in time to see a Quicksilver destroy a Navy Cruiser.

As you are watching, the Quicksilver changes form! Now it looks more like a heavily modified Marauder Quicksilver. Realization of what you are watching dawns on you as you notice the Quicksilver doesn't have any color other than the underlying metal...

values: The Mythreal is no longer a threat. Return to <origin> and check if the authorities will reward you for your efforts.
The Mythreal is still in orbit. Get back up there!

name: Gathering Specimens: Conservatory Conclusion

values: You receive a message from the Free Worlds Conservatory administrators: "Your contributions have lead to a research break through! Visit the Conservatory on <destination> to learn more."
The Conservatory Specimen research project yielded a cure for Chronic Hyperspace Traveler's Disorder. A portion of the profits from sales of this miracle drug will be paid to me.

children.key: The administrators thank you for helping with the research. And now they present the results of that work: a cure for Chronic Hyperspace Traveler's Disorder.

They explain, "When you've been traveling for days on a cramped ship through Hyperspace, you may experience the following symptoms: muscle soreness, irritability, restlessness, and difficulty sleeping."

"It's Chronic Hyperspace Traveler's Disorder, a condition that affects more than 90% of space travelers to the detriment of their well being. And since you played a important role in developing the cure, a portion of the profits from sales of this miracle drug will be paid to you. Congratulations!"
While you'll gladly accept the reward for your efforts, you can't help but wonder what sort of other projects the Conservatory is researching.

name: Gathering Specimens: Remnant Conclusion
description: Escort the prototype Raptor to <destination>.

children.key: You notice a strange ship parked at the spaceport. While there are some bits of Remnant technology installed on it, the ship is very different from their other designs.
As you are studying the mysterious ship, Taely approaches you. "I see you found the Raptor," she signs.
"It is different from the other Remnant ships."
"Its design was based on the research results from studying the genetic samples you brought us."
"It was made from those jars of goop?"
"It is more accurate to say that this ship was grown, not made. I will admit, I had my doubts. It is not as elegant as our other ships. But it has some features they lack." She pets the hull.
"Not just yet. I have to take it to Caelian for weapons installation. Care to join me?"
You prepare for the journey to <destination>.

values: Taely and the Raptor haven't arrived yet. Better head back to space and make sure they're okay.

The reselt of the Remnant Specimen Research is the Raptor Prototype. Since the research could not have been possible without the specimens I gathered, I've been entrusted with making test flights using the prototype.

children.key: Taely lands the Raptor. Before departing on a ship bound for Viminal, she signs, "I think you'll enjoy piloting the Raptor. The engines are very responsive."
Prefect Chilia arrives with a team ready to install the weapons systems. As you watch them unload the crates, you wonder how the different specimens contributed to each weapon's design.
It doesn't take long for the team to finish. "The Raptor is ready for testing. May the Embers burn bright for you, captain!" he sings.

name: First Contact: Subsidurials

children.key: It is unclear what these creatures are, where they come from, or how they evolved. Scientists have dissected several, but so far the results have simply been that these creatures contain no materials or resources of value; are not even slightly edible, and are too big to be kept as pets.
To date, none have demonstrated any sign of sapience, and the few captains who have seen them basically consider them to be the bison of space.

As you land you notice a ship on a nearby landing pad is unloading some kind of huge creature bound to a hoverlift. It sort of looks like a giant hairy slug. Despite its bindings, the creature manages to make the hoverlift bounce around on the landing pad. Several dock workers narrowly avoid being crushed by it.

When you disembark from your own ship, you can hear a representative from the port authority ordering the captain of the other ship to unbind the creature and let it go. Supposedly, the creature is called a "Subsidurial" and has no scientific, commercial, or nutritional value whatsoever.
"At least once a month!" yells the representative. "A new inexperienced captain hauls one in thinking he's caught some rare valuable specimen that will put him in the history books. Idiots!"
