name: Jail Break Fake

children.key: The pirates thank you for rescuing their warlord... and promptly shoot him!
It turns out a new pirate warlord took over while you were gone. He thanks you for a job well done and orders his crew to shower you with their gratitude. They draw their guns...
... and shoot them into the air! You realize your heart is pounding while they laugh at your expense. The new warlord tells you to get lost while he's still in a good mood.
You raise your hands in the air in a show of surrender. The pirates regard your gesture, shrug, and open fire.
Your cries for a parley are met with derision and laughter before they open fire.
You're already off running before the first clumsy shots ring out. After a frenzied rush, you make it back to your ship and skip the safety protocols for an immediate launch...
You die in a shower of bullets before you even aim at any of them.
Your crew fights bravely. Unfortunately, a stray bullet finds its way into your vital organs.
Your crew fights bravely, but the enemy has reinforcements arriving. Time to beat a hasty retreat!

name: Highly Wanted Passenger (Dirt Belt)
description: This criminal is wanted by every law enforcement agency in the galaxy and needs safe transport to <destination> with their <cargo>. The payment is high at an amazing <payment>, but transporting such a person could lead to trouble.

values: This criminal is wanted by every law enforcement agency in the galaxy and needs safe transport to <destination> with their <cargo>. The payment is high at an amazing <payment>, but transporting such a person could lead to trouble.

Law enforcement rush their way onto your ship through the airlocks, suited head to toe in armor and armed to the teeth. Your passenger is quickly made to surrender and is hauled off in cuffs. The officers consider detaining you as well, but eventually decide to only fine you to reduce the trouble they have to go through.
Your passenger never arrived at <destination>. This doesn't help to establish a name as reliable, no-questions-asked, transporter.

Rather than simply accept the credits, you wonder if they would be willing to offer some other kind of reward. You're certain the station was firing Pug weapons during the battle. This is a knowledge storehouse with all sorts of secrets kept behind locked doors...
(Request a piece of super secret tech.)

They were expecting your request. In the next room they already prepared something to share with you, likely chosen due to your involvement with the recent Pug incident at Deneb: a set of Pug engines larger than any you've seen before. If you don't have 202 tons of available cargo space on your ship, you won't be able to take them off the station...
"I'll take them, but where did you get these?"
"I can't fit these in my cargo hold!"

name: Asteroid Catapult: Midnight Market 2
description: Take the Catapult Schematics to Barmy Edwards on <destination> and convince him to create one.

values: Take the Catapult Schematics to Barmy Edwards on <destination> and convince him to create one.

children.key: You find the bar indicated on the invitation from the mysterious seller. As your eyes adjust to the dark smoke-filled interior, you see the place is packed with all sorts of pirate riff-raff. A group of cloaked figures in a corner booth are staring at you. Before you can react, a bald man in a suit waves you over to a private room.
"Welcome, Captain <last>." He holds up a data pad. "Simply confirm payment on this data pad and it's all yours!"
"What, exactly, am I buying?" you ask.

He holds up a data chip. "Behold! Schematics for the Asteroid Catapult that the Oathbreaker's space battle station Thermopylae was outfitted with! These are no mere copy, but the original data files written by the person who invented the weapon!"
You remember the batle with that space station and its Asteroid Catapult.
(Do not purchase the Asteroid Catapult Schematics.)

He puts away the data pad. "Unfortunately, it appears we were unable to reach an agreement. Thank you for your time. However, I suggest you depart immediately." The cloaked figures you saw when you arrived earlier have now entered the room and you decide to follow the man's suggestion.
"Congratulations on your purchase captain. I'm sure you won't regret it. You'll hear from us again if we happen to acquire any more unique merchandise that might interest you."
When you consider who might be able to turn these schematics into a real physical weapon, one name rises to the top: Barmy Edwards.

values: Purchased the schematics for an asteroid catapult on the Midnight Market. Supposedly, these are the original files from whoever invented the weapon. Now I just need to find an engineer who's willing to build it.
Barmy Edwards informed me that all weapons research involving asteroids was banned by all the major human governments. If I want to make an Asteroid Catapult, I'll have to go beyond human space.

children.key: Of all the people you know, Barmy Edwards is the person most likely to be able to take the Asteroid Catapult schematics and make it real. You visit the labs of Kraz Cybernetics to find out if he's interested. You're surprised by his response.
"No." He says, "I remember hearing something about you getting into legal trouble regarding 'Unlawful Use of an Asteroid' or something similar. I want no part of that."
"That was just a misunderstanding. The courts cleared my case."

"Alright. This is top secret. But since you have the schematics, I suppose you have a need to know. The Thermopylae wasn't just something the Oathbreakers cooked up on their own. It was a stolen Navy prototype that was never deployed during the war." He pauses a moment to let that sink in.

"The Republic marked the project a failure, because the type of asteroids used as ammunition would melt during atmospheric entry. While still destructive to the local impact area, the results were no more effective than a normal area bombardment with conventional weapons."

"Your 'unlawful use of an asteroid' stunt was where the problem started. Republic intelligence was concerned that we had developed our own asteroid weapons program. Various political machinations went into effect. Before you had even set foot in a courtroom, an under the table deal was negotiated between the Republic, the Free Worlds, and the Syndicate. All weapons research involving asteroids were banned. So there's no way I'm getting involved. If you're determined, you'll just have to find someone else to help you with it."

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Asteroid Catapult: Midnight Market 2

name: Asteroid Catapult: Remnant
description: Return to <destination> after one month to retrieve the Asteroid Catapult that Taely is constructing.

values: Return to <destination> after one month to retrieve the Asteroid Catapult that Taely is constructing.

children.key: You remember Taely was interested in examples of the recent development of human technology. Do you want to see if she'd be interested in making the Asteroid Catapult?
You find her directing a crew that is sorting out a collection of outfits salvaged during a recent expedition. She notices you and signs, "Hello Captain <last>, how can I help you?"
"I'd like you to build something for me."

She looks over the data and signs "This is just a rail gun..." There is a pause as she continues to look over the data. "Oh! Well, the choice of ammunition is interesting. Yes, I can make one. Pay us 2,000,000 credits and it should be ready in a month."
After you confirm payment, she signs "As I said, return here in a month and we will have it ready for you."

She signs, "I must admit, such a weapon would be slow to reload and difficult to aim. Probably not worth the cost and effort. Oh, well. It seemed like it would have been an interesting project." A group of technicians unloading some Korath outfits motion for Taely's attention and she bids you farewell.

values: I've convinced the Remnant engineering prefect, Taely, to construct an Asteroid Catapult for me. It should be ready after a month.
Taely is still working on the construction of the Asteroid Catapult. She assures you it will be completed on schedule.
Taely finally finished construction of the Asteroid Catapult. She has arranged for the outfitters on Viminal to supply ammunition when I need it.

children.key: Taely sends you a message informing you that the Asteroid Catapult is ready. "I must admit, this weapon is slow to reload and will be difficult to aim. But it was an interesting project to work on! I've made arrangements for the local outfitters to stock ammunition with the right size, shape, and magnetic properties for you."
She finishes delivering the weapon to you and thanks you for the interesting project.

She finishes delivering the weapon to you and signs, "A few days ago someone infiltrated the factory where the weapon was being constructed. Surprisingly, both the weapon and the schematic data were undisturbed. However, our security forces still take this breech seriously and are investigating a likely suspect. I can't give you any more details than that for now."

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Asteroid Catapult: Remnant

name: Asteroid Catapult: Angry Squirrels
description: Return to <destination> after one month to retrieve the Asteroid Catapult that Go Foo Ku is constructing.

values: Return to <destination> after one month to retrieve the Asteroid Catapult that Go Foo Ku is constructing.

children.key: You remember dropping off the Unfettered weapons designer, Go Foo Ku, on this planet. Do you want to see if he'd be interested in making the Asteroid Catapult?

After some searching, you find his laboratory isolated in a desolate valley. There are a number of craters nearby. The scorch marks and the smell of burnt ozone in the air give you the impression that these were formed recently. When you meet Go Foo Ku, he seems to be in a better mood than he was the last time you saw him.

You travel to his laboratory isolated in a desolate valley. As before, the land is burned with scorch marks and marred by craters of various sizes. Fortunately, the building is still standing. Go Foo Ku is inside, engaged in his wild research experiments.

"Ah, Captain <last>! Thank you for your previous assistance. As you can see, I am still hard at work on testing the limits of the countermeasures technology." Somehow, he has managed to acquire several more of the Quarg devices. One of them sits disassembled on a work table. There is a sudden shower of sparks from the exposed circuitry. Go Foo Ku pays no attention to the sudden burst of sound and light. "So, captain, what brought you all the way out here today?"
"I'd like you to build something for me."

You show him the schematics for the Asteroid Catapult. After taking a moment to look them over, Go Foo Ku begins laughing boisterously. "The monkey wants to throw rocks at his enemies!" After he gets the laughter out of his system, he says "This is basically a large rail gun with some exotic ammunition... Sure, I can make one. Pay me 2,000,000 credits and it should be ready in a month."
"Great! Please confirm payment on this data pad." After you confirm payment, he comments, "As I said, return here in a month and I'll have it ready for you."

"I must admit, such a weapon would be slow to reload and difficult to aim. Probably not worth the cost and effort. Ah, well. It sounded like it would have been a fun project. Thanks for the laugh, but I have to get back to work." He returns to tinkering with the Quarg devices."

children.key: Go Foo Ku sends you a message informing you that the Asteroid Catapult is ready. "I must admit, this weapon is slow to reload and will be difficult to aim. name: Destroy Independence (North)
description: The Independence is the last Mastodon city ship still in service. You've received a tip that it will pass through <waypoints>. Capture this rare ship and add it to your fleet!

values: The Independence is the last Mastodon city ship still in service. You've received a tip that it will pass through <waypoints>. Capture this rare ship and add it to your fleet!
event: fwc peace with the navy

children.key: You're trying to relax at a bar when a woman approaches you. "Captain <first> <last>?"
"You've earned a bit of fame from your previous battles."
"I'm an information broker. I have info on the route that the Mastodon city ship 'Independence' will be taking on its next flight. I'm willing to sell for 15,000. Are you interested?"
"How do I know this info is legitimate?"
"If you're not interested, I'll just find someone else." She gets up to leave.
"Don't let the door hit you on the way out."
You place 15,000 in credit chips on the table and she hands you a data chip. "Pleasure doing business with you, captain."
When you load the data from the chip, you learn that the Independence will pass through the Mirzam system very soon. There isn't much room to take detours...

values: There is no sign of the Mastodon city ship. However, a large Navy fleet is waiting for you. A trap! That information broker set you up!"
Was lured to Mirzam with the promise of an easy way to capture the Mastodon city ship "Independence." It turned out to be a trap set up by the Republic.
event: fwc peace with the navy

name: Escort Requiem Alpha
description: Escort an old War Hauler to <destination> by <date> in preparation for a Remembrance Day festival. War Haulers are a rare antique highly prized by collectors. Pirates may try to hijack the ship. Payment is <payment>.

values: Escort an old War Hauler to <destination> by <date> in preparation for a Remembrance Day festival. War Haulers are a rare antique highly prized by collectors. Pirates may try to hijack the ship. Payment is <payment>.

children.key: Your ship's warning alarm starts soon after entering the system. A fleet of ships that was waiting here has targeted you with their weapons. The <npc> transmits a message to you:

"Thank you for your help evading those pirates earlier. Unfortunately for you, our own organization was planning to steal the <npc> from the start. If only the owner of the ship hadn't been so cautious, you wouldn't have had to get involved. Nothing personal captain, this is just business."

values: The <npc> has been defeated. You make a mental note to check with the local authorities to see if there is any reward for your effort.
A simple job escorting an old War Hauler turned into a trap. With some effort, I fought off the traitorous captain and his allies. Managed to collect some bounty rewards for my trouble too.

children.key: It turns out the festival had been canceled as soon as it was approved. The zoning applications were merely filed as a ruse to lure the <npc> out to this remote area of the galaxy where it could easily be stolen.

"You look into the names of the ships you fought and manage to find a few outstanding bounties for a few of them. After showing video of your battle to the local authorities, you manage to scrape together <payment> in reward money for your effort."

name: Jump Drive Theft 1
description: Infiltrate a Syndicate R&D facility and retrieve the research sample in Lab 51. Deliver it to Stormhold in the Alcyone system.

values: Infiltrate a Syndicate R&D facility and retrieve the research sample in Lab 51. Deliver it to Stormhold in the Alcyone system.

children.key: You receive a message when you land. "Captain <first> <last>, you have a reputation for doing competent work. We have a job suitable for a person with your skills and experience with less than legal activities. 1,000,000 credit payment on delivery. Will you accept?

Your mysterious employer sends you an address on Hephaestus and detailed instructions of the interior layout and security protocols of a Syndicate lab. Specifically, Laboratory 51. Your mission is to infiltrate the lab and retrieve the research sample. Once you do so, you will have ten days to deliver it to a rendezvous location on Stormhold in the Alcyone system. Aborting this mission or failure to deliver by the expected date will not be looked kindly upon.

values: Took on a job to steal a research sample from a Syndicate lab for the Midnight Market. I hope I'm not getting in over my head with this one.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Jump Drive Theft 1

name: Jump Drive Theft 2
description: Infiltrate a Syndicate R&D facility and retrieve the research sample in Lab 51. Deliver it to Stormhold by <date> in the Alcyone system.

values: Infiltrate a Syndicate R&D facility and retrieve the research sample in Lab 51. Deliver it to Stormhold by <date> in the Alcyone system.

children.key: Someone from planetary security must have been bribed by your employer. No one questions you as you locate a discreet landing location near the facility housing Laboratory 51. Following the instructions you were given, you manage to bypass the facility's security systems and enter the lab. Inside, you find an alien device.

According to the research notes here, this device is a functional Jump Drive! You load it onto a hover cart and work to remove it from the facility, taking care to avoid the guard patrols with the aid of the schedule your employer provided. Once you get back to your ship, you load the Jump Drive onto it and take off.

values: The item I found in the Syndicate lab was a functional Jump Drive. I decided to keep it for myself rather than hand it over to the Midnight Market.
It appears that no one from the lab is pursuing you. Your employer must have spent a considerable sum bribing Syndicate employees to help you slip through their security.
Having a jump drive gives you access to regions of space hyperdrives can't reach. You have a few days before the delivery deadline...
A short detour to try out this jump drive couldn't hurt, could it? You have a few days before the delivery deadline...
A jump drive is a rare piece of technology. The thought of keeping it for yourself crosses your mind...
Only a few more days before the scheduled delivery date for this jump drive. Should you formally abort the mission? The thought of keeping it for yourself crosses your mind...

A small fleet of Syndicate security ships is patrolling the system. One of them hails you. "<ship>, I know what you took from Lab 51. You can be boarded while we retrieve the item, or you can pay us off. Your choice, captain. Oh, and don't expect any pirates to interfere. We already have an understanding with them regarding you."
The item I found in the Syndicate lab was a functional Jump Drive. I decided to keep it for myself rather than hand it over to the Midnight Market.
The rendezvous location is deserted. The presence of the Syndicate patrol must have scared off your contact.
A network of fencers, smugglers, and patrons forming an exclusive black market community. Not sure how I got on their list, but the deals look too good to pass up.

name: Midnight Smugglers False Hope 1
description: Escort the <npc> and the escaped slaves it is transporting to <destination>, far away from their pirate oppressor. The captain promises to give you <payment>.

values: Escort the <npc> and the escaped slaves it is transporting to <destination>, far away from their pirate oppressor. The captain promises to give you <payment>.

children.key: When you return to the <ship> a man is waiting at the landing pad. As you approach he asks,"Are you the owner of this ship?"
He smirks. "It's looks like a good ship, but that's not what I'm after."

The man gives you a piercing stare. "I need help. Well, my passengers need help." He scratches his head, appearing flustered. "It's complicated. I wasn't planning to take on this job, but I was asked to help free some slaves by transporting them to <planet>." You remember taking on a similar job in the past.

He winces. "I'm afraid this could technically be seen as human smuggling. Illegal immigration. I see you're with the Free Worlds, so I was hoping you could escort me. Maybe keep the Navy distracted if they get too close. I can pay <payment>." That seems like a reasonable escort fee.
"Aren't they going to scan you at <planet>?"
He relaxes. "The person who made the request gave me a contact who will let me slip past security. So, how about it?"
He looks disappointed. "Well, it was worth a shot. Maybe I should reconsider doing this job..." He shakes his head as he walks off.
His face lights up. "Thank you!" He reaches out to shake your hand. "The name's Slipstein. Captain of the <npc>.

description: Transport Captain Slipstein and the <bunks> freed slaves to <destination> where he will stand trial.

values: Transport Captain Slipstein and the <bunks> freed slaves to <destination> where he will stand trial.

values: I met another captain who agreed to lead slaves to freedom from pirate oppression. After escorting them to Shroud, the slaves were still in chains. He scowls. "Looks like you won't let this go. How about another 80,000 credits? Just forget about them and go on with your life." He glances at the rest of his crew...

values: A human smuggler who transported slaves to Shroud under the pretense of "liberating" them.

I met another captain who agreed to lead slaves to freedom from pirate oppression. After escorting them to Shroud, the slaves were still in chains. I... I probably shouldn't record this. But the credit log shows the deposit into my account. This... It was a bribe. Slipstein paid me to ignore what he was doing and abandon those people. If anyone reads this, just know that I was only a security escort and did not actively participate in capturing his passengers or whatever happened to them after we parted ways. I... I am not involved.

children.key: Slipstein grins. "I'm glad you're willing to be reasonable." He transfers 80,000 credits to your account. "Have a pleasant day Captain <last>." One of Slipstein's crew drives the truck away. Whatever fate await its passengers is out of your hands...
Your crew fights bravely, but you die during the chaos of battle.

After a vicious battle, Slipstein surrenders. Even as you free the slaves he remains indignant. "I was hoping we could avoid this pointless and messy hassle. But fine. Go ahead, hand me over to the authorities. There isn't a court in the Republic that will convict me."

values: A human smuggler who transported slaves to Shroud under the pretense of "liberating" them.

I met another captain who agreed to lead slaves to freedom from pirate oppression. After escorting them to Shroud, the slaves were still in chains. After a violent confrontation, I arrested Slipstein for human trafficking under my authority as a Militia captain. I'll let the judiciary on Bourne sort out the legal details.

children.key: Slipstein's smug arrogance melts at those words. Some of the freed slaves agree to travel with you to <planet> so that they can testify in court. Fortunately, the evidence can serve as transportation. It even has a brig to hold Slipstein in.
(The replacement crew for the <npc> will cost 6,000 credits per day.)

values: Died in custody during transport to Bourne for his involvement in slavery and human trafficking. The crew claims that he killed himself, but the circumstances surrounding his death seem suspicious to some and when word gets out about this it became a sensational news story.

Before leaving Shroud I hired a replacement crew for Slipstein's ship. The trip to Bourne was long. After we arrived we found Slipstein's corpse in the Brig of the Saint James. The crew claims he killed himself. The autopsy indicates he died from strangulation. But the video feed in his cell was deleted...

children.key: After a long journey, you've finally brought Slipstein to justice. At least, that's what you thought when you arrived. When you try to retrieve him from the brig you find his dead body. The crew piloting his former ship insist he must have killed himself. But the circumstances surrounding his death seem suspicious to some and when word gets out about this it becomes a sensational news story.

At least the former slaves who traveled with you testify that he was indeed a slave trafficker. The Free Worlds grants them asylum. As for his ship, they allow you to keep it. A Vicious Falcon is an extremely rare Marauder variant. You should thoroughly inspect it in the outfitter to make sure he didn't leave any nasty surprises hidden inside.

You locate the hangar. Opening it you find a nasty surprise: a nuclear warhead with a countdown timer that triggers as soon as you find it!
Despite your best efforts, there is no escaping the explosion.

Despite your effort, you were unable to disarm the warhead before it explodes. If life were a game, you could load a save file and try disarming it again. You might have better success if you learn how these devices work.

Recalling what you previously learned about nuke activation settings, you pop open a panel and see the activation code is set at "6-6-6". Enter the deactivation code. It is:

name: Midnight Market: Nukes of Peace?

children.key: One of the locals approaches you. "<first> <last>, welcome to <origin>. We believe you would be a suitable client for some special merchandise we happen to have available."
"I'm not interested in buying anything right now."
"That's not important. Are you interested or not?"

"Please follow me." The stranger leads you through a series of sidestreets and alleys. You pass by several shops selling strange food and exotic merchandise. As you walk, you can't help but notice you are getting farther away from the spaceport...
(Ditch the stranger and return to the spaceport.)
Suddenly you are ambushed from behind! There's no room for discussion. These people are out for blood!
Fortunately you are armed and manage to fight off your attackers. With nothing better to do, you decide to check out some of those shops on the long walk back to the spaceport.
Before you can draw your weapon, sudden pain pierces your back! You turn to see one of your attackers holding a knife covered with your blood. The rest of them close in to finish you off...

After a long walk you arrive at what looks like an abandoned store. The doors and windows are boarded up. Despite this, you notice someone move to hide behind a curtain on the upper floor. The stranger leads you to a side entrance. Inside are a pair of massive crates. The stranger opens one, saying "Behold! Nuclear missiles, a powerful addition to your arsenal. Just confirm payment of 2,000,000 credits on this datapad and they're yours."
You pull out your gun and tell the stranger you'll be taking the missiles for free.

The room explodes in a burst of violence as guards suddenly swarm in from other rooms in the building. You manage to put several down before one of them gets lucky with a knife. Your hands become slick with blood as you grasp at the wound. The surviving guards put a bullet into your head.

The room explodes in a burst of violence as guards suddenly swarm in from other rooms in the building. Though you expend all of your bullets in the fire fight, you miraculously come out of that bloodbath unharmed. A search of the building reveals several more crates in a hidden underground bunker. You begin the arduous task of hauling them back to your ship.

The stranger puts away the datapad while some guards enter from adjoining rooms. "It appears our negotiations have failed. Please find your own way back to the spaceport." You begin the long walk back. Maybe you can grab something to eat from one of the shops you passed earlier...
"Good choice captain. We'll help haul them back to your ship." Several burly men appear from other rooms in the building and help load the crates into a truck. The ride back is smooth and uneventful.
The seller opens a panel on the missile's side. "Have you read the Bible?"

Inside the panel are a set of controls for entering three digits. "The factory default is all zeroes. Activation is the number of the beast." The stranger sets all three digits to "6-6-6". A mechanism within the missile activates and you can hear a low hum that slowly fades away. "Deactivation is a walk through the valley of the shadow of death. Go ahead."
"I, uh, don't remember reading that part..."
"What are you doing!?!" The stranger shrieks as you are all vaporized in a nuclear blast..."

values: Today I learned the activation code for a Nuclear Missile is the number of the beast and deactivation code is "2-3-4". The latter is supposedly inspired by Psalm 23:4 from the Bible.

children.key: The stranger reaches over and sets the digits to "2-3-4". Closing the panel, the stranger says, "Psalm twenty three four. Well?"

values: Today I learned the activation code for a Nuclear Missile is the number of the beast and deactivation code is "2-3-4". The latter is inspired by Psalm twenty three four from the Bible: "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me; your rod and your staff, they comfort me."

children.key: Setting the digits to "2-3-4" causes the mechanism within to deactivate. The stranger smiles while closing the panel. "Well?"

values: Today I learned activation code for a Nuclear Missile is "6-6-6" and the deactivation code is "2-3-4". These are supposedly references to something from the Bible, but the person who taught you never specified what they are.

children.key: Inside the panel are a set of controls for setting three digits. "The factory default is all zeroes. Activation is six, six, and six." The stranger sets all three digits to "6-6-6". A mechanism within the missile activates and you can hear a low hum that slowly fades away. "Deactivation is two, three, and four." The stranger sets the digits to "2-3-4" and the mechanisms within make a few noises before falling silent. Satisfied, the stranger closes the panel. "Well?"

name: Nuke Deactivation Code

children.key: A sales clerk is demonstrating how to operate Nuclear Missiles to other customers. Listen in?
Are you sure? This information could help save your life in the future.
(I am not interested in this information.)

The sales clerk opens a panel on the side of the missile. Inside are controls for setting three digits. "The factory setting on these defaults to zero, zero, and zero. Activation is set at six, six, and six. To deactivate, set the digits to two, three, and four. Any questions?"
"Sorry, I'm not authorized to do that."
"Yes! Simply set the digits back to six, six, and six."

name: Thraal: Moreau

children.key: Soon after arriving, you receive a distress signal from a Shuttle Pod. A man speaks, "My goodness, it's been forever and a half since I've seen another human! Can you help me? My ship is disabled! Any assist-" The signal dies out. It's unusual to find a lone Shuttle Pod outside of human space. Perhaps you can get his story after assisting him.

After introductions you learn that the man's name is Thraal. "I was aboard a ship, a Star Explorer named Icarus. We acquired a Jump Drive and were exploring this region of space. I had gone out in the Shuttle Pod to do some asteroid mining when aliens, the Korath, attacked the Icarus. Icarus fled, abandoning me in this system.
"It's amazing that you survived alone out here!"
"It's amazing the Korath didn't hunt you down!"
The man sighs. "It was hard at first. The Korath are a bit xenophobic. But once you get to know them, they aren't so bad."

Thraal places the cover back on some recently repaired circuits and says, "Would you like to meet them? I can arrange it." The Korath have been an implacable adversary. This could be a chance to establish peaceful relations with them. Before you respond, Thraal hails Gresku Fodar, the Korath station in this system, and speaks to them in their language. After a short exchange, he smiles at you reassuringly. "They're waiting."

You have no interest in old pirate tales and look elsewhere to relax.

"And so, afterwards me and the boys took our plunder. We then set off from Stormhold into the northern passage, where few dare to go unless ye have a good supply of fuel or a ramscoop. It was on the 3rd day of our voyage when it appeared out of the darkness: the Dire Omen. The ghost ship what haunts the northern passage descended upon us like a pelican on a bucket of sardines."
"A ghost ship!?!" you shout out. "Surely, you jest."
"It be real! I remember clear as day my tactical scanner readouts! That ship, the Dire Omen, has no crew! But it attacked us all the same. I escaped. The others... weren't so lucky."
The old pirate falls silent and stares somberly at his mug. The mood has shifted and it is clear he is done telling his tale.

values: Heard an old pirate's tale of a ghost ship haunting the far north near <planet> in the <system> system. He claimed the ship had no crew. Probably just an embellished tale of being caught off guard by a stray Navy drone. Still, he told the tale well. It would make a good ghost story to frighten young children.

name: Ghost Hunting: Dire Omen 3

children.key: As you land on <planet>, you recall the tale told by an old pirate regarding a ghost ship haunting the northern passage. <planet> is the closest pirate stronghold to the southern entrance of that dark corridor through northern space. Do you want to ask the locals about the Dire Omen?
You came here for other business. Ghost hunting will have to wait.

While walking around the spaceport you notice a woman studying the sky with a telescope. She's dressed like a stereotypical cowgirl from an old Earth western. The pistol at her hip is an overt warning to not consider her an easy mark. It is a necessary fashion accessory on any pirate world.
"Did y'all get that pickup line from some discount bin?" she replies with a drawl.
"Whoa, easy now." You raise your hands as a gesture of peace. "Actually, do you know anything about ghost ships?"
"The Dire Omen? Oh yeah, I may know a thang or two." She holds out her hand expectantly, palm up.
"Uh, hello?" she says in irritation. "Info ain't free. Is this your first time on a pirate world?"
You begrudgingly hand over some chips worth 500 credits.

"Yee haw! I love tourists. We don't get 'em often 'round these parts, what with all the killin' and lootin'." After pocketing the chips she extends her hand again. This time it's an offer to shake hands. "I go by the name Calamity, but you can call me Cali!"
"I'm <first>. So, about the ghost ship?" you ask.

"Right. Right. So a while back this weird alien ship drifts into the system from out of the dark edges of human space. The old thang is powered down. Typical derelict. So a bunch of the 'ol pirate boys head on out to do some salvagin'. Ain't no one has ownership rights to a derelict 'cept the one who gets to it first, right? Right. Thang is, that ship weren't no derelict. Soon as some poor fool got close, the durn thang sprung into action like an angry bull with a hot poker jammed into its butt. The few who survived swear up and down that their tacticals showed the ship had no crew. Ever since then, that durn ghost ship's been hauntin' the northern passage."
"Can you tell me what the ship looked like?" you ask.
"They reckon it's shaped like a ring."

values: Met someone on Stormhold named Cali who told me a story of how the ghost ship Dire Omen drifted into Alcyon from beyond human space. It might have spent centuries resting in peace before the pirates woke it up. Supposedly, it's shaped like a ring.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Ghost Hunting: Dire Omen 3

name: Ghost Hunting: Dire Omen 4

children.key: As you start to land you notice smoke and flames coming from a nearby parked ship. That's not too unusual in this dangerous sector of space. What does catch your eye is the nature of the damage. Large portions of the hull look to have melted right off. Whatever did this must generate intense heat.
(Best not to get involved. Go find another place to land.)
(Stick around and find out what happened.)
You hastily cancel the landing sequence for your autopilot and search for another landing pad.

When you exit your ship you hear the captain of the damaged ship filing a report with the port authority. "No, no. It wasn't pirates!" he exclaims. "It was the ghost ship. The Dire Omen." The government official stops typing on her datapad and gives the captain a skeptical look.
(Ask him where he encountered the ghost ship.)

You shake your head at this superstitious nonsense and go about your business. This is probably some sort of insurance scam and from the expression on the face of the government official, she probably shares this sentiment.
After he is done filing his report you approach the captain and ask, "Where did you last spot this 'ghost ship'?"

"About halfway through the Northern Passage," he responds. "I didn't believe the tales of a haunted war ship. But the legend of the 'Dire Omen' is real! According to my scanner, the ship has no crew."

values: A merchant captain claimed to have been attacked by a ghost ship he referred to as the "Dire Omen". The government official who filed the report seemed skeptical of his testimony.

name: Ghost Hunting: Dire Omen 5
description: Merchants have asked you find their missing escort, the 'Lucky Horse Shoe', which was last seen heading towards Rajak in the northern passage. Supposedly, it was attacked by a ghost ship named 'Dire Omen'. If you manage to rescue it, escort the 'Lucky Horse Shoe' back to <destination>.

values: Merchants have asked you find their missing escort, the 'Lucky Horse Shoe', which was last seen heading towards Rajak in the northern passage. Supposedly, it was attacked by a ghost ship named 'Dire Omen'. If you manage to rescue it, escort the 'Lucky Horse Shoe' back to <destination>.

children.key: As you open your hatch there is a group of merchants waiting for you. "Excuse us captain. We are seeking volunteers for a rescue mission. Will you hear us out?"
(There's no harm in just listening to their request.)
"Sorry, I have my own business to attend to."
"Our convoy was traveling through the northern passage when we were attacked by..." the merchant seems hesitant to continue.
"Pirates! We were attacked by pirates," another merchant interjects.
"No," says the first merchant. "We should speak the truth. You may find this hard to believe. But we were attacked by that ghost ship! The rumors are true!"
"You mentioned something about a rescue earlier..."
"Our escort, the 'Lucky Horse Shoe' was separated from us as we fled. We believe it is still out there. Would you be willing to search for it? We last saw it heading towards Rajak."
"Forget it. I'm not going on a wild ghost chase."
"You really believe that it was a ghost ship?"
"Will you be willing to pay me for my trouble?"
"It was like no other ship I'd ever seen before. And our tactical scanners showed no crew."
"I'm certain the captain of the 'Lucky Horse Shoe' will repay you for your assistance."

values: I've been asked to rescue the lost ship "Lucky Horse Shoe" which was last seen heading towards Rajak. Supposedly, it was escorting a merchant fleet when it was attacked by a ghost ship named "Dire Omen".

children.key: When you enter the system your scanners show the "Lucky Horse Shoe" surrounded by some small pirate ships. Then something else arrives...

values: When you open the hatch you're surprised to be greeted by Cali, the person who sold you info back on Stormhold. "Well, ain't you a sight for sore eyes! Much obliged for your help, captain! I'll make sure to rustle up a reward for you once we get back to port."

After you land, Cali hands over a stack of chips worth <payment>. "You were great out there <first>! Thanks again for savin' my bacon!" At the spaceport bar you tell the tale of your encounter with the ghost ship "Dire Omen". Amongst the crowd listening, a skeptic scoffs. "Ghost ship!?! Surely, you jest!"
The ghost ship "Dire Omen" turned out to be an alien ship with an advanced autopilot system. Like a drone. A very large and deadly drone.
A cowgirl who is also captain of the ship Lucky Horse Shoe.

name: Ghost Hunting: Poltergeist King 1
description: A madman calling himself Poltergeist King is holding three children hostage in Menkalinan. Search for the perpetrator, rescue the children, and return them to <planet> in the <system> system.

values: A madman calling himself Poltergeist King is holding three children hostage in Menkalinan. Search for the perpetrator, rescue the children, and return them to <planet> in the <system> system.
Hint: Some missions only appear when you have enough open bunks/cargo space required for the mission.

children.key: It's just about closing time at the bar and you're the only customer left. The bartender is almost done cleaning up. As he reaches for the power button on the holoprojector the program that was playing is suddenly replaced by a live feed showing some derelict ships floating in space.
A crazed voice suddenly yells out of the speakers.
"Testing! Testing! Hey! Is this thing working!?! Ah, I'm sure they can hear me. Hellooo people of <planet>! Tonight's entertainment is brought to you by the Poltergeist King!"
The image then shifts to a photograph of three children.
"Looky what I've got! If you want to rescue them, come to the Menkalinan system."
The image switches back to the shot of derelict ships.
"As you can see, I've prepared a wonderful series of funhouses for us to play in!"
After a few moments of silence, the bartender looks at you. "What're you gonna do captain?"
If those kids are from this world, they probably have rich parents who'll reward you well. On the other hand, heading out there could get you killed.
"Smells like a trap. I'm not going out there."
It's quiet. Suddenly, the air is filled with static as some speakers crackle on.
You look through several more corridors and empty rooms.
You find a storage room with some cargo containers.
You find the missing kids gagged and tied up inside a cargo container. "I'm here to rescue you!"
(Whip out your trusty pocket laser razor.)
The ropes fall to the floor after you release the children and you all quickly run back to your ship.
(Set the thrusters to full blast and get outta here!)
You manage to launch just as the other ship violently explodes!"

values: You've returned to <planet> but have not rescued the hostages.
Ghost Hunting: Poltergeist King Trick A
Ghost Hunting: Poltergeist King Trick B
Ghost Hunting: Poltergeist King Trick C

Your ship is slightly singed from all the explosions, but the important thing is that the children are safely returned. Their grateful parents give you <payment> to help cover your repairs. Unfortunately, you did not find the Poltergeist King on any of the derelict ships. Back at the bar, you realize that video of your efforts has been posted to the net. The bartender and several patrons treat you to some drinks.

Rescued some children being held aboard an explosive derelict by a madman calling himself the Poltergeist King. The galaxy is a big place and there are some truly sick individuals hiding out amongst the stars.
A madman who uses drones and remote detonated explosive devices. He is not above kidnapping children and threatening to kill them. A genuine sadist who takes delight in the misery of others.

name: Ghost Hunting: Poltergeist King 2
description: A derelict Korath Raider just entered the <system> system. Salvage it before anyone else does, then land on <planet>.

values: A derelict Korath Raider just entered the <system> system. Salvage it before anyone else does, then land on <planet>.

children.key: While walking through the space port you recognize a familiar looking cowgirl studying the sky with a telescope. This time, however, Cali is surrounded by some rough looking men.
You whip out your pistol and order the men to back off slowly. "Cali, are you ok?" you call out.

Cali turns towards you, startled by your sudden outburst. The men look at her. She looks at them. Then they all start laughing at you. As the laughter slowly dies down, she explains, "Thanks for the knight in shinin' armor routine, but this is my crew!"
With a bit of embarrassment, you put away your pistol.
"Hi Cali, see any ghost ships up there?"

"This time, I'm actually lookin' fer aliens." She introduces you to the other guys. "Guys, <first> is the dude who saved our bacon back on Rajak. <first>, this here is the crew of the Lucky Horse Shoe." The guys thank you and introduce themselves, but it's hard to keep track of all their names.

Cali lowers her voice, "A reliable feller spilled the beans to me about some aliens who raid this system from time to time. Sometimes the pirates get into regular 'ol scraps with enforcers from the Syndicate, while a derelict alien ship is left adrift. And you know how the sayin' goes 'bout derelicts..."
"Ain't no one has ownership rights to a derelict 'cept the one who gets to it first," you reply.
The group gets a good chuckle at your performance.
"Hello?" she answers. "What? Begin preflight prep. We're on our way."
"Speak of the devil. Boys, we got a derelict comin' in system! Sorry <first>, but you know how it is. Race you there?"
"I'll sit this one out. Happy hunting!"
"Last one there is a rotten egg!"

You didn't realize it as you watched her and her crew run towards their landing pad. But this would turn out to be the last time you ever saw Cali and her crew. Witnesses would later claim that the orbital explosion was bright enough to be seen from the planet's surface... (MISSION FAILED: If life were a game, maybe you could load a previous save file and try again.)
As Cali and her crew ran towards their landing pad, you were running towards your own.
You board the ship and soon realize that anything of value has already been ripped out. The ship does appear to be outfitted with a Jump Drive, but it is clearly broken.
Before you do anything else, the doors slam shut! The sound of static fills the air as some speakers crackle on. A familiar voice begins to speak...
"Testing. Testing! One, two, three! Ahem, well well well! Lookie who I've caught here! If it isn't my old friend <first> <last>! You DO remember me, don't you!?!
"I, I, I'm the Poltergeist King! How could you forget after all the EXPLOSIVELY fun times we had back in Menkalinan?"

"Today, I was just looking to have some fun! Bait some pirates or Syndicate scumbags into this little fun house and listen to their screams of despair! But this should still be entertaining. This time, the hostage is you!"

"As you can see, there are three wires within this panel. Ready for a special game of Rock, Scissors, Paper? Here are the rules: Per the normal game, Rock beats Scissors, Scissors beats Paper, and Paper beats Rock. I've already Reserved my choice. If you want to Request Rock, cut the Red wire. If you want to Select Scissors, cut the Silver wire. If you want to Pick Paper, cut the Purple wire. I've left a clue in my words. Oh, and if you happen to Request the same choice I Reserved, you also lose. Heh, heh, heh... Three second tiii-merrr!"
A clue is in his words. Request Rock with Red. Select Scissors with Silver. Pick Paper with Purple.
He already Reserved his choice. You lose if you make the same Request.
Could Picking it really be so simple? You're dealing with a madman, after all.
(Cut the Red wire to Request Rock.)
(Cut the Silver wire to Select Scissors.)
(Cut the Purple wire to Pick Paper.)
The doors remain shut. A surveillance drone floating outside a nearby viewport captures your final moments as the ship explodes and you die in the ensuing fireball.
The doors slide open, clearing a path for you to board your ship. You can hear the voice of the Poltergeist King laughing behind you as an explosion in the distance rocks the derelict.

values: The derelict ship is still in orbit waiting for someone to claim it!

children.key: Back at the space port you find Cali. "Thank goodness you're OK! I saw the whole thang! Someone posted a video of it to the net." She shows you a portion of the video on a portable holo projector. "That's an interestin' haul you got there," she says, pausing the video to point at the broken jump drive. "I reckon you could try to pass it off to a gallery or a collector as some kind of modern art," she shrugs.

values: The Poltergeist King struck again. This time he tried to lure in pirate or Syndicate salvagers with a rigged alien ship. I managed to escape his trap, but the only thing I was able to salvage was a broken jump drive.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Ghost Hunting: Poltergeist King 2

name: Ghost Hunting: Zubenelgenubi Ghost Ship
description: An alien ghost ship is projected to pass through the Zubenelgenubi system. Head over there if you want to investigate. Return to <planet> afterwards and tell Cali what you found.

values: An alien ghost ship is projected to pass through the Zubenelgenubi system. Head over there if you want to investigate. Return to <planet> afterwards and tell Cali what you found.

children.key: When you enter the bar a familiar voice calls out your name. "Howdy <first>! Don't be a stranger! Pull up a chair!" Cali waves you over to where she and her crew are seated. "How have you been since that incident with the exploding derelict?"
You update her on the adventures you've had.
"So, have you heard about the ghost ship headed for Zubenelgenubi?" she asks."

"It sure seems like it. As the story goes, it coasted through Beta Lupi three hundred years ago. Calculations of its course headin' project it's path'll cross Zubenelgenubi real soon. Back in Beta Lupi the durn thang was broadcasting somethin' weird. Might've been a message, but ain't no one figured out what they were tryin' to say. Folks nick-named it the Revenant and the name stuck."
"Are you going to check it out?"
"Well, I'm gonna pass on this one. After that last exploding derelict, I reckon I'd best stick to regular jobs for a spell. If you do check it out, mosey on back here and tell me all about it!"

While you haven't seen this ship before, the derelict you've found strongly resembles a Coalition design. Perhaps it spent hundreds or even thousands of years floating through the empty void to get here. Unfortunately, it did not make the journey unscathed. A tiny asteroid has wedged itself into the hull.

You've seen this type of ship before. The derelict you've found is a rare Coalition design. Perhaps it spent hundreds or even thousands of years floating through the empty void to get here. Unfortunately, it did not make the journey unscathed. A tiny asteroid has wedged itself into the hull.
Also, it looks like you weren't the first one to find this derelict.
Hints of the scent of rotting flesh are mixed in with the otherwise stale air. The ships' internal lights unsteadily flicker on and off. Life support is functional, but erratic.

The next room shows signs of a struggle. Blood is splattered on the floor and there are energy burns on the walls. The rotting corpse of a Saryd lies on the floor. While the smell of burnt ozone is fresh, the corpse looks to have been dead for a very long time. It's head has a large hole burned through it.
In the next room you find a set of bloody boot prints leading towards the door on the right. Suddenly, you hear a loud "clunk" from the door on the left.
(Investigate the door with the bloody footprints.)
(Investigate the door where you heard the strange noise come from.)

You hear another "clunk" come from the door on the left. This time, the sound is louder. When you push the button to open the door, a rotting hand jerks out from the other side and grabs you with inhuman strength! It quickly pulls you through the gap in the open doorway. The door slams shut as your screams fill the air. The sound of your bones crunching and snapping can be heard from the other side of the door before all becomes quiet again. Moments later, the sound of a loud "clunk" comes from the door you were pulled through...

The footprints stop at the door. Whoever made them must have stepped through. You push the button to open the door and quickly step away from it. An burst of laser fire flies through, narrowly missing you!
You pull out your gun and start shooting back! Suddenly, a woman's voice calls out "Hey! Cease fire! Cease fire!"

As the smoke clears, you find a woman on the other side of the door. She's dressed in a black clothing you'd expect a spy or thief to wear on a stealth mission, her face partially hidden under a hood. She hasn't put her laser rifle away. "Have you seen them? The ship is infested with... with zombies! Zombie centaurs!"
You can't help but look at her incredulously. You've seen a lot during your travels across the galaxy. But zombies? Maybe she's the type to watch horror movies.

As you're about to speak you are interrupted by another loud "clunk" from the door behind you. Suddenly, the door bursts open and the rotting corpse of a Saryd pushes it's way through! A piece of shrapnel from the broken door knocks you against the wall and you are momentarily too stunned to aim your gun at the rampaging creature. The mystery woman shoots the undead Saryd in the head until it falls to the floor.
She stares at the corpse lying still on the ground and mutters, "Like I said: zombie centaurs."
You nod your head, still in disbelief despite what you've just witnessed.

The woman activates a communication device. "Necromanteion, this is Greythatch. Come in for pickup." She turns to you and says, "I'm leaving. If you're smart, you will too. My boarding crew is already dead and I'm not about to risk the few I have remaining to pilot my ship." She runs off without waiting for a reply. As you watch her go, you notice she's wearing a small backpack that isn't empty. Whatever she looted was probably not worth the lives of her dead crew members.
Before you make up your mind on what to do next, the lights in the hall beyond the door stop flickering and stabilize, beckoning you to enter.
(Maybe you should give up on this one.)
When you got your pilot license, you weren't planning to star in a zombie movie. You ignore the lighted hallway and go back to your ship.

As you traverse the empty hallways, the lights ahead of you stabilize while the lights behind you fade to darkness. You are certain that someone or something is deliberately leading you through the ship. Occasionally you find the corpse of a dead Saryd or a dead human you assume to be part of Greythatch's crew. Sometimes you hear the sound of a loud "clunk" from the other side of a door you pass. Always, the lights ahead beckon you on while the lights over head start to fade if you remain idle for too long.

Eventually, you reach what appears to be the ship's command bridge. A control panel lights up, waiting for you to approach it. Words in a language you do not recognize dance across a view screen. Then you notice that some of the characters are being replaced by letters from your own language. Soon, whole words begin to form...
CREW INFECTION BY UNKNOWN VIRUS OF ALIEN ORIGIN = 100%.
You're not sure which buttons to press. Perhaps the interface is a touch screen. Only one way to find out...
( C O M P L Y )
( R E J E C T )

Suddenly, the lights turn red and a countdown timer appears on the view screen. The words "MISSION FAILURE" repeatedly flash on the screen. It must not have liked your answer. Unfortunately, the path to get back to your ship is a long one and there isn't enough time to escape. You watch helplessly as the seconds count down...

The lights completely stabilize and a map of the ship is displayed on the view screen. Areas occupied by the zombie crew are highlighted. With the lights restored and the ship's computer supported tactical information at your disposal, you expect you should be able to clear out what remains of the zombie crew and take the ship. From the message you read earlier, this must have been a warship from the era of the Coalition's rebellion against the Quarg. It might be a good idea to replace the ship's computer with a less genocidal one. As for the zombie virus, you hope you weren't infected and make plans to sterilize the ship once you get back to port...

values: Salvaged an old Saryd warship from the era of the Coalition's rebellion against the Quarg. After a tiny asteroid crashed into the ship, some sort of alien virus it contained had infected the crew and turned them into zombies. Fortunately, the virus doesn't seem to infect humans and I was able to sterilize the ship.

You find Cali in the spaceport after you land. She listens to your story about your run in with a zombie infested ship and gives you an incredulous look. "<first>, I reckon you might've watched a few too many horror movies for yer own good."

name: Ghost Hunting: Friendship 1

children.key: As you are leaving the spaceport, some kids approach you. The oldest one asks, "Excuse me, but are you a starship captain?"
"Yes, I am. What business do you kids have with a starship captain?"
"Beat it kid, I have work to do."
"It's a drone that the Republic was forced to abandon during the war. Once the war was over, instead of taking it back, they left it to guard the system from pirates."
"How nice of them. So what does it have to do with me?"
"It stopped broadcasting updates a week ago. Someone needs to go check up on it!" exclaims one of the younger kids.
"Hold it. You keep track of the drone's updates?" you ask.
"All the true fans of Friendship 1 do!" another kid speaks up.
"OK, I'll keep an eye out for it when I leave the system."
"Forget it. That drone is a weapon of war. If it's malfunctioning, it might attack me."
"That's what all the starship captains say!" whines the kid who first spoke with you."

"WAH! Starship captains are big meanies!" cries out the youngest child. Soon several other people are looking at you disapprovingly as several of the kids start weeping. You quickly retreat to your ship and leave before their parents can show up to complain.
"Yay, thank you so much captain!" The kids are elated by your proclamation. It's enough to make you almost wonder if you should settle down somewhere and have kids of your own. Almost.

values: You managed to get the drone operational again. When you close the maintenance hatch it transmits a series of chirps and beeps to you. If you didn't know better, you'd think it was thanking you.

Repaired Friendship 1, a Republic drone that was abandoned during the war. Instead of taking it back after the war was over, it was left to guard the system from pirates. It seems the local kids are fans of it. Perhaps they regard it as a symbol of hope for galactic peace.

name: Grudge Fight 1
description: Head as quickly as you can to the Hintar system, where you will duel with a small Navy vessel named the Majestic. After fighting, go to <destination> to follow up.

values: Head as quickly as you can to the Hintar system, where you will duel with a small Navy vessel named the Majestic. After fighting, go to <destination> to follow up.

children.key: While you are walking around the spaceport, you notice a woman in rugged clothing looking intently at you. "Oh, I'm sorry," she responds in a apologetic voice. After a moment of hesitation, she asks, "Are you Captain <last>?"
"I don't know who you're talking about."
The woman's expression changes to one of slight disappointment. "Oh. My mistake. Sorry for bothering you." She walks away without another word.

"It's my job to know things." She looks around then leans in to whisper in your ear, "I am a recruiter for Navy Intelligence and I believe that, after reviewing your record, you would be a great candidate to join our team. However, there is a test you must pass. I will use one of our smaller ships in our fleet, the Majestic, to challenge you to a duel in the system of Hintar. If you manage to disable me, go to our office on <planet>, and we'll let you join."
"What sort of vessel is the Majestic?"
"I don't feel comfortable fighting a woman."
She grabs you by the collar. "Don't worry. I promise not to go easy on you." From the expression on her face when she lets go, you can tell you've hit a nerve.
She leans in to whisper her answer, "Just an old Quicksilver I use for undercover work. I'm sure you'll be up to the challenge."

She steps back and says, "Well, I better be going now. Meet me at the designated location as fast as you can if you want to take on the test." The woman starts to walk away, then turns back. "I suppose I should let you know that the number of available positions is limited. Don't make me wait too long." She then continues on her way.
(Ready your ship for the battle with the Majestic.)

values: When you take off, you see no sign of the Majestic. It's probably already waiting for you at Hintar.

children.key: When you enter Hintar, you continue to see no sign of the Majestic. Suddenly, an alarm rings out as your sensors detect that a heavily modified Hauler named "Mockingbird" is rapidly approaching. Before you can respond, your ship intercepts a hail, and it opens communication.

A voice you recognize as the "Navy Intelligence recruiter" booms out. "Ha ha ha! What a fool! Why would Navy Intelligence recruit someone like you? Ha ha ha!" The Mockingbird targets you with its weapons. "Try not to bore me. My last mark died too quickly..."

You enter Hintar, but see no sign of the Majestic. The "Navy Intelligence recruiter" must have lied about that too. You should visit <planet> to see if you can claim some sort of reward for your fight with the Mockingbird.

You enter Hintar, but see no sign of the Majestic. The "Navy Intelligence recruiter" must have lied about that too. You should revisit the system where you left the Mockingbird to make sure it has been fully destroyed.

As you enter Hintar, the Mockingbird follows behind you, and opens a hail. "Did you think that if you went to Hintar, I would let you off the hook? Ha! Now give me a real fight! Struggle desperately for your pathetic miserable life!" The Mockingbird once again targets you with its weapons. This seems extreme for a recruitment test. At this point it's clear she was serious about not being a recruiter.

values: The Mockingbird hails you. A familiar voice says, "Looks like you've got the right stuff for Navy Intelligence. Too bad, I'm not actually a recruiter." The Mockingbird targets you with its weapons. "Try not to bore me. My last mark died too quickly..."
The Mockingbird has been destroyed. You consider visiting <planet> to see if you can grab some sort of reward for your effort.
Was lured into a trap by Carrie Grudge. With some effort I managed to overcome the disadvantage in our fight. Managed to collect a sizable bounty for my trouble.

children.key: A woman in a business suit approaches you. "Excuse me, but you're Captain <last>, aren't you?"

I saw the <ship> in the port registry and knew that you would be around here. You may not realize it, but you've been developing quite the reputation as a combat pilot. Which brings me to my point. I'm looking for an able pilot to test a new prototype ship we've developed. All you have to do is go to the testing area and fight the ship until it's disabled. "Sure, I'm always interested in new ship models."

children.key: When you return to your ship, you notice a charmingly pleasant older lady waiting for you.
"Pardon me, are you the captain of this ship? I am looking for transportation to <planet>."
"I can take you there for 2,000 credits."
"Sorry lady, I'm not headed in that direction."
"Thank you," she says. "My name is Mara Grundy. What is your name?"
Not long after launch, Mara enters the cockpit with a bowl of soup. "Are you hungry?" she asks. "I've prepared a bowl of soup for you."
"I brought all the utensils and ingredients in my luggage. A proper lady is always ready to whip up a meal."

You look at the bowl of soup incredulously. It definitely looks and smells fresh. Certainly not like the canned slop you keep in storage. "If the ship gets scanned right now, we could get in trouble for carrying undeclared produce..."
"Better eat the evidence then..." she holds the soup out to you.
You carefully take the bowl of soup and sample a sip. It's not bad. Soon you've slurped down the entire bowl. Mara watches you with a satisfied look on her face.
"Did you enjoy your final meal?" she asks.
Something seems wrong about that question. Before you can reply you notice your vision becoming blurry and feel light headed. Soon the room is spinning and you slump from your seat to the floor.

"My trade name is Mama Grudge. This is payback for killing my family." You have a vague sense of being dragged somewhere on the floor. Suddenly, you hear a warning alarm. You must be in the air lock. The hatch is opening. You realize that she's jettisoning you out into space...
You dump the soup out into space.
"My goodness," she gasps. "In my day we didn't waste food." She retreats to her bunk area.
Shaking your head, you settle in for the long flight...

Mara seemed upset when you dumped the soup out into space. She's been quiet since then and you realize that maybe you did over react. When you check on her, she appears to be fast asleep. Perhaps this would be a good time to set the ship on auto pilot and get some shut-eye yourself.
You set the ship to auto pilot and settle in for a quick nap in the pilot's seat. If any pirates come along, the alarm should wake you.

You are startled awake by an intense pain in your head. You open your eyes to see Mara standing next to you with a strange device in her hand! She presses a button and the pain in your head intensifies! You try to move but your body stumbles and you collapse onto the floor.

"My trade name is Mama Grudge. This is payback for killing my family." You have a vague sense of being dragged somewhere on the floor. Suddenly, you hear a warning alarm. You must be in the air lock. The hatch is opening. You realize that she's jettisoning you out into space...
Even though a nap is tempting, you decide to remain awake.

Mara seemed upset when you dumped the soup out into space. She's been quiet since then and you realize that maybe you did over react. When you check on her, she appears to be fast asleep. Perhaps this would be a good time to set the ship on auto pilot and get some shut-eye.
You set the ship to auto pilot and settle in for a quick nap in the pilot's seat. If any pirates come along, the alarm should wake you.
You are startled awake by the sound of soft giggling. Mara is standing next to you. A can of some sort of chemical is in her hand. Gas is spraying out of it.
"My trade name is Mama Grudge. This is payback for killing my family." She drops the can onto the floor. "Nerve gas," she says. "Soon, I'll get to see my family again."
Both of you quickly succumb to the gas and die in agony.
Even though a nap is tempting, you decide to remain awake.

Mara seemed upset when you dumped the soup out into space. She's been quiet since then and you realize that maybe you did over react. When you check on her, she appears to be fast asleep. Perhaps this would be a good time to set the ship on auto pilot and get some shut-eye.
You set the ship to auto pilot and settle in for a quick nap in the pilot's seat. If any pirates come along, the alarm should wake you.

You are startled awake by a loud explosion. You open your eyes to see Mara standing next to you with what appears to be a remote detonator in her hand! You try to move but your hands and feet are bound together in thick coils of duct tape!

"My trade name is Mama Grudge. This is payback for killing my family." According to the ship status readouts, half the hull is gone and the rest is rapidly disintegrating. Mara laughs maniacally. "Soon, I'll get to see my family again!" The cockpit collapses and you are engulfed in a scorching fireball.
Even though a nap is tempting, you decide to remain awake.

You set the ship to auto pilot and settle in for a quick nap in the pilot's seat. If any pirates come along, the alarm should wake you.

You are startled awake by a sharp pain in your ear. You open your eyes to see Mara standing next to you with a jar full of some strange worm-like creatures in her hand! Warm blood is gushing out of your ear and your head is throbbing in pain. You try to move but your body stumbles and you collapse onto the floor.

"My trade name is Mama Grudge. This is payback for killing my family." She jiggles the jar of creatures in front of your face. "Almachian Brain Maggots. I'm told that death from these is slow and painful." Soon the pain overwhelms you...
Even though a nap is tempting, you decide to remain awake.
Soon after entering the system, Mara visits you in the cockpit.
"So many new starships these days," she comments on the other ships landing and taking off. Gripping your right shoulder while pointing to your left, she asks, "What kind of ship is that?"

You feel her let go of your shoulder as you try to figure out which ship she's pointing to. But from the angle of her finger, it doesn't look like she's pointing at any ship in particular. Suddenly, you feel a sharp pain in your back! Then another! And another! You slump to the floor and see her standing over you grinning with a bloody knife in her hands.
"My trade name is Mama Grudge. This is payback for killing my family." She drags you away from the cockpit and leaves you to bleed out on the floor while she takes control of your ship...
"We'll be landing soon." You turn towards her. "I need you to get out of the cockpit so that I can focus on getting us safely to the ground."
"Well!" Mara says in indignation. "You are the rudest starship captain I have ever had the displeasure of traveling with." She leaves in a huff.
You shake your head and begin preparations to land.

values: Had a near death experience transporting a dangerous criminal aboard my ship. I had no idea my life was on the line as Mama Grudge rigged my ship with a variety of death traps. Fortunately, the port authority managed to catch her and clear the ship of these hazards.

children.key: Mara pays you the agreed upon payment of <payment> and disembarks from your ship without a word. All her charm at the beginning of the journey has mysteriously disappeared.
As she is walking away from your ship a squad of spaceport security officers swarm around her and place her in handcuffs! One of the officers approaches you.

"Captain <first> <last>?" he asks. You nod an affirmative. "Were you aware that you were transporting a dangerous fugitive?" You shake your head to disavow. "Well," he says, "given your past history with the Grudge crime family, I suppose we can overlook this. That woman is Mama Grudge. I'm still going to have to ask you to submit your ship for inspection. Trust me, it's for your own safety."

The inspection takes hours. Somehow, Mama Grudge left bombs, alien parasites, nerve gas, and various other traps aboard your ship. The spaceport security team assures you that the ship has been cleared of all the traps and should be safe to fly again. You hope they didn't miss anything...

children.key: While relaxing at the bar, a waiter delivers a fresh bowl of soup to you.
The waiter shrugs before muttering, "Compliments of the chef." It has a pleasant, yet familiar odor...
The waiter answers, "She's a sweet old lady we just hired. She definitely knows her way around a kitchen!"
The waiter responds, "I don't know her real name, but everyone here calls her 'Mama G.'"
Somehow, you get the feeling that eating this soup would be hazardous to your health. The waiter looks at you with concern. "What's wrong? Are you okay?".
You toss enough credits on the table to cover your bill and leave.
You carefully take the bowl of soup and sample a sip. It's not bad. Soon you've slurped down the entire bowl.
You suddenly realize that the waiter left while you were eating and the person standing next to you is someone else. It's an old woman dressed as a chef. You quickly recognize who she is.
But the words never leave your throat. Having lost control of your muscles, your body slumps to the floor. "Oh no sweetie! Looks like you've had too much to drink."
As she drags you to the kitchen, you hear one of the other patrons gasp "Isn't that Mama Grudge? Did she escape from prison?"

But she quickly has you through the kitchen door, away from the crowd. "I thought about you every day since we last met. I couldn't believe my luck when I noticed you had walked into this bar!" Alone with this mad woman and unable to move, you hear the sound of metal being sharpened. "Fresh ingredients are important for operating a restaurant on a space station." She whispers in your ear with glee. Mama Grudge then proceeded to carve you up for her next recipe...

children.key: The instructions given to you at the job office lead you to a run down farm house far from the space port. There is a simple fence with an unlocked gate surrounding the perimeter.
After checking both the fence and gate, you find no traps.

With no other entrance in sight, you enter through the gate. You hear a loud squawk and notice some chickens wandering about within the fenced enclosure. The door to the house is just a few steps away.
You ignore the front entrance and search the other side of the house for a rear entrance. You easily find one.
After checking the knob, you are surprised to find that the door is unlocked.
Searching the edges of the door, you find no traps.
You kick in the door with your pistol drawn and yell out "This is a raid! Nobody move!"

The house is quiet and empty. After searching the rooms, you find an old woman dozing off on a couch. There are no computers or networking equipment in the building. She starts to wake up from all the noise you've been making.
After a moment she realizes that she isn't alone and focuses her attention on you. "Hey there youngun'. It's been a spell since I've had a visitor. Would you like some tea?"
After conversing with her for a while, it doesn't take long for you to realize that you were fed false information.

values: Took on a job to locate the Hackerz. False information lead me to an old lady living alone in a dilapidated farm house instead.

The last time you tried, you were lured onto an exploding Bactrian...
Your information has lead you to an abandoned warehouse. There don't appear to be any guards or traps. Carefully, you make your way inside the building.
You'd just finished searching the third room when someone kicks in the door down the hall!
"Filthy Hackerz!" Screams an angry man with a shotgun. "The bounty isn't enough to pay me back all the money you stole!"
The angry man sees you and opens fire!
You hold your hands up and try to reason with him. But he is too crazed to have a discussion with. You are hit by a shotgun slug and your headless corpse falls to the floor.

You narrowly avoid a shotgun slug and jump out the nearest window. Fortunately, the window was already broken, but you still get some minor scrapes from the few shards of glass remaining in the frame. "Better than a shotgun slug to the head," you exclaim to yourself as you run for your ship.
The angry bounty hunter is still pursuing you in his Headhunter.

If I hadn't been interrupted, the abandoned warehouse I was searching would've probably turned out to become another dud. I'm starting to suspect that the job board system itself has been hacked and all of the jobs for tracing the Hackerz are another one of their sick jokes.

children.key: Hope is an uninhabited frozen wasteland. You know this is probably a trap...
But you've chosen to go anyway.

According to the job posting, the Hackerz are operating out of the abandoned "Subsi Land" amusement park. It's supposed to be buried beneath a ton of ice and snow, but someone must have recently excavated it. A statue of Subsi, the park's mascot character, stands at the entrance, its faded colors almost resembling an actual Subsidurial. The park's rides and attractions are covered in rust, the result from years of being encased in frozen water.
Suddenly, loud carnival music starts playing and the machines begin reactivating. The Hackerz seem to be rolling out a welcome for you.
The nearest ride is a small rail car that goes into a tunnel. Take a seat?

As you take a seat, a safety bar secures you in place and the car slowly moves into the tunnel. It's dark at first, but then the tunnel lights up, revealing a variety of colorful Subsidurial shaped robots singing a happy song.

A robotic Subsi outfitted with a gatling gun pops up and sprays the rail car with gun fire! The Subsidurial shaped robots continue singing their happy song as the damaged rail car carries your bloody corpse out of the chamber.

You duck just in time as a robotic Subsi outfitted with a gatling gun sprays the rail car with gun fire! The safety bar shakes loose and you are able to flee the amusement ride once the damaged rail car exits the chamber.
The theater seems to be showing the "Subsi and Friends Music Show". Check it out?
You take a seat in the theater and the lights fade out. Once it's dark, the stage lights up and the curtain pulls back to reveal several Subsidurial shaped robots singing a happy song.

A robotic Subsi outfitted with a gatling gun pops up and sprays the theater with gun fire! The Subsidurial shaped robots continue singing their happy song as your bloody corpse slumps onto the theater floor.
You duck just in time as a robotic Subsi outfitted with a gatling gun sprays the theater with gun fire! Eventually it runs out of bullets and you are able to escape the theater.
The gift shop has "Subsi and Friends" merchandise on display. Go inside?
The inside of the store is in much better condition than the outside. The Subsidurial plushies even look good as new. As you walk near a display, a giant Subsi robot pops out of a nearby wall panel.

A hidden gatling gun extends from the robot's mouth and sprays the gift shop with gun fire! Eventually it stops firing and the robot retracts back into the wall. The lifeless eyes of the Subsidurial plushies silently watch over your bloody corpse.

You duck behind some cover as a hidden gatling gun extends from the robot's mouth and sprays the gift shop with gun fire! Eventually it stops firing and the robot retracts back into the wall, allowing you to escape the gift shop.

As you run, several more Subsidurial shaped robots armed with gatling guns appear and open fire. By now, it's obvious that the whole amusement park is rigged with these robots. Once you are safely aboard your ship, you fire up the engines and begin to lift off. As you clear the atmosphere, the warning alarms start blaring. A swarm of drones is headed for you.
The hostile drones are still targeting you.
