children.key: Huginn Station is a high security prison. With your previous experiences tracking down the Hackerz, this is almost certain to be a trap...
But you've chosen to go anyway.

No one greets you at the air lock and the <planet> port authority isn't responding to your hails. The security station is abandoned, allowing you access to restricted areas of the station. It could be a problem if security catches you inside armed with anything more significant than your side arm.

You head for the station's command center to get answers. Along the way, you notice blood stains on the floors and walls. Something is definitely wrong here. When you finally arrive, the area is deserted. The communications equipment is damaged, allowing incoming transmissions to be received, but none to be sent. As you take all this in, someone hails the station: "Attention escaped prisoners and their allies. The Republic will not tolerate a prison break of this magnitude. You have all been sentenced to death."

Allies? Could the Navy be referring to you? Looking around the blood splattered consoles, you realize it may not be a good idea to be here when they arrive. Getting back to your ship and fleeing the station may be your only shot at survival.

You head for the prison cells to make sure the convicts are still locked away. The blood stains in the hallways aren't a good sign. When you look into the first prison cell, you find the dead bodies of uniformed prison guards.
"You! You're responsible for this!" A man enters the cell block with a rifle pointed at you. It appears to be another bounty hunter. "I finally caught the Hackerz mastermind. Must be my lucky day!"
"I'm not going to let you frame me for this."
"Just what I'd expect from the Hackerz mastermind!" The man charges at you. What do you do?

He raises the rifle overhead to try and knock you out, but you quickly step in with a series of punches that knock him off balance. As he falls, you leap in and pummel him into submission. Rather than haul him around the station, it is probably safer to keep him locked up in one of the empty cells.
You decide to go for the kill. As you draw your weapon, the man levels the muzzle of his rifle to aim for your chest.
He pulls the trigger first, blasting a hole into your chest. "Damn," he exclaims. "I wonder if I can still get the reward." Those would be the last words you hear before you die.
You pull the trigger first and put him down. As you stand over the dead man, you wonder if this situation can still be salvaged with the station authorities.

He raises the rifle overhead and knocks you out. You awaken some time later locked in a prison cell. Apparently, you've been found guilty of hacking into the prison security system and orchestrating this prison break. Due to the especially violent and gruesome nature of this particular prison break, you've been sentenced to death. The execution is set to take place immediately.
For some reason, you've decided to check out the cargo bay. With the security station abandoned, perhaps you'll be able to help yourself to some unattended cargo...
(Time to pick up some sweet loot!)
When you return, your airlock is overrun by hundreds of rioting prisoners armed with weapons stolen from the station's armory! You are killed as the <ship> is quickly overtaken.

values: The Hackerz set up a trap at Huginn Station, a high security station. They remotely unlocked all the prison cells, which resulted in a violent riot. To make matters worse, I was suspected of aiding the prisoners due to my presence on the station while the riot was in progress.

While the Free Worlds appreciates the offer, I just wanted to make sure this wasn't a miscommunication or some sort of hacking fraud." You don't recall making an offer to relinquish the tribute on Bourne...
Shortly after, you receive a message of gratitude from the Free Worlds.
After completing launch preparations you get a message, but the data inside is corrupted...

Your search for the Hackerz has brought you to New America. It continues to be sparsely populated by anarchists who value their privacy. While exploring one of the abandoned ghost towns, you notice a Surveillance Drone observing you.
The drone responds with a series of beeps and chirps.

The drone must have been rigged with a bomb. It explodes more violently than you expected a normal Surveillance Drone to, engulfing you in the blast despite maintaining what should have been a safe distance.
Remaining on the surface could be dangerous. You retreat to the safety of the <ship> and fire up the engines.
You find no refuge on the surface. The automated ships are still a threat.

values: The Hackerz set up an ambush at New America, an isolated anarchist world. In addition to drones, a fleet of automated Test Dummy ships was arrayed against me.
You've survived the automated ship assault...

children.key: You are approached by a pair of merchant captains, a man and woman. The woman says, "I'm sorry to ask this, but could you escort us to <destination> by <date>? We are carrying medical supplies to help victims of a recent disaster there. We can pay you <payment>, a fair share of the delivery fee." They seem sincere, but you can't help but notice that they already have a couple of heavy warships.
"Seems like you already have some tough ships."
The man responds "That may be true, but for the safety of my sister I'd prefer some additional security, especially with pirates lurking in some of the systems we'll be traveling through."
"Thanks!, By the way, I'm Hansel and she's Gretel," the man introduces himself and his sister.
"I hope we have a safe journey," adds Gretel.
Hansel & Gretel: Medical Supply Escort 1: defered

values: A pair of siblings piloting some Syndicate heavy warships named after themselves. They often take jobs delivering medical supplies to frontier worlds.

description: Use an Asteroid Scanner to search <waypoints> for buried treasures. (The treasures will be there even after completing/aborting this mission)

children.key: An old pirate who reeks of rum approaches you. "Would you be interested in purchasing a treasure map for 1,000,000 credits?"
This seems like a dubious offer, but then again it could be real. Do you buy the map?

You exchange your credits for "the map", which includes an Asteroid Scanner frequency. The seller explains, "Travel to <waypoints> and use this frequency to scan the asteroids. You'd never find them without this."
The seller nods before walking away. It isn't clear how many of those asteroids have treasures in them, but finding them could keep you busy for a long time...

values: Purchased a treasure map for the Archipelago system.
There is someone else mining the asteroids. Perhaps you're not the only one who bought a treasure map.

children.key: You find Barmy Edwards resting on a bench outside one of Kraz Cybernetics hangar bays. He looks worn out.

"Hi <first>. This new ship was a beast to work on. I can already tell that it'll require more crew than they were expecting just to handle weapon maintenance." He stands up and stretches. "Well, since you're here, I guess it's time to see what it can do. As usual, we just want you to disable the Vindicator, not destroy it. Understood?"
"Of course. So, what kind of ship is it?"
"Of course. Is it in this hangar?"
He smirks. "I don't want to spoil the surprise. We can talk about it once the test is over and we're back on the ground. Let's go!"

name: SB-Labs Vindicator 3
description: Escort the SB-Labs Vindicator to <destination>.

children.key: You meet Barmy Edward overseeing repairs at the hangar. The Vindicator towers over you. What looked like a massive cannon from a distance is, in actuality, a cluster of what appear to be several modified plasma cannons crammed together into a single firing module.

"It's your fault, you know." Barmy notices you eyeing the cannons. "From what I've been told, the entire forward section was originally supposed to be a fighter bay. But then you discovered that alien ship out past the edges of The Rim. Of course, word got out about the alien ship with the giant super gun mounted on it. After that, the Southbound Shipyard engineers became obsessed with putting together this monstrosity. They couldn't replicate the spinal mount of your Emerald Sword, so they improvised this concentrated firing mount instead."
"What if one of the guns needs to be replaced?"

"As I mentioned before, the maintenance on these weapons requires extra effort. Any gun not on the edge of the firing cluster can't be reached without first removing the other guns surrounding it. The Southbound Shipyards team thought they could get away with the same crew size as a Dreadnought. I'm recommending they increase that by about ten percent."

"Oh, definitely. That's to be expected from cramming so many guns together in an a tightly enclosed space. Remember how I said that there was supposed to be a fighter bay where the concentrated firing mount is located? That giant cage surrounding the entrance was put there to extend the ship's shields around that area for the purpose of giving fighters additional cover during take off and landing. As you can see, they've bolted the cage to the firing cluster to try using it as a heat sink. It's not very effective..."

"Well, Southbound Shipyards hasn't even approved this design for mass production. My contact over there tells me that there's been some pushback since the original request was for a carrier, not a destroyer. They're hoping to use the results of this test to convince upper management to make an approval."

One of the technicians hands Barmy a status report. After taking a look through it, Barmy says, "We're supposed to bring the ship back to <destination> as soon as repairs are done. Want to come along? We could use the escort."

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::SB-Labs Vindicator 3

name: SB-Labs Vindicator 4
description: Oathbreakers have started a siege in the <system> system. Escape the siege, then return Barmy Edwards to <destination>.

values: Oathbreakers have started a siege in the <system> system. Escape the siege, then return Barmy Edwards to <destination>.
An engineer who works at Southbound Shipyards R&D.

children.key: As you disembark, you see Barmy talking to a man wearing a Southbound Shipyards engineering uniform.
Barmy waves you over. "Captain <last>, this is Ricardo Astillero from Southbound Shipyards R&D. He was just telling me the bad news."
"Wait, THE Captain <last>? The war hero?" Ricardo expresses his surprise.
"The one and only. So what's this bad news?"
"Nevermind that. What's this about bad news?"
"Upper management has decided to cancel the Vindicator project. They aren't even interested in seeing Barmy's test results."
"If that's true, then do they plan on scrapping the ship?" asks Barmy.
"They are. But maybe Captain <last> can help."
Ricardo has a grim look on his face. "Take the ship and leave. I'll tell them I tricked you into taking it for more testing. Please, we worked so hard on this..."
Barmy turns to you. "Even so, there might still be some repurcussions to your reputation. It's your choice, captain."
"Alright, it's a big risk, but I'll take it."
"Sorry, no. I'm not willing to take this much risk for someone I just met."
"I understand. Sorry for asking something so foolish." Ricardo looks dejected. "Excuse me. I have some things I need to do."
"I think I'll stay here for a while." Barmy says bitterly. "I probably can't do much to change their minds, but I'd still like to try."
"Thank you, captain!" Ricardo's eyes fill with hope. "You'd better get going. The sooner you get the Vindicator away from here, the better."
"I'd better come with you." Barmy says. "There might be some difficult questions to answer if I stick around. Besides, I need a lift home."

A squad of Militia ships are launching from the planet. But they're not after you. Instead, they're targeting a large pirate fleet that just entered the system! It looks like the pirates are starting a siege. Time for the Vindicator to prove its worth!

values: Some pirate ships seem to be following you. They must be planning to capture the Vindicator. You can either destroy them or try to shake off their pursuit!

After a series of adventures, I am now the lawful owner of Southbound Shipyards prototype Vindicator heavy warship. While the concentrated firing mount is an interesting concept, I hope to one day find a gun that truly displays the potential of this ship.

children.key: Barmy Edwards thanks you for safely returning him home. You receive a few messages when you land. The timing of the pirate attack couldn't have been more fortunate. Ricardo managed to convince everyone that you had taken the Vindicator in order to distract the pirates. Luring away a significant portion of their fleet may have turned the tide of battle in favor of the defenders. Zug is even rewarding you with <payment> for your contribution to the planetary defense. Southbound Shipyards has decided to let you keep the Vindicator to avoid any public backlash for antagonizing the new hero of Zug.

description: Escort the SB-Labs Liberator to <destination>.

children.key: You meet Barmy Edward overseeing repairs at the hangar. The Liberator towers over you. What looked like a massive cannon from a distance is, in actuality, a cluster of what appear to be several modified plasma cannons crammed together into a single firing module.

"It's your fault, you know." Barmy notices you eyeing the cannons. "From what I've been told, the entire forward section was originally supposed to be a fighter bay. But then you discovered that alien ship out past the edges of The Rim. Of course, word got out about the alien ship with the giant super gun mounted on it. After that, the Southbound Shipyard engineers became obsessed with putting together this monstrosity. They couldn't replicate the spinal mount of your Emerald Sword, so they improvised this concentrated firing mount instead."
"What if one of the guns needs to be replaced?"

"As I mentioned before, the maintenance on these weapons requires extra effort. Any gun not on the edge of the firing cluster can't be reached without first removing the other guns surrounding it. The Southbound Shipyards team thought they could get away with the same crew size as a Dreadnought. I'm recommending they increase that by about ten percent."

"Oh, definitely. That's to be expected from cramming so many guns together in an a tightly enclosed space. Remember how I said that there was supposed to be a fighter bay where the concentrated firing mount is located? That giant cage surrounding the entrance was put there to extend the ship's shields around that area for the purpose of giving fighters additional cover during take off and landing. As you can see, they've bolted the cage to the firing cluster to try using it as a heat sink. It's not very effective..."

"Well, Southbound Shipyards hasn't even approved this design for mass production. My contact over there tells me that there's been some pushback since the original request was for a carrier, not a destroyer. They're hoping to use the results of this test to convince upper management to make an approval."

One of the technicians hands Barmy a status report. After taking a look through it, Barmy says, "We're supposed to bring the ship back to <destination> as soon as repairs are done. Want to come along? We could use the escort."

children.key: As you disembark, you see Barmy talking to a man wearing a Southbound Shipyards engineering uniform.
Barmy waves you over. "Captain <last>, this is Ricardo Astillero from Southbound Shipyards R&D. He was just telling me the bad news.
"Wait, THE Captain <last>? The war hero?" Ricardo expresses his surprise.
"The one and only. So what's this bad news?"
"Nevermind that. What's this about bad news?"
"Upper management has decided to cancel the Liberator project. They aren't even interested in seeing Barmy's test results."
"If that's true, then do they plan on scrapping the ship?" asks Barmy.
"They are. But maybe Captain <last> can help."
Ricardo has a grim look on his face. "Take the ship and leave. I'll tell them I tricked you into taking it for more testing. Please, we worked so hard on this..."
Barmy turns to you. "Even so, there might still be some repurcussions to your reputation. It's your choice, captain."
"Alright, it's a big risk, but I'll take it."
"Sorry, no. I'm not willing to take this much risk for someone I just met."
"I understand. Sorry for asking something so foolish." Ricardo looks dejected. "Excuse me. I have some things I need to do."
"I think I'll stay here for a while." Barmy says bitterly. "I probably can't do much to change their minds, but I'd still like to try."
"Thank you, captain!" Ricardo's eyes fill with hope. "You'd better get going. The sooner you get the Liberator away from here, the better."
"I'd better come with you." Barmy says. "There might be some difficult questions to answer if I stick around. Besides, I need a lift home."

children.key: You visit Syndicate headquarters and ask about the District ship Balthazar. The Syndicate agents are very helpful in providing you with the ship's history. It had been on Foundry since the 24th century. The Syndicate officially took ownership of it in the 27th century. By then, it was being used as an office building. In the 28th century it was dismantled and shipped to R&D facilities on Hephaestus where it was eventually reconstructed. A few ships inspired by its design were actually built and sold, but the product line was deemed a failure and production stopped shortly after.
"Sorry, that is all of the information we have on file. If you want to learn more, I recommend you visit the Syndicated Systems office on Hephaestus."

children.key: The R&D offices are surprised by your inquiry reqarding the District ship Balthazar. The agents inform you that the ship was sold to a private collector on Nimbus towards the end of the 29th century. They will not violate their customer's privacy, but thank you for sharing your interest in the old city ship.
As you are leaving the facility, a technician approaches you. "You're looking for the Balthazar. Are you working on rebuilding the Exodus?"

You nod in affirmation and she holds up a datachip, saying, "My name is Maria Carpenter. This is the information of the customer who bought the Balthazar. If you find the ship and need help getting it operational, let me know." She hands the data chip to you. "I know a few other technicians willing to help. All we ask is that we be allowed to join the ship's crew once it's able to fly again."
"You're willing to abandon your jobs here?"
She responds, "We don't hate our jobs here. But bringing back the Exodus will be a historical event. We'll definitely want to be a part of that!"

values: A technician at Syndicated Systems. She and her associates are willing to quit their jobs and join the crew of the Exodus in order to be a part of history.

name: Balthazar 4
description: Go to <planet> in the <system> system and recruit Maria Carpenter to salvage the Balthazar.

values: Go to <planet> in the <system> system and recruit Maria Carpenter to salvage the Balthazar.

children.key: You locate the customer's address and find a local landing spot. Unfortunately, the current resident doesn't know what you're talking about and suggests you check with the department of Housing and Urban Development. However, the agents at the office don't have any info on what happened to the previous resident.
"Why are you looking for this person?" one of them asks.

"Wow, you should have said that sooner! The story of the Balthazar is famous here. During a pirate raid in 2925, it was the largest ship in the planetary defense fleet. Unfortunately, it crashed into the ocean. If you want, I can give you information on where the wreck is located. Just give me your messaging address." After you give him the address, he forwards the data to you.

You find the ship submerged in a relatively shallow part of the ocean. Despite being covered in algae and barnacles, it appears to be salvageable. But this is going to be a big job. You'll need a dedicated team of technicians willing to put in the work required to bring the ship back to the surface and make it operational again. Fortunately, you know just where to find such a team, and send a notification to Maria Carpenter that you will be needing the services of her technicians in the near future.

Before leaving, you head over to the local seaport and file the paperwork for salvaging rights. Unsurprisingly, the application is rejected because someone else already has those rights. You look up their information and find that the rights holder is based out of a local fishing operation.

It turns out to be a small fishing operation with a single boat. You don't see any salvaging equipment here. When you ring the bell, an old grumpy man waddles out. "Welcome to Barnacle Bobby's Bait and Fish! Are you looking to schedule a fishing expedition?"
"I want to buy the salvaging rights for the Balthazar."
"Hot diggity! I knew someone would want it eventually! 14,520,000 credits! I done my research! You won't be pulling the wool over my eyes!."
"It's an old barnacle covered wreck. There's no guarantee the ship will even fly again."
"Fly?" For a moment, he stares out the window in quiet contemplation. "Fine! Fine. Ya done twisted my arm. 10,000,000 credits. Take it, space jockey!"
"... and I won't file a complaint with the port authority for you squatting on the rights."
"Deal. You drive a hard bargain, space jockey." He pulls out a data pad and fills out the forms to transfer the rights ownership. "Do you think you'll actually get her to fly again?"

values: Owner of a fishing operation on Nimbus. He was squatting on the salvaging rights to the Balthazar for far longer than the local port authority should have allowed. He eventually sold the rights to me after some negotiation.

children.key: While having some maintenance done on your ship, you notice a photo on the wall of the hangar waiting room. It's a picture of a young boy standing in front of a huge ship you don't recognize. The head mechanic stops in for a pot of coffee and remarks, "That's my grandfather posing in front of the Prefecture ship Melchior at the Zug spaceport. I used to dream of going there to see it for myself, but I just never got around to leaving this rock."

values: The Prefecture ship Melchior was once a landmark at the spaceport on Zug.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Melchior 1

name: Melchior 2
description: Go to <planet> in the <system> system and continue searching for the Prefecture ship Melchior.

values: Go to <planet> in the <system> system and continue searching for the Prefecture ship Melchior.

children.key: You visit the Old Port and search for clues to the location of Melchior, the Prefecture ship that was once a landmark here. While touring the shops, you find an old fashioned post card bearing a photo of Melchior similar to the one you saw previously. In this photo there seems to be some kind of festival surrounding the ship's landing pad. "Any idea where the ship is now?" you ask the sales clerk, a cheerful old lady.
"Back when they remodeled the area, it was sold off to an antique collector on Glaze. My father actually took that photo on the day it launched."
You thank the sales clerk and start to leave.
"Wait. You aren't planning to leave without purchasing the post card, are you? It's only one credit." The old lady makes a sales pitch.
"Just one credit? OK, sure." You pay one credit and tuck the postcard into your pocket. Who knows, maybe it will be useful on your search.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Melchior 2

name: Melchior 3
description: Go to <planet> in the <system> system and track down the Prefecture ship Melchior.

values: Go to <planet> in the <system> system and track down the Prefecture ship Melchior.

children.key: After asking around the spaceport, you managed to track down Richard Wigglebottom III, the grandson of the antique collector who purchased the Melchior. However, he isn't particularly welcoming when you arrive at his residence.
"Go away! Whatever you're selling, we don't want any!" he yells.
"Look, I'm just trying to find this ship," you say while holding up the post card you purchased on Zug.
The man notices the picture on the card and is momentarily speechless. Finally he asks, "Can I have that?"

He looks at the card as he says, "When dad passed away my sister, Cathleen, inherited that ship. She and I never really got along. When the Free Worlds declared independence from the Republic, she took it with her to Bourne." He passes the card back to you. "Thanks for the memories. But I'd rather forget."

values: The grandson of the antique collector who purchased the Melchior from Zug. His sister Cathleen, who didn't get along with him, inherited the ship.

values: Go to <planet> in the <system> system and ask the weapons R&D team about the Melchior. Make sure you have a lot of credits. Convincing them to sell you the ship won't be cheap.

children.key: You have no trouble finding Cathleen Wigglebottom, the granddaughter of the antique collector who purchased the Melchior from Zug. After presenting her with the postcard, she tells you the fate of the Melchior.

"I donated it to the war effort. But to be honest, the upkeep costs were more than I could handle. The Melchior was the crown jewel of dad's collection, but most of the actual money making assets went to my brother. Maybe dad was hoping we could reconcile our differences. But it just didn't work out." She holds up the postcard you presented to her. "May I keep this postcard?"
"Thanks! You might want to try searching for it on Rust. Last I heard, they were using it for weapons research there."
You imagine them using it for target practice...
"Also..." she trails off. "If you find the ship, would you consider hiring me to help crew it? I'd really appreciate being able to fly my father's ship again."
You'll need to make sure you have a lot of credits. Convincing the R&D team at Kraz Cybernetics to sell you the Melchior won't be cheap.

values: The granddaughter of the antique collector who purchased the Melchior from Zug. She suggests looking for the ship on Rust and has offered to help crew the ship if you find it.

name: Melchior 5
description: Go to <planet> in the <system> system and recruit Cathleen Wigglebottom to crew the Melchior.

values: Go to <planet> in the <system> system and recruit Cathleen Wigglebottom to crew the Melchior.

children.key: You arrive at Kraz Cybernetics and ask about the Melchior. It turns out that it's scheduled to test a new shielding system today! You inform the receptionist that you are interested in purchasing the ship and she directs you to their R&D department. After rushing over there, you find the person in charge.
You find Barmy Edward, Chief Offensive Engineer at Kraz Cybernetics working on some new type of gun turret.
"<first> <last>, you've got perfect timing! There's this experimental shielding system we've been wanting to try out..."
"We're planning to outfit it onto one of our test ships, the Melchior..."
"All we'll need you to do is shoot at it for a bit to see how well it operates..."
"Huh? What?" He pauses, regarding you quizzicaly.
He takes a moment to process what you've just said. "That old thing? Are you sure?"
"You know, the Melchior is technically a city ship. Do you have a license?"
You press your case. "Wasn't the whole point of the Free Worlds to get away from oppressive Republic regulations?"
He takes a moment to think about it. "I guess you've got a point. This isn't The Deep, and those licenses are really only for purchasing Bactrians."
"Alright." He looks something up on a data pad. "6,000,000 credits. Don't bother haggling. I've already cut down the suggested price."
You look at the data pad and see that he has given you a huge discount.
"Do you have a crew set up for it?" he asks.
"I know someone who's able to help with that."
"Great. You can hold off on completing the transaction until you bring the crew here. In the meantime, we will continue to use it for weapons testing..."
"I think I'll pay for the ship now."
You explain, "I wouldn't want it to get blown up in one of your experiments." You complete the transaction and he marks the Melchior as unavailable for all of their future projects.
With that settled, you get ready to return to Bourne and recruit Cathleen Wigglebottom to crew the Melchior.

values: Rescued the Melchior from being a test ship at Kraz Cybernetics. I just need to pull together a worthy crew to fly the ship again.

children.key: Family squabbles can be so messy. You keep your distance and let Cathleen do the talking.
"Richard, I know we haven't gotten along. But we have an opportunity to put that behind us. Won't you pilot our father's ship?"
She holds out the postcard you previously gave her. Richard takes it and stares at it.
Cathleen continues. "I think the reason dad gave me the ship is so that we would have a reason to set aside our differences and work together. Please Richard..."
Richard nods. "Alright, I'll pilot it. Maybe you're right about dad's reason for giving you the ship. I never could figure out what he was thinking."

Cathleen hugs her brother and Richard, surprised by the gesture, drops the old postcard onto the ground. As the two siblings walk into the house to catch up on old times, you pick up the forgotten postcard and dust it off. As you stuff the postcard into your pocket, you hear the siblings starting up a new argument...
Once the siblings calm down, you get ready to head back to Rust.

name: Caspar 1
description: Head to <destination> and learn the fate of the Municipality city ship Caspar.

values: Head to <destination> and learn the fate of the Municipality city ship Caspar.

children.key: While you are trying to relax at the bar you notice a music video of a There Might Be Riots concert playing on the bar's main video display. The song they're singing is about a metropolis that fell to ruin when the inhabitants couldn't get along.
"What a sad song," says the bartender. "Reminds me of Caspar and the Exodus."

"It all started with the Exodus voyage heading south from Sol. Not long after the start of its journey, the city ship was attacked by..." the bartender looks around then whispers to you, "... aliens."
"Why is there no historical record of this?"
"Not at all! According to the stories, that's what happened!"
"No one actually saw the aliens themselves, but their ships looked organic. Like they were using flying squids as their ships."

"It's a government coverup. They don't want you to know anything about what's out there. Can you imagine the social upheaval? Better to keep people in the dark, believing that humanity alone is in charge of its destiny."

"The Exodus had a feature that allowed the ship to separate into three distinct sections, each operating as its own ship. The idea was that, along with its support fighters, you could suddenly have a nimble fleet of smaller ships instead of just one big target. The story says that one of the ships immediately fled instead of helping in the fight. As a result, the remaining ships fled as well."

"I'm not sure. There are different accounts blaming each of the three ships. Who can say which one is real? What I can tell you is that Caspar fled north to this area, the region that would eventually become the Paradise planets. Different planets claim to have been the one founded by Caspar. And there are stories of the ship continuing to act as a cargo hauler and transport between various systems for decades. But one day, the ship left to make a delivery to Follower, in the Alphard system. And it never returned." The bartender leans back. "That's it. That's as much of the story as I know."
You thank the bartender for the story.

values: The Exodus was attacked by aliens during its initial voyage beyond Earth's solar system. The ship used its separation feature to try outmaneuvering the aliens. Instead of working together, the three ships fled the battle.
The merchant ship Guiding Star is asking for assistance.
"We were attacked by pirates. Thanks for your help! Could you escort us down to the planet? I'll make sure to reward you once we land."
The captain of the Guiding Star thanks you for your assistance and rewards you with <payment>. "If we'd been able to head north into The Deep, we probably would have been safe from those pirates."

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Caspar 1

name: Caspar 2

values: The Caspar was last seen heading towards Follower in the Alphard system. Here, the trail goes cold. My search for this city ship will have to be put on hold until I can find another lead.

children.key: "Caspar?" replies the bartender. "Never heard of it."
"I know about Caspar." A kid at the corner vending machine speaks up. "It's a ghost ship that terrorizes the far western reaches of The Dirt Belt."
"Aliens!" a one-eyed man yells out. "They took over the ship after it was attacked and are hiding in the void between the hyper space links!"
"Don't be ridiculous," interjects a woman with a mo-hawk. "The ship was definitely taken over by Alphas. I'll bet they're hiding somewhere in The Deep."

You've been asking around the spaceport while searching for clues to what happened to the Municipality ship Caspar. But all the responses conflict in some way. The trail seems to have gone cold here. Perhaps you'll get lucky and stumble upon it again someday. But for now, your search for Caspar has reached a dead end.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Caspar 2

name: Caspar Capture

children.key: You receive a distress signal from a ship identifying itself as Caspar! The crew has mutinied against their pirate captain, but are now derelict. This could be a golden opportunity to acquire the final piece of the Exodus!

When you board the ship, you find the only surviving crew are children. Amazingly, they are diligently repairing the ship and pay you no attention. When you meet their new captain, Tyler Maverick, you find that he is a mere teenager.

"Welcome aboard my ship Captain <last>, hero of the war. I was both surprised and relieved when our scanners indicated <ship> was nearby. Surely, a captain of your reputation could be trusted to render assistance."
"Your crew is already repairing the ship. What do you need me for?"
"I'll help, on the condition that you relinquish your ship."

"Earning our freedom was a hard battle. There were a lot of deaths on both sides. But what now? Our parents are dead and we have no homes to return to. I'm only captain because I'm the oldest one here."

"We need guidance and would willingly join your fleet, Captain <last>. However, we demand that all of us be allowed to continue to operate Caspar as its primary crew." From his expression, you can tell he is sincere.
"Once the ship is operational, your first mission is to follow me to Urd for refueling and repair."

values: Found the Caspar in the Archipelago. The pirate crew mutinied against their captain and offered to join my fleet.
The newly appointed captain of the Caspar, after its crew of children mutinied against their pirate captain. He seems sincere in wanting to keep his crew together.

name: Metropolis 2
description: Take the Exodus to Earth and enjoy a celebration reception!

values: Take the Exodus to Earth and enjoy a celebration reception!

children.key: <payment> were deducted from your account to cover the costs of reassembling the Metropolis ship.

When you see Joseph Welder you are surprised to find him in a wheelchair. "My health has been deteriorating. But don't worry! I don't need to walk in order to oversee this project. Mark my words, the Exodus will fly again!"
A special docking bay was reserved for the Balthazar, Melchior, and Caspar to park in. Now that all three ships are reunited, it's time to begin the process of combining them to form Exodus.
There are a few uncomfortable moments of silence before a transmission is received from Melchior.
"Melchior is..." Richard's voice is cut off by sounds of a scuffle...
"Melchior is..." Cathleen's voice is cut off by sounds of a scuffle...
"Melchior, is everything all right up there?" asks Joseph.
"YES!" Richard and Cathleen respond in unison. "Melchior is in position!"
Joseph turns to you. "They've been like this during all the practice runs. Thankfully, they'll be your problem after today."
The three ships align and begin connecting as their binding clamps lock into place. Finally, the Exodus is whole again.

"Congratulations!" Joseph claps while the technical team whoops and hollers. "Let's take it out for a test flight. The entire spaceport has been looking forward to this since you brought the first ship in. A reception has been prepared for us on Earth. Let's give them a show!
"She's flying smooth as a Sparrow," reports Richard Wigglebottom III.
"All the systems are operating at acceptable levels," reports Maria Carpenter.
Soon after launching, you receive a message:
"Congratulations on reassembling the Exodus, Captain <last>. It would be a shame if someone were to steal it."
Tyler yells, "Sensors are showing hostiles incoming!"
"Maybe I shouldn't have had that second bowl of oatmeal this morning..." Joseph rubs his stomach.

values: [MISSION FAILED]: You have failed an essential part of the Exodus missions. If life were a game, you could reload a previous save file and try again.

children.key: The reception party will have to wait until after you shake off your pursuers.

values: Joseph passed away the day after the restored Exodus' test flight. One of his ancestors was on the design team for the Exodus. Seeing that ship fly again was a childhood dream of Joseph's. His dream will live on as the Exodus returns to the Endless Sky.
The Exodus had an exciting test flight. Unfortunately, damage to the interlocking mechanisms from an attack by Marauders prevents the Exodus from splitting into its component sub-ships.

children.key: After an exciting test flight, the Exodus has finally arrived to the celebration reception on Earth.
"Alright everyone!" exclaims Joseph. "Begin the separation sequence and land!"
"... What are you doing!?!" yells Cathleen.
"... Don't blame me! The system isn't responding!" yells Richard.
"Melchior, what is going on?" asks Joseph.
"It's not just Melchior!" replies Maria. "None of the binding clamps are responding. All of Exodus' binding clamps appear to be frozen in place."
Joseph turns to you. "We're going to need a really big landing pad..."

It takes an hour for the local spaceport to clear three adjacent landing pads to accommodate the Exodus. The reception party proceeds despite being a bit behind schedule. The entire Exodus crew is eager to celebrate. Several times during the evening you are interrupted by incoming congratulatory messages from various people you've encountered and worked with in the past. After you finish responding to one such message, you notice Joseph has also excused himself from the reception area to sit on a balcony overlooking the spaceport.

"Thank you, Captain <last>. I never mentioned it before, but one of my ancestors was on the design team for that ship. Seeing the Exodus fly again has been a childhood dream of mine." He pauses to make a great big yawn. "I suppose I've had enough excitement for one day. Figuring out how to unlock those binding clamps will have to wait until tomorrow. For now, I just want to rest. Go on back to the party. I'll be fine. I have an assistant I can call to fetch me when I'm done here."
You congratulate Joseph on a job well done and thank him for giving you the opportunity to be a part of his dream. The last time you saw him, he was staring out over the spaceport.

He had a look of contentment on his face that you will never forget. The next day you received the news that he'd passed away in his sleep. The crews for the Balthazar and Melchior were especially distraught, since they'd spent more time with him during the wait for Caspar to be found. A funeral was quickly organized as most of his friends and family were already in the area for yesterday's celebration. Through their tears, many of them thanked you for helping him to make his dream a reality.
The Exodus crew had their own reactions to this turn of events.

After that day, the Wigglebottoms stopped arguing. If Cathleen and Richard ever did argue, you never heard about it. From what you could discern, Joseph had taken a fatherly sort of role to them during the time they spent with him. Perhaps his passing brought back memories of their own father.

Tyler Maverick withdrew from taking the lead. He'd been no stranger to death, having lived on a pirate ship for the past few years. But this was the first time he'd experienced the death of someone whose life seemed to matter to the people around him. It was a strange feeling that he would need time to sort out.

So it was that Tyler stepped down while Maria Carpenter ascended to take a leadership role. With Joseph's guidance, she'd already been acting as a chief engineer of sorts. Now that he's gone, she felt a certain responsibility for maintaining the ship in his honor.
It's time for the Exodus to fly again.

"I could. But why do you need mine?"
Both of them look at each other and nod.
"It's a rare limited edition!" exclaims Kiru.
"AND YOU HAVE MODEL NUMBER ONE OF ONE HUNDRED!"
You remember the box having a big "1/100" printed on it.

"So, will you sell it to us? We can pay you 1,000,000 credits for it."
"Okay, sure. I can let it go at that price."
You all head to your ship, where you retrieve the model and exchange it with them for 1,000,000 credits. Both appear to be very happy with their purchase.
"Yeah, it has sentimental value to me," you respond.
"Besides, I accidentally broke a piece when I first opened it."
Both of them stare at you wide eyed with mouths agape.
"Thanks for the offer. But I have to get going." You stand up and leave before they can recover from the shock.

children.key: You locate the hangar that was indicated in the message and land near it. Idly, you wonder if they could have chosen a warmer location to hold this meeting. On the way down, the snow drifting across your field of vision almost obscures your view of several nearby hobos warming themselves by bonfires. It's difficult to see, but you are certain that they are armed with weapons.
You decide that the presence of the armed hobos is a risk you're unwilling to bear and abort the landing.

You make sure the gun at your hip is fully loaded before opening the cargo bay doors. A bald man in a gaudy suit waves at you and holds up a data pad. "Simply confirm payment on this data pad and it's all yours!"
"What, exactly, am I buying?" you ask, as you wonder why he isn't wearing a hat in this snow storm.

"Behold!" he gestures towards the hangar. As he speaks, the door to the hangar slides open and inside is a space ship. "The prototype Hauler VI! Stolen from Southbound Shipyards and left abandoned at Terminus. It eventually found its way into our inventory. While most of the original outfits were looted by scavengers and had to be replaced, the original cooling systems are still installed!"
By the time he finishes his sales pitch, a snowplow has cleared a path for the ship to move out. All it needs is a crew to pilot it.
The salesman holds the data pad out expectantly.
As you weigh your options, memories of a cargo hold bursting into flames and the scent of burnt sushi float through your memories...

He puts away the data pad. "Unfortunately, it appears we were unable to reach an agreement. Thank you for your time. However, I suggest you depart immediately." The armed hobos are no longer warming themselves by the fires and are instead trudging their way through the snow towards the hangar. You decide to follow the man's suggestion.
"Congratulations on your purchase captain. I'm sure you won't regret it. You'll hear from us again if we happen to acquire any more unique  merchandise that might interest you."

values: Purchased the stolen Hauler VI prototype on the Midnight Market. The prototype refrigeration system is a terrible cooling device, but there's something interesting about the energy feedback it creates. Might be worth holding onto them for now.

"Congratulations on your purchase captain. I'm sure you won't regret it. You'll hear from us again if we happen to acquire any more unique merchandise that might interest you."

children.key: You've stolen a Wanderer micro-satellite. If you were searching for a place to convert it into some quick credits, you could do worse than the spaceport on <origin>.

You find a street vendor selling industrial devices. Most of it was probably plundered off of merchant vessels.
You try to get at least a million credits for the micro-satellite, but he is having none of it. Perhaps you'll have better luck with a different vendor.

After some negotiating, you both manage to agree on a price. You hand over the Wanderer micro-satellite and are 1,000,000 credits richer. The vendor immediately begins tinkering with the micro-satellite.

He is poking at one corner of the cube with one of this tools when there is an audible 'click'. The micro-satellite begins to glow red while emitting a high pitched whine. The last thing you see before you die is the explosion...
You've decided to keep this valuable piece of alien technology for yourself. Perhaps you'll even figure out how it works someday. After returning to your ship you hide it in a safe place.

name: Lares Camping (Bums)

children.key: Despte being abandoned, the nearby cabins are well furnished. It might be a nice change of pace to sleep somewhere other than the cramped bunk on your ship.
Archipelago nights can be bright as twilight, depending on the positioning of the nearby star systems. Looking out the window, you see some wild animals moving among the trees.

You grab your gun and head out into the woods. Not too far is some kind of three legged furry creature. You take aim and fire! The creature collapses while other animals farther away flee. Hauling the carcass back to the cabin isn't difficult and you start skinning the creature. You're just about done when there's a knock on your door.
You open the door and find a pair of hobos who were attracted by the gunfire. They're hoping you'd be willing to spare some of whatever you caught.
You give each hobo one of the creature's legs. They are overjoyed at the gift and thank you before leaving. You watch them head over to one of the other abandoned cabins.
It's two against one and it turns out these bums have guns of their own! You manage to shoot one, but the other one shoots you. The bullet lands somewhere inside a vital organ.

It's two against one and it turns out these bums have guns of their own! Fortunately, their shots miss and you manage to take them down. With all the gunfire, you've no doubt that more unwelcome guests will be approaching. Better head back to your ship and get out of here.

You light up the fireplace and roast the meat from the creature you hunted. The smell of the charred meat is heavenly and you can't resist taking a bite of the delicious barbecue as its juices glisten in the firelight. It's always great to have fresh food instead of the usual canned slop you keep in your ship's pantry.
After a restful night, you clean up the cabin and head back to your ship.

name: Lares Camping (Raiders)

children.key: Despite being abandoned, the nearby cabins are well furnished. It might be a nice change of pace to sleep somewhere other than the cramped bunk on your ship.

You settle in for a peaceful night's sleep when the silence is broken by the sounds of an afterburner ripping through the night sky! That sound is quickly overttaken by a loud explosion from the direction of the spaceport!
You kill the lights and huddle with your gun in the darkness. There are distant sounds of yelling and gunfire. Eventually, the sounds fade and silence reclaims the night.
You try to get some sleep, but you keep your gun clutched close in case someone comes looking for trouble. Eventually, morning comes.

When you get back to the spaceport, you find the burnt wreck of a pirate interceptor near your ship. It looks like someone tried and failed to pry open the hatch to your ship. There are no other ships nearby and other than the addition of the wrecked interceptor, the spaceport looks as deserted as usual.

name: Lares Camping (Scavenger)

children.key: Despte being abandoned, the nearby cabins are well furnished. It might be a nice change of pace to sleep somewhere other than the cramped bunk on your ship.
The night is surprisingly dark and a cool breeze blows in the window. As you close the shutters, you hear a scratching sound on your door.

You've barely opened the door a crack when a small furball darts in underfoot! The cabin is riddled with innumerable nooks and crannies between and under the furnishings. There's no telling where the creature went. All night long you hear weird scratching sounds as the creature scampers about unseen. Before you can get any shuteye, the first light of dawn is already filtering in between the window shutters. To your dismay, you discover that the creature managed to get into your food stash, leaving crumbs scattered about. You tidy up the cabin as best as you can, but are unable to find the little creature responsible for your sleepless night of misery. You are still bleary eyed when you return to your ship and idly wonder if you should really be piloting it in your current condition.
After a restful night, you clean up the cabin and head back to your ship.

name: Biohazard 1: Star Explorer
description: A ship named Biohazard-031 seems to be kidnapping the crews of merchant ships in the north. Find the ship and rescue any captives that you can. Then return to <planet> for payment (<payment>).

values: A ship named Biohazard-031 seems to be kidnapping the crews of merchant ships in the north. Find the ship and rescue any captives that you can. Then return to <planet> for payment (<payment>).

children.key: A navy officer approaches you. "Do you have combat experience? We are offering <payment> to any pilots that can fight to help track down the ship known as Biohazard and rescue any people they have kidnapped. The Biohazard has raided several merchant ships in the north over the last few days. The victims could be sold into slavery or suffer some other horrible fate."
The Biohazard has attacked ships in the north. It may be in one of the many uninhabited systems scattered across this region.

values: The Biohazard emerges from the luminescent clouds surrounding the star and hails you: "New test subjects! Excellent! The last batch didn't fare so well..."

children.key: When you board the ship, no defenders challenge you. Occasional screams can be heard in the distance. Your search for the kidnapped victims leads you to the ship's brig. But the prisoners have escaped! A few dead bodies of the prisoners remain. Each has the alphanumeric sequence "BH-031" tattooed onto the back of their neck. You also notice their skin is mottled with greenish patches...

You find the Biohazard's medical bay. Strapped to the operating table is a man's body. His skin is more greenish than the ones you saw previously. Suddenly, he opens his eyes and moans in pain. "Scientists... turning... us... into... alphas." The man falls unconscious and his breathing slows to a stop. He's dead.

You find several more dead bodies as you explore the ship. Some appear to be escaped prisoners with the strange green patches on their skin while others are normal humans in lab coats or tactical gear. The ones in uniforms bear a patch with "BH-031" printed on them. The humans are carrying rifles loaded with some sort of injection round. A bayonet style needle protrudes from under the barrel.

As you take all this in, a door at the far end of the hall opens and an escaped prisoner emerges from it before running in your direction! Green splotches mar her arms and face. She yells out, "Help! They're killing us!" One of the Biohazard crew members appears from behind her, shooting her in the back of the leg with a single injection round. She falls, seemingly dead before she even hits the floor. More Biohazard crew arrive and they turn these weapons towards you...

values: [MISSION FAILED]: You were supposed to rescue the kidnapped victims before destroying the Biohazard-031. If life were a game, you could reload a save file and try again.

Encountered a ship named "Biohazard". The crew were kidnapping humans and performing experiments to turn them into Alphas. None of the victims could be saved. The crew wore uniforms with the tag "BH-031" and their prisoners had a similar mark on their necks. This ship was "Biohazard-031". There could be other "Biohazard" ships performing similar experiments.

children.key: Although you failed to rescue any of the victims, the government of <planet> pays you <payment>. You managed to stop the Biohazard from kidnapping any more people for their twisted experiments. But some details about this mission linger. The crew of the Biohazard didn't seem like normal pirates. The uniforms were too professional. And the antipersonnel weapons they carried require specialized ammunition. But most concerning of all was the "031" appended to the ship's name. It seems to suggest that there are other Biohazard ships out there...

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Biohazard 1: Star Explorer

name: Biohazard 2: Bulk Freighter
description: A ship named Biohazard-013 seems to be freeing slaves from pirate slavers in the core. Find the ship and rescue any slaves on board. Then return to <planet> for payment (<payment>).

values: A ship named Biohazard-013 seems to be freeing slaves from pirate slavers in the core. Find the ship and rescue any slaves on board. Then return to <planet> for payment (<payment>).

children.key: Several odd flyers are posted around the spaceport:
"Don't be fooled by strangers offering freedom from slavery! It's just a trick from rival pirates!"
"My favorite slave was kidnapped! Reward of 1,000 credits for her safe return. Contact Cygnet on Deadman's Cove for more details."
"Is your master mistreating you? Contact us for a better tomorrow!"
The intricacies of rival pirate slavers normally wouldn't catch your attention, but the job board has something interesting:

Wanted: A pirate ship named Biohazard-013 working for an unknown group is suspected of liberating slaves. Find them and retrieve any stolen slaves found onboard. Show no mercy to the ship's crew. Payment is <payment>.
A ship that liberates slaves may seem heroic, but the name of the ship evokes horrible memories of another ship with a similar name you've encountered in the past.
(Take the job to hunt down the Biohazard-013.)
If this ship is anything like the previous Biohazard you encountered, the missing slaves could have been harvested for some terrible experiment.

You find the Biohazard-013 lurking in this system with several Headhunters escorting it. The freighter hails you: "You were responsible for the incident with BH-031. We will not permit you to interfere with our operation."
Suddenly, the Biohazard releases a cloud of drones that move to attack!
When you board the ship, no defenders challenge you. The ship is eerily quiet. Your search for the kidnapped victims leads you to the ship's brig. But no one is being held here.

You find a relic of the Pug invasion on board. Nearby is a shelf with empty canisters that are designed to be attached to the Pug Biodefenses and filled with its gas. Several spots on the shelf are empty...

The cargo bay is stuffed with dead slaves. They appear to have died from exposure to the Pug Biodefenses. Perhaps this ship was focused on bio weapons experiments. The vents begin to hiss as gas from the Biodefenses flows in... The crew must still be controlling it from elsewhere on the ship. You exit the cargo bay and plan your next move.

values: [MISSION FAILED]: You were supposed to retrieve the stolen slaves before destroying the Biohazard-013. If life were a game, you could reload a save file and try again.

Found a ship named "Biohazard-013". This one was kidnapping slaves from pirate slavers and using them for bioweapons experimentation. I put a stop to this operation, earning the gratitude of the pirate slavers. Whether this was a fate worse for the slaves or not is a debate too lengthy to include here.

children.key: Although you failed to retrieve any of the stolen slaves, the Biohazard-013 has stopped stealing them from the pirate slavers. The pirates reward you with <payment>. The strange canisters you spotted aboard the ship could be deadlier than Nerve Gas. Hopefully no other ships were developing this weapon.

A militia pilot adds, "They also made the announcement during Han Sizer month to maximize interest. Bidding will definitely reach several million credits."

children.key: The Museum of Space Exploration on <origin> is hosting an auction for the Blue Ridge, the ship Han Sizer used to explore the Southern Rim. They are only accepting bids from militia members. Do you want to check it out?

values: Decided to ignore the auction of the "Blue Ridge," the ship once used by Han Sizer to explore the galactic rim.

children.key: You've decided to ignore the auction of the Blue Ridge.
You visit the Museum of Space Exploration to see how the auction on the Blue Ridge is progressing. To prove your eligibility, you show the receptionist your Militia license.

"Your license checks out," she says after looking you up in the computer system. "You have perfect timing Captain <last>! The auction ends today. Once bidding hit a million credits, we started only accepting bids in increments of 100,000 credits to help limit the auction to serious bidders only. The current bid is at 5,900,000 credits. Would you like to place a bid for 6,000,000 credits?"
"I'm sorry to hear that," she says. "The 5,900,000 credit bid has been up for a while now and no one seems willing to go over that. With 6,000,000 credits, I'm certain you'd win."

values: Decided not to place any bids on the "Blue Ridge," the Hipparion once used by Han Sizer to explore the galactic rim.

children.key: You leave the Museum of Space Exploration without placing any bid on the Blue Ridge.

values: Purchased the "Blue Ridge," the Hipparion once used by Han Sizer to explore the galactic rim. The ship was lacking a Hyperdrive. Supposedly, it was removed for security. But maybe there's more to it than that...

children.key: "I've placed your bid into the system," she says. "Come back once the Museum closes to learn the result."

You stop by the museum as it is about to close. "Congratulations Captain <last>. You are the winner of the Blue Ridge," says the receptionist. "Let's process the payment and legal transfer of ownership."

Once that gets taken care of, she shows you where the ship is stored. You look over the ship and notice that the weapons are archaic, but functional. More concerning is the lack of a Hyperdrive. You can drop by the outfitter later to buy one, but your curiosity has been piqued.
She grins and answers, "It's for security, so thieves can't just take the ship and flee the system." It sounds like a reasonable explanation.

But then she leans in and whispers conspiratorially, "There are rumors that Han Sizer got ahold of some alien device, like the ones the Quarg use instead of a Hyperdrive. Supposedly, the government confiscated it after he died." She leans back, "But whether that's true or not, who can say?" She smiles mischievously and you're uncertain if that's just a story they tell museum guests to enhance the legend of Han Sizer.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Blue Ridge 2

values: Help the Sunriser eliminate a Modified Firebird named the <npc> which has been attacking merchants near <system>. Then report to <destination> for payment (<payment>).

children.key: You notice a young pilot staring intently at the job board.
He looks at you and shrugs. "It's a bounty hunting job. The pay is good, but I've never done this kind of work before."
"I could lend a hand for a share of the reward."
"You should stick to safer jobs like hauling garbage."
The man scowls at you. "I didn't ask for your advice." He walks away.
He gives you a skeptical look. "What do you know about bounty hunting?"
"That's okay. I have a tough ship, a Rancor."

You've heard stories about them. The Rancor was originally a pirate vessel, and many were used in the early turf wars. The Alpha War was the beginning of the Rancor's decline as faster interceptors quickly outpaced and outmaneuvered this relatively slower ship. Today it is seen as a relic of the past, most noteworthy for influencing the design of the Fury.
"Look kid, I'm willing to help out. Just don't die out there."
"On second thought, I don't want to be involved in this."
"Alright, I'll let you tag along. Just don't get in my way old timer."
"I'm Rocky. My Rancor is named Sunriser."

values: Rocky hails you: "Where should we look first? Is one jump away far enough? Should we try two?"

children.key: While at the spaceport bar, a drunk freighter captain is loudly complaining about something called the "New China Supply Run" to anyone who will listen.
"Eight days! How the hell is anyone supposed to get that done in eight days?" He chugs down his beer and orders another.

One of his crew mates responds, "Even when we tried adding extra Fuel Pods, it takes ten days with no stops to refuel. I don't see how it can be done any faster." He finishes off his beer and orders another.

"It must be a scam. A scam!" The captain accepts his fresh beer from the waitress and immediately chugs it down. "I'll bet Wang Xiang Tai is just awarding the Special Supply Run jobs to their friends and claiming that they completed the New China Supply Run." The waitress comes to collect his empty mug and he orders another.
"Yeah, that must be it." A third man with a whisky bottle downs a shot and refills his glass.

They keep going on about how unfair it is. By the time they leave, you've learned that their ship is named the <npc> and they've been trying and failing to complete something called the New China Supply Run. Supposedly, its a job given out at some place called "Wang Xiang Tai". It seems completing the job gives a pilot access to better quality jobs there.

name: Limit Breaker Syndicate Patrol
description: Accompany the <npc> on its patrol of Core pirate systems. Return to <destination> once the patrol is complete... if the <npc> survives, that is.

values: Accompany the <npc> on its patrol of Core pirate systems. Return to <destination> once the patrol is complete... if the <npc> survives, that is.

children.key: You notice a pilot wearing a Syndicate flight suit opening a maintenance panel on his Wasp."

You see him installing a Limit Breaker onto the Wasp. These are notoriously dangerous, an outfit that bypasses the internal safey mechanisms to keep a ship operational beyond the point it would normally be disabled.

He look at you, thoughtful. Then he nods, "I suppose so. But I'm not on salary. And the Syndicate doesn't pay me for time spent adrift while disabled. So this should allow me to keep operating and earning money to send home to my family." Seems risky. He must really need the money. Perhaps he owes a debt to the bank to pay for that Wasp...
"Would you mind if I tagged along?"
He smiles ruefully. "I get you. But at least the insurance pays well if I die on the job." He gets back to work, the conversation over. Life must be tough for a company man.

He looks at you with skepticism. "I won't stop you, but I can't afford to pay an escort. At best, I can share map data for some of the nearby systems if you don't already have it. The name's Syphus. And this..." He extends his hand towards the Wasp, "is the S-13X9. Technically, the Syndicate still retains ownership of it until I exceed 50% of the loan payments.

values: Syphus sends a warning, "There are rumors of debris from wrecked ships floating in from beyond the system edges here. Take care that your own ship doesn't turn out that way."
"I've heard other pilots talk about aliens showing up in this system." Syphus pauses as something briefly registers on the radar. "But I've never seen them myself..."
Syphus sends a hail, "In my experience, Mutiny doesn't cause much trouble. It's the other planet you have to watch out for."
"I usually don't get out past Gienah." Syphus seems nervous. "If you get disabled this deep in pirate territory, the rest of the galaxy probably won't come rescue you."
"Woohah!" Syphus exclaims. "I've never actually made it into Misam before. Some patrol pilots think this system is just a myth that doesn't actually exist..."
"That should be good enough. Patrol's over. Let's to head back to <destination>."
The <npc> was destroyed. Life is hard for Syndicate wage slaves.
Syphus hails you: "I'll wait in orbit. If the supervisor catches me loitering down there my pay will get docked!"

children.key: As you part ways with Syphus he says, "Any patrol you return alive from is a good one. Thanks for the escort."

name: Midnight FW Epilogue: JJ and Brother Greg
description: Transport JJ and Greg to <destination>.

children.key: While wandering the spaceport, a familiar voice calls to you from a nearby alley.

"<first>, it's really you! Finally, a familiar face!" Looking at the source of the voice, you see JJ and brother Greg dressed as independent traders. "I'm here on an undercover mission, but we need a lift to <planet>. Can you help us with that?"

JJ hesitates before answering, "Before you joined the Free Worlds, I arranged a large precious metals deal in case they were needed for funding the war effort. With the earliest government bonds maturing soon, the Free Worlds is going to need fresh funding. I came here to convert those precious metals back into credits. Brother Greg joined me to help negotiate that exchange."
Brother Greg responds, "No, that actually went fine. The problem is our ship was stolen, leaving us stranded here."
"Thanks <first>!" You lead them back to the <ship>.

You and JJ exchanged war stories during the journey. Brother Greg had a few stories of his own to contribute. There were more than a few injured Navy and Militia crash survivors who arrived at the monastery seeking treatment. JJ salutes you. "Thanks again, <first>. I'll make sure you get bonus pay for your assistance." The Free Worlds deposits <payment> into your account.

name: Midnight FW Plasma Missile 2
description: A test ship with new weaponry is in orbit around <planet>. Fight and disable it (but do not board or destroy it!) and then land to give Barmy Edward feedback on its performance.

values: A test ship with new weaponry is in orbit around <planet>. Fight and disable it (but do not board or destroy it!) and then land to give Barmy Edward feedback on its performance.

children.key: You received a message recently from Barmy Edward, asking you to stop by the Kraz Cybernetics facility to help test a new weapon. Do you want to visit them now?

You find Barmy Edward studying what appears to be a Meteor Missile that's been painted purple. "Thanks for coming. We're under pressure to give the Free Worlds something to keep pace with recent advancements in Republic technology. I've decided to push forward on a previous proposal that was rejected for being too risky...

Barmy clears his throat. "Well, that was a long time ago, before the war. But since management is looking for a quick solution, I think it'll be accepted under the circumstances. That's where you come in." He gestures at the missile. "Plasma Missiles. The component chemicals are inert until impact, at which time they are compressed together resulting in a plasma explosion. We've outfitted the Doombat with them. We'll need you engage in combat against it. As before, make sure you don't destroy it. Return here and we can review the results."
"Sorry, this sounds a bit too risky. I'd rather not be involved in this sort of testing."
"I knew I could count on you! I've waited so long for this day..." Barmy seems eager to get started.
Barmy Edward thanks you for traveling all the way out to Rust. However, testing on Plasma Missiles was completed without your assistance.

values: You've landed on <planet>, but you have not disabled the <npc> yet. Disable it before returning.
Assisted Barmy Edward with another weapon test: this time, missiles that cause a plasma explosion on impact. They might work best when combined with other plasma weapons.

children.key: You head to the hangar to meet up with Barmy Edward, and find him tinkering with the missile you saw earlier. "So, what did you think?"
"The Inferno Rockets used by pirates are more terrifying."
"It's a simple upgrade, isn't it? I suggested making them a year before the war started but management thought selling them was too risky. The on-going war has caused them to reconsider."
"When will it be available for sale?" you ask.

"True, but the heat generated from any that do get through will also aid the infrared trackers for subsequent missiles. Being able to deliver a plasma explosion from such a distance will make the enemy more vulnerable to Plasma Cannons and Flamethrowers once they engage at closer range."
"That is an interesting point," you say. "Are they available for sale yet?"
"Hmph. I came up with my idea first. Their rockets are unguided and if they hit anything too close are likely to overheat the ship firing them as well."
"I guess that makes sense," you say, "Are you going to be making them available for sale?"
"Once we have production going we should have them for sale in a month or so," he says. "Thanks for your help." You say goodbye and head back to your ship.

children.key: You finally arrive at <planet>. Diana opens her bag and pulls out something dangerous...
"Shield Suppressor?" She looks at the outfit in her hands. "I thought these were some kind of modified shield generator..." It figures she wouldn't know the difference.

"These devices are used for sabotaging a shield generator. Every outfitter has a sign warning new pilots to get rid of it if they find one installed on their ship." Is this really the loot she wanted to share?
"You can keep them. All of them."
"Get these off my ship right now."

"I'm sorry <first>, I really didn't know..." Diana seems to be holding back tears as she stuffs the Shield Suppressor back into her bag, then leaves. It might be a good idea to check your ship in the outfitter, just in case one got left behind.
A short while later you receive a video message from Diana: "So, <first>, the people I was supposed to meet turned out to be pirates..."
"While talking with them your name came up..."
"And now they want you to pay them the half billion credits I left you or they'll make me a slave..."
"Alright. Just tell me where to meet them and I'll be there."
"You got into this yourself, so deal with it yourself."
"What? Are you serious? Come on <first>! I really need your help here! These pirates aren't playing around!"
"Please don't joke like that! Come on <first>! I'm begging for your help here! These pirates are really dangerous!"
"That's not funny! Come on <first>! I really need your help! These pirates are no joke!"
"You can't be serious! Come on <first>! These pirates aren't kidding around! You're my only hope!"

"You'll save me? Thanks <first>! I'm being held aboard an old city ship called the <npc>. They want you to meet them at <waypoints>." She never asks if you actually have the credits. This is definitely a trap. You won't need to have half a billion credits, but being prepared for a fight is essential.
The <npc> is waiting for you, as indicated. It sends a hail, "Greeting Captain <last>. Did you bring the half billion credits?"
"No, I'm hoping to collect a bounty on you instead."
"Get real. She's not worth that much."

One of the pirate crew whispers something in the other captain's ear. He turns and yells, "What? Find her!" The pirate crew can be heard arguing amongst themselves in the background, their negotiation with you already forgotten.
You cut them off and prepare to fight. Hopefully Diana is safe. To rescue her, you'll have to board the <npc> and defeat its crew without destroying it first.

The battle was suspiciously easier than you expected and it isn't long before you find Diana hiding in the cooling ducts. Her backpack is noticeably empty. She grins and says, "Thanks for coming to rescue me <first>! I managed to stick those suppressor thingies all over the ship while they were distracted by you. When the shields stopped working, they started blaming each other..." With Diana safely in your custody, you should head to <destination>. name: Pandora's Problems 1

values: The Syndicate has supposedly been secretly keeping an alien ship for their experiments at a facility named Pandora's Box. When a reporter tried to reveal the contents of this facility, it was empty.

children.key: A crowd has gathered at the bar watching a special news program:

"This is Harold Riviere reporting live from the hangar rumored to be Pandora's Box, a facility where the Syndicate supposedly has been secretly keeping an alien ship for their experiments. After months of investigating we've finally located this place and are here to give you an inside look into what the Syndicate is hiding within." Harold pushes his way through a door and the cameraman follows. Alarms can be heard in the distance. "Our operatives are keeping the security guards distracted so that we can bring you this exclusive video." Harold passes by an abandoned security checkpoint. The camera zooms in on a laser rifle sitting on a tripod, then shifts to a heavily fortified doorway. "We managed to get the entry password for this doorway from an informant. This information didn't come cheap." Some beeping sounds can be heard as Harold enters the password, but the camera is focused on Harold's determined facial expression rather than the number pad. There is a click and the doorway starts to open. "This is it folks! The contents of Pandora's Box lies beyond this door..."

The crowd in the bar waits with baited breath as the camera zooms past Harold's shoulder to the opening doorway beyond. The room is dark, but soon lights from above begin to illuminate the area. The lights reveal...
"It's... empty?" The camera catches a glimpse of Harold looking around in confusion before being knocked violently to the floor as the video feed is cut off!
The display switches to a nervous anchorwoman who apologizes for "technical difficulties" then cuts to a commercial break.
The crowd bursts into a cacophony as suddenly everyone has an opinion on what was just witnessed.
"This was probably just a publicity stunt."
"Pandora's Box? It's a hoax if you ask me."
"I'd bet Harold is being arrested right now."
"Nah, I'm guessing this is fake news."
When the commercial break is over, the news program has moved on to another topic. No mention is made of what happened to Harold or Pandora's Box...

name: Star Explorer Fan Tour
description: Escort the <npc> through the systems marked on your map. Be prepared to engage in mock battles with 'aliens'. Once all of the systems have been visited, return them safely to <destination> for <payment>.

values: Escort the <npc> through the systems marked on your map. Be prepared to engage in mock battles with 'aliens'. Once all of the systems have been visited, return them safely to <destination> for <payment>.

children.key: You notice a long line of strangely dressed passengers waiting to board one particular ship.

"It's a cruise for fans of Star Explorer, an old Earth science fiction show," one of the people waiting in line exclaims. You find it hard to believe that all these costumes came from the same show. Some fans are dressed in simple black pants and shirts of various colors while others are wearing elaborate battle armor and make-up.
Before the rabid fan can begin talking your ear off about the show, the ship's captain approaches and asks, "Excuse me, would you happen to have a pilot's license?"
"Uh, yeah... Do you need a pilot?"

"As a matter of fact, our escort cancelled on us and we're in urgent need of a replacement. Just accompany us to <waypoints>. We'll be engaging in mock battles with 'aliens' flying some custom painted Blackbirds. Of course that's just for show, so make sure not to destroy them. We'll return here when we're done. Oh, and of course we'll need protection in case real pirates show up."
"That's too bad. Sorry for wasting your time." He walks off to continue his search for a licensed pilot."

Orchestral music plays as a message from the Star Explorer's captain is transmitted, "This is Captain Tim Smirk of the Last Frontier. The Star Explorer wasn't just a work of fiction. It was an ancient space exploration vessel from the early days of Hyperspace travel. Its design was heavily influenced by an old Earth science-fiction show with the same name as a marketing gimmick to entice young people to leave Sol and risk their lives exploring the vast unknown. Of the few that haven't been lost or destroyed, there are some still being used as actual science and exploration vessels. We'll be traveling to <waypoints> in search of new life and peaceful civilizations as we explore in the Last Frontier. But beware! The dreaded Grabons could attack us along the way! Rest assured I will endeavor to keep us safe along with our escort, Captain <first> <last> and the <ship>." Apparently that was an address meant for the passengers. Nice touch, adding your name at the end.
