name: Turner Inc.: Hai Power 7
description: Escort the <npc> to <destination>.

children.key: You find the <npc> parked behind the abandoned warehouse mentioned in the note. There aren't any guards, but marks on the ground indicate other ships were parked here recently.
Exploring the ship, there's no one aboard, but you find that the prototype fission reactor is still installed.
Exploring the warehouse, you find the hostages watched over by pirates!
Your crew fights bravely. Unfortunately, a stray bullet finds its way into your vital organs.
Your crew overpowers the pirates! You rescue David and his crew then leave.
The pirates take your money and add you to their captured hostages. "You lot are going to be sold at the slave markets."
"Wait, don't you know who I am?"
The pirates look at each other in confusion. "No. Should we?"
"Oh yeah?" Their leader turns to another pirate. "Are there any bounties on this one?"

The other pirate reads some info off of a data pad, "Sixteen offers to capture alive. Lowest is five hundred thousand credits and highest is eight hundred thousand credits. But we can only claim one."

Looking at his data pad, the other pirate answers "Fifty three offers. The lowest is one hundred thousand credits and highest is four hundred thousand credits. Altogether, about ten million credits. We just have to record it."
Their leader smiles as another pirate pulls out a video recorder.

The leader cuts your throat open in front of the camera and exclaims, "I'm the pirate that killed <first> freakin' <last>!" The sound of his maniacal laughter is the last thing you hear as you bleed out.
You eventually get sold as a slave working latrine duty for an illegal zoo stocked with exotic animals. Your days traveling the stars are over.

You step forward into the pirates field of vision. "Intruder!" They draw their weapons and open fire. You take a deep breath and activate the Quantum Keyblade just in time to let the barrage of bullets phase through. The confusion and panic of pirates upon seeing this gives you an opening to strike down the closest of them. Seeing this, some of them flee while others try shooting you again. You manage to quantum shift before the bullets strike. The few pirates who didn't run away earlier turn tail to escape.

You finish off the terrified pirates before releasing the captives. David eyes the Quantum Keyblade. "I'd heard rumors about the Quantum Keyblades, but after seeing one in action I have a better understanding for why the Hai consider it one of their greatest treasures."

You let the pirates run away and deactivate the Quantum Keyblade. The fight left you winded. After taking a moment to catch your breath, you release the captives. David eyes the Quantum Keyblade. "I'd heard rumors about the Quantum Keyblades, but after seeing one in action I have a better understanding for why the Hai consider it one of their greatest treasures."

You remotely activate T.H.O.R. A minute passes without anything happening. Then it suddenly crashes through the main entrance! The pirates shoot at it but their weapons have no effect on T.H.O.R.'s armored plating. T.H.O.R. uses it's Tactical Laser Rifle to snipe each pirate with surgical precision. None of the captives were harmed. As you are releasing them, David remarks, "You have a T.H.O.R. test model? I guess your connections with the Free Worlds has some extra benefits."

You allow Midnight's Lost Orphan to exert its full influence on the pirates. After a few moments, they start arguing among themselves. The arguments give way to violence and a firefight breaks out! Eventually, only one pirate remains. You easily shoot him in the back. Some of the captives were caught in the crossfire. Fortunately, David Turner was unharmed. "Thanks for the save." Shocked and bewildered, he looks upon his blood splattered crew members. "Such senseless violence. I don't understand what came over the pirates. Despite the criminal nature of their work, they seemed like professionals until just a few moments ago."

values: David thanks you for rescuing him and his crew.

name: Midnight Korbschläger 1
description: A Navy Gunboat named R.N.S. Hongshui has been harassing our patrols at <waypoints>. Drive them off or capture the ship without killing the crew if possible. Destroy them only as a last resort. Payment is [<payment>].

values: A Navy Gunboat named R.N.S. Hongshui has been harassing our patrols at <waypoints>. Drive them off or capture the ship without killing the crew if possible. Destroy them only as a last resort. Payment is [<payment>].

children.key: A militia officer approaches you. "Captain <first> <last>! The militia is trying to hunt down a Navy Gunboat named R.N.S. Hongshui that has been harassing our patrols at <waypoints>. Any assistance you can provide would be greatly appreciated. Our objective is to drive them off or capture the ship without killing the crew if possible. We are only to destroy them only as a last resort. There's a <payment> reward for successfully completing this mission. Please pass the word on to any other militia pilots you meet.

values: Militia captain of the Korbschlaeger, an old Saber that is an unusual ship to find in the Militia. He has a deep hatred for the Republic.

children.key: You arrive at <waypoints> to find the R.N.S. Hongshui disabled and under heavy fire from a Saber named Korbschlaeger. This isn't the sort of ship normally used by militia pilots and captains...
A panicked voice answers. "We surrender! Please stop your attack!"

The Korbschlaeger continues it's brutal assault on the R.N.S. Hongshui showing no signs of relenting. Inevitably, a Javelin strike pushes the battered and broken Gunboat crew beyond any hope of salvation as it explodes in a ball of flames. The Korbschlaeger slowly turns towards you and sends a hail.
The hail is audio only. A man's gruff voice addresses you. "Better luck next time. The reward for the Hongshui is ours."
"You aren't like the other militia I've worked with."

The man doesn't hesitate to reply. "We are at war. I think you'll find that Republic scum won't be so merciful when you find yourself at their mercy. Captain Mensur signing off." The Korbschlaeger cuts the connection and leaves the system.

The man laughs. "I signed up after the war started just for the opportunity to kill Republic scum. Make sure you stay out of my way if you don't want to get caught in the crossfire. Captain Mensur signing off." The Korbschlaeger cuts the connection and leaves the system.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Midnight Korbschläger 1

name: Midnight Korbschläger 2

values: The anarchists of the Outer Rim have a hatred for the Republic that started long before the formation of the Free Worlds. It seems some of them might have joined the Militia.

children.key: You spot an oddity among the other militia and Free World ships. It takes a moment before you realize it's the Korbschlaeger. Captain Mensur must have upgraded his ship since your last encounter. A Republic Rainmaker flees the system and the Korbschlaeger pursues them despite the orders to let them flee.

A merchant ship speaking on an open line remarks, "That was savage. The Korbschlaeger mercilessly destroyed a pair of Navy Outriders before leaving to chase that Rainmaker. The captain must be from the Outer Rim."
"The anarchists of the Outer Rim have a hatred for the Republic that started long before the formation of the Free Worlds. It shouldn't be too surprising that some of them might join the Militia."

name: Oathbreaker Strategos Deployed

values: Captain of the Strategos class Navy super carrier "R.N.S. Poisonwood." The first of its kind, the ship will be stationed in the Dirt Belt due to a resurgence of pirate activity there.

children.key: There's a broadcast playing at the bar. They're showing the deployment of the Strategos class Navy super carrier, "R.N.S. Poisonwood." The first of its kind, the ship will be stationed in the Dirt Belt due to increased pirate activity there.
There's a low whistle. A spectator in the crowd comments, "The war might've gone differently if the Navy had a few of those in their fleet."
Another one quips, "I'll bet the real reason they're deploying to the Dirt Belt is to keep the Free Worlds in check."
Someone else notes, "Even the name Poisonwood refers to that one southern planet that refused to leave the Republic."

As the ceremonial wine bottle is about to break over the hull, the captain, Marcus Junius, is asked to comment. "I look forward to a successful campaign." The red wine splatters across the ship's pristine hull.

children.key: You've just finished parking your ship in a hangar when you hear a loud commotion outside. A fleet of Oathbreaker ships has just landed and the locals are stocking them with supplies.
(Lay low and keep your head down until they leave.)

As you cower in your ship, someone knocks on the hatch. Then the voice of Arnold Benedict booms over external loud speakers. "Militia Captain <first> <last>, disembark unarmed and surrender yourself. Or does the hero of the war intend to cower inside that miserable tin can indefinitely?"
(Call upon the terrifying power of Midnight's Lost Orphan.)
As soon as you open the hatch, a firing squad bathes you in hellfire.
The entity does not respond. Perhaps it is gorging itself on your own frustration...
The glittering blade shines in your hand. Inhaling deeply, you activate the Quantum Keyblade before floating out of the <ship>. You are immediately bathed in hellfire...

You deactivate the Quantum Keyblade. Perhaps you held onto a silver of hope to dodge the remaining bullets and cut down the nearest soldier. Unfortunately, there are too many to dodge and you crumple under their relentless fire.
The laser fire and sniper fire are staggered, never relenting. Captain Benedict has trained these troops well. You are having difficulty holding your breath...

You try to return to the <ship>, but you've drifted too far from the hull... With your ability to hold your breath running out, you have no choice but to deactivate the Quantum Keyblade. Perhaps you held onto a silver of hope to dodge the remaining bullets and cut down the nearest soldier. Unfortunately, there are too many to dodge and you crumple under their relentless fire.

You fire up your engines and tear through the hangar doors. As you rise through the stratosphere your scanners show several of the Oathbreaker ships taking off in pursuit. This is going to be a bumpy ride!

name: Oathbreakers: Rum Cellar Fight
description: Visit <stopovers> to purchase a dose of stolen medicine for Magdalena's orphanage. Payment is <payment>.

values: Visit <stopovers> to purchase a dose of stolen medicine for Magdalena's orphanage. Payment is <payment>.

children.key: When you return to your ship, you find a nun waiting for you by the landing area.
"Yes. Do you need transportation off this hellhole?"
"I'd say no, but I don't feel comfortable lying to a nun."

She laughs. "Actually, I need a competent captain to retrieve something for me: stolen medicine that's being sold at <stopovers>. According to the registry, this is the <ship>. And that would make you Captain <last>. My name is Sister Magdalena from the Happy Hearth Orphanage. Would you please help me get this rare medicine for the children?"
"I assume you'll be paying me for this."
"Sorry, I don't want to be involved with stolen medicine."
"But it's for the children! Won't you please reconsider?"
"Fine. This had better be legitimate. Impersonating a nun is probably a sin."
"No way. Find someone else to do it."
"Of course I can pay. Is <payment> enough?"
"Thank you so much! Here are instructions for picking up the goods." She hands you a data chip. "I'll give you <payment> when you deliver the medicine to the orphanage."

"A pirate confessed to me about it while oh his death bed. He hoped passing on the knowledge would earn him some penance in the afterlife. If the medicine you bring me saves some children, I'm sure that penance was earned."

You follow the instructions Magdalena gave you and find the seller who has the stolen rare medicine she wanted. The seller confirms Magdalena deposited the payment and hands you a case of the goods. Everything is going smoothly when suddenly someone calls out...

"Well, well, if it isn't Captain <first> <last>, hero of the war!" The disheveled Navy uniforms on a pirate station tells you that you've crossed paths with a group of Oathbreakers. There are seven of them, probably the crew of a Gunboat.
(Wield the terrifying power of Midnight's Lost Orphan.)
There's no avoiding this fight. Unfortunately, the seven of them overpower you before you can fire a shot. They grab your Pilot's License as a trophy then toss you out of an airlock.
Before things turn violent, their captain orders them to stand down. He must have noticed that you have a crew of your own to back you up. The Oathbreakers glare at you as they stand aside.
There's no avoiding this fight. Your own crew tries to back you up, but a stray shot still finds its way into your vital organs.

There's no avoiding this fight. Your crew acts heroically, killing a couple of the Oathbreakers in the shootout while the rest flee. Not knowing if they've got reinforcements to back them up, you quickly board your ship and depart.

With a wave of your arm you ruthlessly flay their leader's skin from his body. As he writhes on the floor, screaming in agony, the other Oathbreakers draw their weapons and open fire. The beams and bullets bend around in mid-flight, returning to the ones who fired them. Amid their anguished tortured moans and final gurgling gasps of death, you calmly board the <ship> and depart.

There is an awkward pause as the small band of terrorists observe you drawing forth the Quantum Keyblade. Then they start laughing before drawing their weapons and firing. When the dust clears and they see you standing there, defiant, their confidence evaporates.
"Let me through and none of you have to die."
After hesitating a moment, the Oathbreakers reluctantly stand aside, allowing you to board the <ship> and depart.
You deactivate the blade and cut one of the Oathbreakers down! You strain to gasp fresh air before they open fire and you phase out just in time for their bullets and beams to pass...

You deactivate the blade and cut another Oathbreaker down! Unfortunately, you've relied on the blade for too long and are winded. While you gasp for air one of the Oathbreakers lands several hits, ventilating your body before you are able to phase out again. The new holes do nothing to help you breathe better.
You deactivate the blade and cut down the last of the Oathbreaker crew. Not knowing if they've got reinforcements to back them up, you quickly board your ship and depart.
You dive through a nearby wall and flee the Oathbreakers. After taking a detour, you manage to board your ship and depart.

values: It seems the Oathbreakers have access to the Rum Cellar on Chasm. This gives them a strong border base near the Free Worlds capital in Gamma Corvi.

children.key: You find the Happy Hearth Orphanage. It's a run down shack in a poor region of a pirate world. There are several graves nearby, probably children who succumbed to disease, starvation, or some other tragedy. One of the older children hands you a small box loaded with the <payment> for this mission while Sister Magdalena thanks you for delivering the stolen medicine. There's no time to celebrate as she gets to work administering it to the children who desperately need it. You almost feel guilty for taking this much money from them. Almost. The child who handed you the box says "It's okay. Magdalena's brother was a pirate. He saved up that money for emergencies like this."

name: Oathbreaker Pirate Gossip

values: Among the pirates there are rumors that Captain Arnold Benedict's flagship is of alien origin. A "Shield Fortress" that is described as having a huge wing span. It's officially named "Kornephoros" but many just call it the "Oath Breaker."

children.key: As you try to relax in the bar you hear someone mention the name of Arnold Benedict.
"It was really him! He looked just like he did on the holovideos," says a man with a scar on his face.
"What was he doing on <planet>?" asks a woman with a mohawk.
"Repairs and maintenance. A wanted fugitive like him fits right in on worlds like ours," replies the scarred man.
"I heard he has a fancy flagship," replies the mohawk woman. "What was it called again?"

The scarred man responds, "It's officially named Kornephoros, like the star system where the Republic and Free Worlds had one of their first big clashes. From what I've been told, all the Oathbreaker ships are supposed to be named after historical battles. But everyone I know just calls it the Oath Breaker."
Another man, one wearing a stereotypical pirate eyepatch, asks, "Is the Oath Breaker a carrier or a cruiser?"

"Neither," replies the scarred man. "He has some weird alien ship that was salvaged by Marauders before he confiscated it. One of their crew referred to it as a 'Shield Fortress'. They attached parts of a wrecked Navy Carrier to it, giving it a huge wing span. The thing is a beast of a ship. A real monster."

Eyepatch man downs his drink in one gulp and gets up to leave. The mohawk woman also excuses herself, despite the scarred man's offers of more free drinks. You should probably get going too. If either the eyepatch man or mohawk woman are bounty hunters, they may already be on their way to share this information on the Kornephoros, the Oath Breaker, to the authorities for a piece of the reward...

children.key: You've found the R.N.S. Poisonwood! It hails you: "Captain <last>, I assumed we would cross paths at some point. I should enjoy the challenge of fighting a war hero of your reputation."
"Why are you attacking the Free Worlds?"
"I didn't lose anyone close to me during the war, if that's what you're asking. The Oathbreakers are willing to carry on the fight. That is all."
"Just because they'll carry on the fight?"

"After years of rising through the ranks, I was given command over this elite warship. But the war ended before I could prove my mettle. Am I to spend my time in command parked on some obscure backwater system? Will my accomplishments be limited to policing petty smugglers and pirates? name: Nemesis: Oath Breaker
description: Defeat the main Oathbreaker fleet, then return to <destination>.

values: Defeat the main Oathbreaker fleet, then return to <destination>.

children.key: You've just taken a seat at the bar when suddenly you hear raised voices and shouting outside as pilots run for their ships: "The main Oathbreaker fleet has appeared over <planet> and is demanding tribute! The local militia has already been wiped out and the government of <planet> is requesting help from any combat-worthy ship at the spaceport to join the defenses!" Joining the battle could be an opportunity to finally put an end to Benedict's campaign of terror, but this could also be an easy way to get yourself killed.

You are the only pilot still on the ground as the battle rages overhead. "Want something to calm the nerves?" asks the bartender. He downs a shot before you have a chance to respond. A loud explosion goes off nearby and you swear to yourself as you look out the window. Your ship has just been hit by a stray missile! You rush outside to check the damage when a shadow falls over you... One of the Oathbreaker carriers is crashing into the spaceport. Flames are leaking from where you'd expect the fusion reactor would be located. There's no escaping the impending explosion. As the rapidly descending carrier deteriorates into a ball of fiery death, you idly wonder why you didn't take your own destiny into your hands up in the sky rather than cowering here on the ground.

The Oathbreaker flagship hails you: "I've called in reinforcements. There'll be no place for you to hide."

Captain Arnold Benedict is no longer able to terrorize the Free Worlds. Return to <planet> and claim your reward.

The government of <planet> thanks you for eliminating the Oathbreaker threat and rewards you with <payment>, the last of the reward money. With their leader gone, the remaining Oathbreakers will eventually fall apart.

Fought the main Oathbreaker fleet today. Arnold Benedict will no longer terrorize the Free Worlds. Some of his surviving followers will still need to be hunted down. I was rewarded with the last of the reward money, a meager 4,321 credits.

name: Oathbreaker expeditionary 1

children.key: Your warning alarm suddenly goes off! There is an Oathbreaker fleet in the system, but they aren't powering up their weapons. One of the ships hails you.

A woman speaks. "Good day to you, Captain <last>. I am Captain Magna of the Agincourt. We have not forgiven you. However, we are no longer interested in fighting. Not everyone in the Oathbreakers actually swore the oath. In actuality, only a few of the leaders and organizers did. The rest of us just happened to lose friends or family in the war and rallied to Benedict's banner. Eventually, those of us who were not prepared for the toll of fighting a war lost the will to fight. Unfortunately for us, we could no longer go home. When Benedict got his hands on some jump drives, he assigned us to these ships and ordered us to explore the region beyond the rim. We were uncertain of our future at first, but the Coalition has been very welcoming towards us. We will not start a fight with you in the presence of the Heliarch. And we advise you to grant us the same courtesy. Farewell."

values: Leader of an Oathbreaker expeditionary fleet in Coalition territory. This fleet is no longer interested in fighting and has settled into a peaceful life with the Coalition.

name: Skeleton Key North 1
description: Follow the pirates that took Tod to <destination>.

values: Follow the pirates that took Tod to <destination>.
event: midnight skeleton key north zero timer

children.key: This is the planet where you left Tod, the boy you rescued from pirates, to start his new job as a miner. Check to see how he is doing?
The labor department isn't very helpful. Citing employee privacy, they refuse to give you any information. As you head back to your ship, it seems someone who was also at the office is following you.
After turning a corner you break into a run, taking a roundabout course to get back to your ship. You managed to give them the slip. Whatever it is they were after shall remain unknown to you.
Your pursuer appears to be a miner. "You're a friend of Tod Copper, aren't you?" He stares at you with an uncertain expression.
"Yes, I'm his friend. Can you tell me where Tod is?"

With a look of relief he says, "We were ambushed by some thugs while on our way back to the dorms after our shift yesterday. From the sound of it, they were pirates who knew Tod. He bargained for them to spare us in exchange for guiding them to something they are seeking on <destination>. We reported this to our employer, but they aren't doing anything about it!" Thanking him for information, you are left with the decision of whether to rescue Tod once again.
You prepare for the journey to <planet>. Make sure to keep an empty bunk for Tod.

values: A battle between rival pirate gangs is taking place over Mutiny. Land on the planet and find Tod!

name: Skeleton Key North 2
description: Search for the pirate treasure at <waypoints>. Then take Tod back to his home on <destination>.

values: Search for the pirate treasure at <waypoints>. Then take Tod back to his home on <destination>.
You don't have space for Tod!

children.key: As you descend through the atmosphere, you notice a group of pirate ships has converged around a canyon near the equator. With no other leads, you set the <ship> to land nearby. Preparing for the worst, you open the hatch and walk into what could be an ambush.
(Sneak up on them by creeping among the rocks.)

You boldly walk through the canyon and find the pirates deliberating over a sealed crate. Despite your bravado, none notice you. Everyone is focused on the argument taking place between the captains of two different factions or too busy looting the dead corpses of a third faction.

You creep among the rocks, trying to stay hidden. As you slowly make progress, you can hear two men arguing. Risking a glance, you see all the pirates are gathered around a sealed crate. Any pirates not focused on the spectacle of the argument between the captains of their factions is too busy looting the corpses of a third faction.
Tod quietly approaches you and mouths, "Let's leave before they notice us."
One of the pirate captain yells, "How do we even know the treasure is in there?"
Tod tugs at your sleeve. He seems eager to leave.
The other responds, "This do be the crate what the boy done lead us to."
Tod tugs at your sleeve. He seems eager to leave.
"And where's that boy now?" asks the first pirate captain, looking around."

The other captain, suddenly aware of Tod's absence, yanks the lid of the crate open. "Empty!" The pirates all draw their weapons. "Find the boy! Find the treasure!" Turning to Tod, you notice he's already running off in the wrong direction, away from your ship!
(Wield the terrifying power of Midnight's Lost Orphan.)

As you move to follow, someone shoots you in the back! Collapsing to the ground, you bleed out, as the sounds of more gunfire and screams of anguish briefly enter your consciousness. The pirate's temporary truce has unraveled into a chaotic bloodbath. You notice with irony that you can no longer feel the pain from your wound. Your mind starts to wander, wondering why you're lying on the ground in this canyon or what your name is. Was it Tod? No, Tod is someone else. <first>? Maybe. Yeah, that's probably it. You smile in satisfaction at the name. At least you think you're smiling. Wait, are you smiling? Why? You're not really sure. The answers to these random questions no longer seem to matter as your existence fades into a dark realm of nothingness.

You fire at the pirate closest to Tod, allowing him to escape. As you do so, someone else shoots you in the back! Collapsing to the ground, you bleed out, as the sounds of more gunfire and screams of anguish briefly enter your consciousness. The pirate's temporary truce has unraveled into a chaotic bloodbath. You notice with irony that you can no longer feel the pain from your wound. Your mind starts to wander, wondering why you're lying on the ground in this canyon or what your name is. Was it Tod? No, Tod is someone else. <first>? Maybe. Yeah, that's probably it. You smile in satisfaction at the name. At least you think you're smiling. Wait, are you smiling? Why? You're not really sure. The answers to these random questions no longer seem to matter as your existence fades into a dark realm of nothingness.

values: used midnight orphan to rescue tod

children.key: You allow Midnight's Lost Orphan to exert its full influence on the pirates. Already agitated, they begin shooting at each other. The firefight doesn't last long and soon all the pirates have either died or fled. Fortunately, Tod was unharmed. He seems confused. "How... How did I survive that?"

You lead Tod through the canyon back to your ship. While walking he explains, "The crate's a decoy setup by the pirate captain you originally rescued me from. What they're really looking for is in my head."

He recites a string of numbers. It sounds like the scan setting for an Asteroid Scanner. "I didn't realize it before, but now I think it's some kind of mapping code. The pirate that took me off Placer said he wants the map to a treasure in <waypoints>."
Closing the hatch to your ship, you start up the engines. <waypoints> is on the other side of the galaxy.
"I could take you to <waypoints>, but the ride won't be cheap."
"I'll split the treasure with you. Once we have that, I'd like to return to my mom on <planet>." With that settled, you activate the engines and head for the stars.

values: Received a treasure map for the Gorvi system.

children.key: After scanning the frequency indicated by Tod's code, a non-descript chunk of rock lights up. Digging into the asteroid, you find a crate containing 10,000 credit chips and a small object that resembles a key. As you are studying the strange artifact, the scanner highlights another rock. Pocketing the key, you maneuver the <ship> towards the new asteroid. This one has 30,000 credit chips in it. Several more rocks are highlighted. After salvaging a few more, you've managed to collect 2,000,000 credit chips.
"We're rich <first>!" Tod raises his hand in the air expectantly.
You give him a thumbs up. Tod looks at you awkwardly. "Didn't they do high five's where you're from?"
"Oh, I remember seeing that in a movie once."
"I remember my teacher mentioned that in a lecture about old Earth customs."
"Well then, gimme five!" Tod stretches his hand higher up.
You raise your hand similarly and say, "Live strong in prosperity."
Tod looks at you awkwardly. As you start to wonder if you got Mr. Spork's catchphrase wrong, he asks, "Didn't they do high five's where you're from?"

You raise your open hand and Tod smacks your palm with his. Grinning, he lowers his palm and says, "Down low!" Before you can respond, the warning system goes off. A hostile ship is targeting the <ship>!
"Why is a bulk freighter attacking us?" Tod stares at the ship wide eyed.
"That's a Battle Barge, a heavy war ship used by pirates in the Dirt Belt." As you finish your explanation, the enemy hails you and a familiar voice speaks.
"You thought you done gave me and my boys the slip on Mutiny, did you? You done thought wrong."

Closing the communications channel, you get ready to fight when Tod asks, "Can't we just run? We've got enough treasure." Even if you escape, there's no guarantee these pirates will leave Tod alone in the future. Stopping them here is the best course of action.

values: You've eliminated the pirate flag ship. Hopefully that was enough to deter the rest from chasing Tod. Make sure he gets to <destination> safely!
[MISSION FAILED] You lost track of Tod! If life were a game, you could load a save file and try again.
The boy you rescued from slavers recalled a secret code that revealed the location of a pirate's treasure.

Found a strange key amongst some pirate treasure hidden in the asteroids of Gorvi. I've heard urban legends about three "Skeleton Keys" which unlock pirate treasure. Could this be one of them? Perhaps someday I'll eventually find the treasure it unlocks...
used midnight orphan to rescue tod

children.key: You were able to get in touch with Tod's mother before landing. As the <ship> touched down on the landing pad, Tod wastes no time opening the hatch and running out to greet her. You hand him his share of the treasure, giving them a million credits to make a better life for themselves. Despite the incredible haul, it's not entirely certain that you and Tod found all of the hidden treasure at Gorvi before the pirates interrupted your search. Perhaps it might be worthwhile to visit the system again with an Asteroid Scanner the next time you head north. After bidding them farewell, you stick your hands into your pockets and feel your fingertips brush against a rough hewn object.

You've arrived at <planet>. For some reason, you have the lingering feeling that you're supposed to be transporting a special passenger home. But no such person is aboard your ship. You sense Midnight's Lost Orphan is curious about something in your pocket, brushing any thoughts about what may have happened to your non-existent passenger aside. Reaching in, you feel your fingertips brush against a rough hewn object.

The key found in the first crate at Gorvi... You've heard urban legends about three "Skeleton Keys" which unlock pirate treasure. Could this be one of them? Perhaps someday you'll eventually find the treasure it unlocks...

name: Skeleton Key South 1
description: Visit <destination> and find out what happened to the Deadly Wager.

values: Visit <destination> and find out what happened to the Deadly Wager.

children.key: When you land, you are surprised to receive a message from Joe, the young man you transported from Smuggler's Den to Millrace to help his family escape their lives as pirate crew members. "Dear Captain <last>," he writes, "I didn't want to worry Maria, so she doesn't know I've written this letter. But I've learned that there may have been some kind of pirate rebellion on Smuggler's Den. While I don't regret leaving the pirates, I can't say we didn't have some friends among them. If you happen to visit Smuggler's Den again, could you please look up the crew of the Deadly Wager? It's the ship Maria and I were on. The captain and his officers were scum, but some of the regular crew weren't so bad. I don't know who else to ask, so I've decided to reach out to you."
This is where you met Joe and Maria. Most of the station occupants have either fled or are in hiding. Check the spaceport to see if you can find someone who has information on the Deadly Wager.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Skeleton Key South 1

name: Skeleton Key South 2
description: Find the <npc> near the Men system. Once you've learned the fate of its crew, return to <destination>.

values: Find the <npc> near the Men system. Once you've learned the fate of its crew, return to <destination>.

children.key: The spaceport seems like a ghost town. Hardly any ships are docked and you don't see anyone around. The silence is broken by the sound of glass being smashed.
Fearing rioters, you return to your ship and depart.
Rushing towards the sound of the broken glass, you find a vagrant looting a vending machine. As he gathers up candy bars and bags of chips, he eyes you warily.
"Easy now, I just want to talk."

The man immediately leaps towards you like a cornered animal. As the candy bars and bags of chips he was holding in his arms fall away, you see that he was holding a knife the whole time! You are impaled before both of you crash to the floor. "There's no justice here," he yells. The overwhelming stench emanating from him is the last thing to register in your mind as you lay there dying...
The man thinks a moment... then starts running!"
But the passages on the station are a labyrinth outsiders like you can easily get lost in. He effortlessly slips away in the dark tunnels...
The man thinks a moment... then tosses you a pack of Chocolate Num Nums. You catch it and rip open the wrapper. As you reach in, you say:
"Thanks. I'm looking for a the <npc>. Do you know it?"
"I love Chocolate Num Nums! By the way, are you from around here?"

He spits. "That damned Marauder Falcon! It's all their fault this is happening!" He nods towards a nearby viewport and a Hawk being chased by two Sparrows fly by, their red lasers briefly filling the chamber with a warm glow. "They lead the fleet that started this whole mess. Got heavily damaged in that first battle and ran away. But the fightin' didn't stop after they left." He grabs a few more things from the machine then runs off.
If they're heavily damaged, the <npc> might still be nearby...
You've found the <npc>. It is adrift and not responding to hails. You'll have to board it to get answers.

The crew aboard the <npc> are dead. Some escape pods are missing, so there may be survivors. But the captain isn't among them. Clutched in his hand with a death grip is some sort of key... You've heard urban legends about three "Skeleton Keys" which unlock pirate treasure. Pocketing the key, you wonder if this could be one of them.
Visit Joe on <destination> and let him know the final fate of the <npc>.

values: Joe used to be part of the crew aboard a pirate ship named the "Deadly Wager". While they didn't get along with the captain and his officers, Joe admits to having had some friends among the regular crew. Long after you helped Joe and Maria to freedom, the Deadly Wager started a pirate rebellion on Smuggler's Den. While some escaped, most of the crew died along with their captain.

After tracking down Joe's former pirate ship, the Deadly Wager, I found some sort of key... I've heard urban legends about three "Skeleton Keys" which unlock pirate treasure. Could this be one of them? Perhaps someday I'll eventually find the treasure it unlocks...

children.key: You find Joe and tell him what you found on the <npc>. "Hopefully, our friends are among the ones who got out alive." He looks at the key. "The captain once mentioned that this was the key to something hidden on an abandoned outpost in the Dirt Belt. But two other keys were also needed to unlock it. You keep it, <first>. You're more likely to find them than I am."

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Skeleton Key South 2

name: Skeleton Key Core 1
description: Locate a pirate raider named the <npc> in the uninhabited systems of the Northern Passage and board it to rescue Pookie. Then return her to <destination>.

values: Locate a pirate raider named the <npc> in the uninhabited systems of the Northern Passage and board it to rescue Pookie. Then return her to <destination>.

children.key: While walking through the spaceport you bump into a tall woman in a suit carrying a leash. Her face brightens up upon recognizing you. "I remember you! You're that transporter who took Pookie home that one time! Please, I need your help!" This woman is the "aunt" of Pookie the dog, one of your more memorable passengers.
"Nope. You must have me confused with someone else."
"Really? I could have sworn it was you..." The woman looks downtrodden as you walk away.
"So what do you want me to do about it?"
"Just yesterday!" That means Pookie was found sometime after you presented Puny to Pookie's owner.
"So what do you want me to do about it?"

"The kidnappers were on a pirate ship named the <npc>. They fled to the uninhabited systems of the Northern Passage, those empty systems stretching south from Alnitak. I've reported this to the authorities, but they won't devote resources to rescuing a dog. Please help!"
"I can pay 160,000 credits." That's not unreasonable...
"Wouldn't it be cheaper to just buy a new dog?"
"I tried looking, but none of the ones for sale look remotely like Pookie..." That's right, Pookie belongs to a different woman on Hestia. This one was just taking care of her.
"I tried looking, but none of the ones for sale look remotely like Pookie..." That's right, Pookie's owner rejected Puny based on the dog's appearance.

"Thank you so much!" She hands you the leash and starts reminding you about feeding schedules and other details that turned out to be irrelevant the last time you dealt with Pookie. "I'll be waiting for you on <destination>."
You've located the <npc>! Board the ship and find Pookie!

You demand to know what the pirates did with the dog they captured. One confesses that they sold it to a kennel on Stormhold in the Alcyone system. "Lots of cold hungry people there you know," he taunts you. "Maybe they already turned it into a nice warm stew..." The pirate rubs his belly and grins.

values: You have to rescue Pookie! Track down the <npc> and board the ship!

children.key: The crew of the <npc> sold Pookie to someone on Stormhold in the Alcyone system! Visit that world and rescue her!

children.key: Although most of it is uninhabited frosty wilderness, Stormhold is still a big world. Even if Pookie hasn't been eaten, there's no guarantee you'll be able to find her. As these thoughts go through your head, you find the kennel nearest to the spaceport and try your luck. As you open the door, your senses are assaulted by the smell of dogs kept indoors for too long and a chorus of random barking. Looking at the poor animals in cages, you see no sign of Pookie. It looks like you'll have to try somewhere else. You exit the kennel and begin trudging through the cold to the next one. How many kennels will you have to search through anyway?
Before you can dwell on that question for too long, a dog resembling Pookie runs up towards you! It wags its tail and rubs against your leg. You notice there's something in its mouth.

It's a human arm, severed at the elbow... It looks half frozen, as if Pookie dug it up from beneath the snow. Gripped in its hand is some sort of key. You've heard urban legends about three "Skeleton Keys" which unlock pirate treasure. Could this be one of them?

As you're thinking about this, Pookie decides to pee on your leg... Any doubts you may have had about whether or not this is really Pookie just got washed away. You quickly pocket the key and put her on the leash. Better get her back to <destination> before she vomits on anything.

children.key: You send a message to Joe informing him that you'd like his insight on where the abandoned outpost could be located in the Dirt Belt. He agrees to meet at a spaceport cafe. Perhaps he still hasn't told Maria about his request to look into the Deadly Wager.

After you settle in at a corner booth, Joe gets down to business. "Hope, in the Wei system is one possibility. But storing things there can be risky due to scavengers. My old captain tried to stash some gold there once. But when he went back later to retrieve some, it had already been pilfered.

Then there's Watcher, in Algieba. I've never been that far north myself, but from what I've heard the smugglers who use that moon to do their exchanges occasionally run into scientists doing research on the moon's wildlife. Finally, there are the two abandoned stations."

Joe nods. "Eureka Station in the Ipsing system gets a lot of smugglers too. The Deadly Wager would sometimes go there to provide backup if a client's trade went bad or to pick off an easy mark after they had finished their exchange."

"That would be Cadrelock Rock, a fuel waystation at Eber. Some pirates who don't have enough fuel tanks use it to get through the Dirt Tunnel." He sees your reaction to the term and clarifies, "That's pirate slang for the string of uninhabited systems stretching east of Wei. There's nothing special about it other than being an out of the way place to refuel. It's basically just a small docking bay with some fuel tanks and a ramscoop bolted to an asteroid. The Deadly Wager used it plenty of times."

Before Joe can say more, he receives a message. "Sorry <first>, I have to go. Maria needs me to pick up some things from the market for tonight's dinner. Good luck with your search." As he gets up he adds, "You've done a lot for us. I hope this information was able to help you."

children.key: As Joe described, Cadrelock Rock is a small docking bay attached to some fuel tanks and a ramscoop. But he didn't specify how huge these fuel tanks are. Most of it all is buried beneath the surface of the asteroid, making the waystation inconspicuous to anyone looking at it from a distance. Searching the area, you find three places to plug in the Skeleton Keys.
You hear the sounds of old machinery activating deep within the asteroid...
You hear the sounds of heavy metal sliding against metal deep within the asteroid...

A section of the wall retracts, revealing a passage leading farther into the rock. It leads to a concealed hangar, where a ship you're unfamiliar with is parked. At first glance, it resembles a Modified Aerie. But after a closer inspection, this is a heavier warship. The entry hatch is open.

Looking through the halls and rooms, it appears that no one is aboard. While searching the ship's computers, you find data files about it. This is the Starcadia, a Deep Security prototype Volary that was in development near the end of the Alpha War. The Starcadia was stolen before the Volary design could be finalized for mass production. The blueprints are on file and you can see that the technology on it is a bit dated. However, this was a cutting edge ship for its time, easily surpassing the Navy Frigate.
You put away the Skeleton Keys. The secrets of Cadrelock Rock will have to wait for another day...
Do you want to see the Volary again?

children.key: As you exit your ship, you are greeted by officers from Deep Security. A man steps forward and addresses you. "<first> <last>, wecome to <origin>. We couldn't help but notice that you've arrived flying a stolen ship."
"I didn't steal it. I found it abandoned."
"Don't you have a statute of limitations for that?"

"Of course you didn't steal it. The Starcadia was stolen long before you were even born. Most people wouldn't recognize it today. Still, Deep Security would appreciate the opportunity to study that Volary. It was originally our ship, after all."

"You have a point. The Starcadia was stolen long enough ago that most people wouldn't recognize it today. Still, Deep Security would appreciate the opportunity to study that Volary. It was originally our ship, after all."
"Don't you have the original blue prints?"

"The only copy of the Volary blueprints is in that ship's computer and was lost when the Starcadia was stolen. Don't worry, we'll let you keep this Volary. We are only interested in regaining the blue prints and checking if any modifications were done since it was stolen." While the officer is talking, a pair of Daggers pass overhead...

"Thank you for your cooperation Captain <last>." The officers call in a tech team and they retrieve the blue prints. While doing so, they make additional scans of the <ship>. Satisfied with their data, they release you.

You slam the entry hatch shut and begin preparations for lift off. Most of the officers are clearing away from the landing pad, but the one you were talking to is calmly speaking into his communicator... Your radar shows a pair of Ravens is targeting you.

"We were trying to get through the Dirt Tunnel, that string of uninhabited systems on the southern edge of the Dirt Belt. But we got low on fuel. It seemed that we'd be stranded for a while, but one of the crew spotted some sort of structure built into an asteroid. After getting a closer look, we realized it was a hidden refueling station! We docked and started filling our fuel tanks."
"Did a malfunction cause the fuel to explode?"
"Did one of the crew light a cigarette near the fuel?"
"No, the damage wasn't caused by a fuel explosion. Just as we were finishing up, a pirate Sparrow found us!" The damage to their ship seems more severe than you'd expect from a single Sparrow.

"We could have handled a single Sparrow. But this one had friends. It turns out that the station is maintained by pirates! They called it 'Cadrelock Rock' and said we had invaded their turf. They wanted a bribe, but we didn't have enough credits. It was a miracle we were able to get out of there in one piece."
"We were more focused on getting out alive than maintaining our maps... But I'm fairly sure it was in Eber."

children.key: You are approached by a cyborg. It speaks to you with a mechanical male voice, a hint of the person buried underneath the external machinery. "YoU aRe <first> <last>, CaPtAiN oF ThE <ship>. YoU HaVe ExPeRiEnCe HaCkInG dRoNeS. wE hAvE a JoB fOr YoU." You notice it speaks differently when it says the name of you and your ship...
You hear a series of beeps and clicks before it responds, "YoU wIlL tRaNsPoRt OnE tOn Of HaCkInG eQuIpMeNt To ChEcKpOiNt Tertio In ThE Mirfak SyStEm. OnCe ThErE, tHe EqUiPmEnT wIlL dO tHe ReSt."
There is another series of mechanical sounds before it responds, "CoMpEnSaTiOn WiLl Be OnE mIlLiOn CrEdItS." Big jobs have big rewards.
"That's not enough. I want a share."
There is another series of mechanical sounds while it considers your counter offer. After several minutes of this, it suddenly speaks, "We AcCePt. YoU wIlL gAiN a ShArE oF tHe PrOfItS."

The cyborg stands motionless after you ask that question. There are no clicks, beeps, or other sounds of internal machinery. Just silence. He struggles to speak, saying with a normal, but tortured, voice, "Th... thank you! Mm... my name... is..." But he never gets a chance to finish the sentence. The machinery suddenly fails, with circuits catching fire sending sparks, smoke, and blood spraying from his joints! His body collapses, the artificial limbs and organs falling apart in a heap of blood soaked metal, rubber, and plastic. Whatever job his masters intended for you to do will have to be taken up by someone else.

The cyborg loads the equipment onto your ship. "Do NoT lEt LaW eNfOrCeMeNt CaTcH yOu. AfTeRwArDs Go To <destination> aNd DiSpOsE oF tHiS EvIdEnCe." The cyborg gestures towards the equipment then leaves, never giving you its name.

"UnAcCePtAbLe. BuT wE wIlL fInD sOmEoNe ElSe." There are a series of beeps before the cyborg suddenly explodes, incinerating you and anyone else who might have been close enough to listen in on your conversation.

"Investigators have evidence that Third String Incorporated has been involved in hacking Checkpoint Tertio and influencing the outcomes of Tertio League races." "Third String's accounts have been frozen and anyone tied to them will be apprehended." That's not good. The Syndicate authorities probably have you on their list. You'd better wrap up whatever business you have here and leave. Soon.

children.key: Some men in suits approach you. "This grand space faring vessel is the <ship>, which would indubitably make you the one and only Captain <last>. We come to you on this fine day, to extend a formal invitation to a very exclusive and elite private business meeting with our most esteemed boss, Mister Al Cologne." It would appear you've attracted the attention of the local mafia. "We strongly advise you not to turn down this very fortunate of opportunities our boss has chosen to grace you with." They probably want you to do something highly illegal...
(Skip the small talk and just start blasting.)
(Skip the small talk and just start blasting.)
(Wield the terrifying power of Midnight's Lost Orphan.)

They start to lead you down a side street. As you pass the entrance to a nearby alleyway, you break away make a run for it. You seem to be making good progress, but then a shot rings out and you no longer have the strength to keep running. Strange. Sure, they shot you in the back so it was impossible to dodge. But a single shot? Low level henchmen never had such good aim in the movies. Such are your last thoughts as death claims you...
You draw your weapon and open fire. You manage to take down a few mafia men, but the rain of bullets is impossible to dodge and you go down in a bloody heap...

You will the Orphan to make the their blood flow backwards. The mafia men scream in agony as their blood vessels rupture, causing them to collapse into a pile of bloody flesh. The horrible scene fills you with a depraved delight which a rapidly shrinking part of your mind recoils from in revulsion...
You take a deep breath and activate the Quantum Keyblade as the mafia men draw their guns and open fire!
You let the bullets pass through, then deactivate the blade and cut one of the mafia men down! You strain to gasp fresh air before the next burst of bullets hits and you phase out again...

You let the bullets pass through, then deactivate the blade and cut one of the mafia men down! Unfortunately, you've relied on the blade for too long and are winded. While you gasp for air the next burst of bullets strike, ventilating your body before you are able to phase out again. The new holes do nothing to help you breath better.

values: The head of a mafia organization. He had a business proposal for me but I didn't stay around to hear what it was.

children.key: You dive through a nearby wall and flee the mafia men for the safety of your ship. Once you are safely aboard, you make an emergency launch and leave <origin> behind.
"Oh? Is that so?" You feel the barrel of a gun nudge your back...

The mafia men escort you to a large manor. After passing though a well tended garden, you arrive at a patio where an aged man in fine robes is enjoying what appears to be a meal of roasted Rock Scavener. He cuts off a piece and gulps it down as you approach. "Ah, if it isn't the great Tertio Champion, <first> <last>, here in the flesh! Welcome! Welcome. Have a seat and I'll get the maids to bring out a plate for you." He extends his hand towards you...
"Thank you. But why am I here?"
"No thank you. Why am I here?"
"I'm busy. Why did your goons drag me here?"

"No thank you?" He pulls his hand back, scowling. "What? You think you're too good for my hospitality? Huh!?!" He picks up his knife and stabs it into the roast. "A man welcomes you into his home and generously offers you the privelege of partaking in the good Lord's bounty for which he has shed his own blood, sweat, and tears for. YET THIS IS HOW YOU REACT!?!" He picks up a wine glass and takes a sip before sighing. "The kids, they have no respect these days."
"I'm sorry Mister Cologne, but why am I here?"
"I'm not hungry. Now, why am I here?"

"You got chops on you kid!" He starts cutting a fresh slice off the roast. Blood gushes from the charred outer crust as the blade sinks into the pink flesh. "But that's probably why you were able to scrape your way to the top." He bites into the roasted meat and some of the juice runs down his chin. Wiping it away, he leans back and sizes you up.

"Why?" Cologne pauses and allows the silence to hang in the air. "Why? Why? Why? Tell me, <first>... Do you mind if I call you <first>?" Without pausing to hear your answer he continues on. "Why do you race? Is it for pride? Honor? Prestige?" This time, he waits for an answer.

values: The head of a mafia organization. He had a business proposal for me but after some discussion he seemed to think that I'm too idealistic and changed his mind.

children.key: "That's very idealistic of you." A maid walks in carrying a fresh plate. He waves her away. "But I don't think you're the pilot I'm looking for after all." He raises his glass towards you. "I think you'll find that your future in the Tertio League will be especially challenging. Escort the good captain out fellas." The men who brought you here take you back to the spaceport.
Cologne starts laughing. "I think I'm going to like having you work for me kid!" He gulps down the rest of his wine. "Together, we'll make loads of money. It'll be easy work."

"Nothing complicated. From now on, whenever you win first place in the Tertio League, I want you to take last place in the qualified rankings of the following Tertio race." He wants to be able to control where each pilot ends up in the final rankings. You'll still have to do well enough to be ranked, so getting disqualified isn't an option. But by having you take last place in every race after you win first, he'll be able to profit from making bets based on that knowledge. For your cooperation, a portion of the gambling winnings will make its way into your account.
Cologne laughs, but then notices from the expression on your face that you're not joking.

values: The head of a mafia organization. He has worked out a gambling scheme that will be mutually beneficial if you lose certain Tertio League races on purpose.

children.key: "Perfectly timed," Cologne exclaims as a maid walks in carrying a fresh plate which she sets on the table for you. "Go on." He gestures to you. "Have a seat. We're partners now." You take your place at the table...

You are shot in the back as soon as you reach for your weapon. Knowing when you've been outplayed is an important survival skill. Unfortunately, this is the last life lesson you learn before you pass away.

children.key: When you arrive at Lionheart's shipyard the manager greets you. "Welcome! Captain <last>, we at Lionheart are impressed with your Tertio League victory and would like for you to pilot the Accelerator." The manager presents you with the Modified Flivver you saw in the invitation. "This Flivver has been specifically modified to meet the stringent Tertio League weight requirements." A technician shows you its specs. The ship is lighter and more maneuverable than a Sunracer. In order to accomplish this, it no longer has a Hyperdrive and the hull is made from more fragile materials. To help protect the ship, the Accelerator has been outfitted with stronger shield emitters. "How about it, would you like to pilot the Accelerator?"

"Nothing at all!" The manager explains, "We'll be the ones paying you 500 credits for every day you fly the Accelerator. A Tertio Champion piloting it will help support our ad campaign for the Flivver."
"Wait, so it's not to promote the Accelerator?"
"Do I have to use it while racing?"
"Unfortunately, the Accelerator is just meant to be used as a promotional model. Ideally, you would use it to compete in the Tertio League. So how about it?"
"That would be ideal. But just using it for normal flying is fine too. Just don't leave it parked. We're paying for the ship to be seen in use by you. So how about it?"
"Wait, so it's not to promote the Accelerator?"
"Do I have to use it while racing?"
"Great! We'll have it shipped to Sunracer. Head over there when you're ready to receive it."
"That's too bad. Please let us know if you want to buy something. Our sales clerks will be happy to help you." The manager leaves you alone on the sales floor.

When you leave the <ship> there is a camera crew waiting for you. A Lionheart representative arrives with the Accelerator in tow. They make a big show of publicly registering it to you. The photo op ends with the representative wishing you good luck on your next race.

name: Midnight Earth Retirement Inheritance
description: Travel to <destination> by <date> and participate in the funeral of Charles, who you previously transported to <planet> for retirement.

values: Travel to <destination> by <date> and participate in the funeral of Charles, who you previously transported to <planet> for retirement.
event: midnight earth retirement inheritance timer
An elderly couple you helped relocate to Earth for their retirement. They seemed to be under stress, abandoned by what Charles referred to as "spoiled brats".

children.key: Upon landing on <origin> you receive a message from Donna: "Captain <last>, I hope this message finds you well. Charles and I were very grateful for your assistance in helping with our retirement. Sadly, he passed away after becoming ill. If you can, would you please attend the funeral on Earth? It can't be held any later than <date>. I would appreciate your participation. I'm sure Charles would too."
While you weren't particularly close to Charles and Donna, apparently the short time you spent with them was very impactful to their lives. Earth is only a short distance away. What will you do?
You reply to the message with your RSVP and prepare for the trip to Earth.
You ignore the invitation to attend the funeral and delete the message.

You travel from the spaceport to the cemetery where the funeral will be held. Most of the graves are centuries old and only the extremely wealthy can afford to be buried instead of cremated. Donna, dressed in a black dress, greets you. The ceremony is open casket. The morticians did an excellent job with Charles. He doesn't look much different from how you remember his appearance the last time you saw him. "Thank you for coming Captain <first>." Donna is well composed. She is either out of tears or is holding them back for later. You don't see any other guests.
"Am I the first guest to arrive?"
She frowns. "Only one other will be attending. Thomas may seem rude, but please forgive him. He is paying for today's ceremony after all."

She smiles. "We were doing well the first few months after you brought us here. Charles and I actually enjoyed being retired at first. But then he fell ill. Thomas paid for the medical bills, but this only strained the relationship between him and Charles."

"Thank you." She smiles. "We were doing well the first few months after you brought us here. Charles and I actually enjoyed being retired at first. But then he fell ill. Thomas paid for the medical bills, but this only strained the relationship between him and Charles."

A black limousine approaches. The driver gets out and helps a man in a suit exit the vehicle. He carries the aura of a young corporate executive. This must be Thomas. He strides towards you and Donna, pausing briefly to regard Charles. Briefly glancing at you he addresses her. "Are you well mother?"
Thomas nods. After briefly taking in the scenery of the cemetery, he starts walking back to the limousine.
"Aren't you going to stay for the ceremony?"
Thomas snarls at you. "Mind your own business! I provided for them back home! Gave them a job! Paid the medical bills when he got sick! Paid for today's ceremony! Me! They should be grateful!"
"So you're one of the 'spoiled brats' Charles mentioned?"
Donna grabs your arm. "Let it go. Please." She starts to tear up.
The rear window of the limousine lowers and a young woman wearing an expensive looking gown and jewelry leans out. She calls out to Thomas. "Is this going to take much longer babe?"
Thomas doesn't hesitate to get back into the vehicle and they quickly depart, leaving you and Donna alone again.

"Sorry you had to see that." Donna apologizes. A short while later, the minister arrives and completes the ceremony. Before you leave, Donna hands you an envelope. "Thanks again for being here today. Please take this. It may not seem like much, but Charles wanted you to have it."

After returning to the <ship>, you open the envelope to find a Syndicate preferred stock certificate and a note from Charles: "Hello <first>. I know we only met briefly, but you were the last friendly face we saw on that miserable planet we called home. Truth be told, Earth isn't as horrible as we expected it to be. In some ways it's nicer. The people here aren't as pretentious and stuck up. I'm giving you this stock certificate that my father passed on to me. My son, Thomas, wouldn't appreciate it. He's already got everything he thinks he needs. But back when I was young, this certificate was a symbol that helped motivate me to keep working towards being able to build my own fortune. In the end, I never got there. Hopefully, you'll have better luck at it. Sincerely, Charles."

name: Titania: Syndicate Stock Vote

children.key: You receive the following message from Syndicate Financial Holdings:

As a holder of Syndicate preferred stock, you are qualified to vote on an important matter regarding the future direction of the Syndicate. With the changing economic landscape following the war between the Republic and the Free Worlds, our financial strategists have identified opportunities to push forward the Titania Station project in the Eteron system. In order to gain control of the Eteron system and complete Titania Station, shall the Syndicate issue ten year bonds valued at one billion credits with a five percent annual interest rate to be paid at maturity?

Searching for info on the hyperspace network, it seems that the Syndicate is asking for permission to fund the construction of a new space station in the Eteron system by borrowing money from outside sources that will be paid back with interest after ten years. The Eteron system is currently controlled by the Republic. Some of that money will probably be used to "persuade" Republic officials to transfer control of Eteron to the Syndicate.
You vote to fund the creation of a new space station in the Eteron system through the use of corporate bonds.
You vote not to fund the creation of a new space station in the Eteron system through the use of corporate bonds.

name: Titania: Syndicate Republic Bribery
description: Transport a Syndicate agent to <destination> by <date>. Do not let the authorities scan you.

values: Transport a Syndicate agent to <destination> by <date>. Do not let the authorities scan you.
In addition to the fine, the Syndicate agent is taken into custody.

children.key: As you walk through a secluded area of the spaceport, a man in a suit approaches you. He's carrying a briefcase handcuffed to his wrist. "Captain <last>, I presume? The Syndicate has need of your services."
"What does the Syndicate want with me?"

"You voted to go forward with the Titania project, did you not?" Titania is the name of the space station that the Syndicate wants to build in the Eteron system. "I've been assigned to help lobby for the Republic to transfer control of Eteron to the Syndicate. I need a competent starship captain to provide transportation for myself and this package to <planet>. Of course, we must avoid being scanned by Republic patrols. But getting caught by Syndicate Security could also cause problems. Can you assist me with this endeavor?" The man patiently waits for your response.
"How do I know you are who you say you are?"
"No, I don't want to be involved."

"Are you certain? Billions in corporate bonds have been issued and this is only one of several planned diplomatic lobbying missions, some of which have already been completed." His expression is grim.

"Very well, I respect your decision. Please excuse me." As you walk away you hear a gunshot. Warm liquid spurts from a hole in the back of your head and another hole in your forehead. Your corpse collapses to the ground, the source of the bullet already gone.

"I've been asked to maintain secrecy. If you don't want to trust me, I suppose I'll have to find someone else. But I must say, you are probably the most experienced starship captain in port right now."

"Financially? I suppose I can give out some pocket change. <payment> should be adequate. As a Syndicate shareholder, you'll benefit as well. Outside of finances, I'll make sure my superiors are aware of your assistance in this matter."
"No, I don't want to be involved."
"You've made the right choice." The man heads towards the <ship>'s landing pad...

values: You've become an enemy of the Syndicate after pushing their agent out of your airlock.
You've become an enemy of the Syndicate after their agent died while riding on one of your ships.

During the trip, the Syndicate agent doesn't speak much other than to express confidence in the future financial performance of the Syndicate. As soon as you land, he hands you a payment of <payment> and promises to tell his superiors of your assistance before heading towards Parliament.

illegal.message: In addition to the fine, the Syndicate agent is taken into custody.

name: Midnight Incipias First Contact Update
_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Midnight Incipias First Contact Update

name: Midnight Incipias Arcus Expedition 1
description: Escort the Arcus, a newly constructed transport-freighter to <system>.

values: Escort the Arcus, a newly constructed transport-freighter to <system>.
event: midnight incipias first contact update

children.key: You notice several new ships docked at the spaceport. As you look at them, an Incipias approaches you while flashing multiple colors. Clearly, it is trying to catch your attention.
You do your best to rush through the alien corridors of the station, but your feet cannot match the effortless gliding of your pursuer...
As you walk through the spaceport you notice an Incipias following you while flashing multiple colors. Clearly, it is trying to catch your attention.

The Incipias slows down as does the rate of its color fluctuations. Finally, the translator is able to interpret what it is trying to say. "Hello outer-traveler. Your assistance to our previous exploration vessel-ship has not been forgotten. We will be embarking on another voyage-expedition to <system>. Would you have any interest-curiosity to join us?"
"What do you want me to do?"
I don't have time for this right now."
"No, I am not interested in this."
The Incipias glows blue. "I understand. Perhaps next time." If slowly drifts way, it's lights dim...
The Incipias explains, "We will attempt a jump-shift to <system>. This time, we will use a vessel-ship that can carry enough crew and cargo to serve as the core for a colony-station."
"Looks like a good plan. I will participate."
"Sorry, I am not interested in this."
"Thank you. Our vessel-ship is a newly constructed transport-freighter: the Arcus. It is the first of it's kind-type. We hope it will not be the last."

values: event: midnight incipias first contact update

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Midnight Incipias Arcus Expedition 1

name: Midnight Incipias Arcus Expedition 2
description: Return the crew of the Arcus to <destination>.

values: Return the crew of the Arcus to <destination>.

children.key: Soon after arriving, you notice the Arcus appears different. It seems to have aged from years, perhaps even decades, of neglect. It hails the <ship>. The signal is weak, but stable enough for the translator to convey a message. "Greetings, I presume you are the outer-helper our progenitors would light of..." The signal stutters.

"... are not sure why, but after entering the space-between something surprise-unexpected occured. Our vessel-ship remained trapped there for two generation cycles. We used the supplies to sustain ourselves and our vessel-ship, but perhaps that may have only extended-prolonged the duration of our imprisonment..." The signal stutters again.

"... eventually the power systems briefly falter-failed. To our surprise-unexpected, the vessel-ship was released once its systems were no longer operational. Outer-helper, we ask that you return us to <destination> on your vessel-ship. We no longer have enough supplies or crew to..." The signal failes completely. It appears you will have to board their ship if you want to help them.

values: The few remaining crew light their gratitude. From what you can see, much of the ship has been repurposed to prioritize long term survival over normal operations.

children.key: The Arcuses crew are grateful to finally see the home of their progenitors. While conversing with them during the journey, you learned that they are what humans would consider grandchildren of the original crew of the Arcus. The actual cause of their multi-generational entrapment is a mystery, but the research data they brought back should help Incipias scientists progress closer to achieving safe FTL travel.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Midnight Incipias Arcus Expedition 2

name: Midnight Incipias Nimbus Expedition 1
description: Escort a Nimbus, to <system>.

children.key: As soon as you open the hatch of the <ship>, you find an Incipias outside flashing multiple colors. It gradually slows down before settling on a dull shade of green as it waits patiently for you to activate your translator.
"Hello. Do you need something from me?"

It slowly resumes flashing. "Welcome back outer-traveler. We are about to begin-start a new voyage-expedition to <system>. Would you have any interest-curiosity to accompany us?" The Incipias pauses, resuming a neutral shade of green.

"The Arcus was designed for missions to establish-create a colony-station. Our goal now will only-merely be to scout-explore <system> and test some modifications-updates to our interspace technology-device. It is our hope that you would be willing to assist if we encounter a surprise-unexpected occurence."
"I am not able to help this time."
The Incipias glows blue. "I understand. Perhaps next time." If slowly drifts way, it's lights dim...
The Incipias flashes several colors. "The crew will be pleased-excited to know that you will accompany them on this voyage-expedition. Thank you." It floats away, its lights bright.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Midnight Incipias Nimbus Expedition 1

name: Midnight Incipias Nimbus Expedition 2
description: Return to <destination> to inform them of the fate of the expedition to Il'le.

values: Return to <destination> to inform them of the fate of the expedition to Il'le.

children.key: The Nimbus you were escorting explodes as soon as it enters the system! Perhaps something went wrong with their experimental FTL drive... There don't appear to be any survivors. All you can do for them is return to <destination> and inform the station of their fate.

The Hicemus are troubled by the news of the destruction of the Nimbus sent to Il'le. The flashing lights of the ensuing conversation are too much for your translator to fully interpret, but it does catch mention of developing a stronger ship hull to help survive the journey between systems.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Midnight Incipias Nimbus Expedition 2

children.key: You receive a message from Charles Atinoda: "Good news! They caught the thief. Well, one of them anyway. He admitted to being part of a pirate gang called 'The Grave Diggers'. He kept saying 'Tell <last> that the Grave Diggers will get their revenge with what we found in the Graveyard.' I thought I should warn you."
You thank Charles for the warning. Maybe it would be a good idea to check the Graveyard again for Grave Digger activity.

values: The Grave Diggers had a base here, but it looks abandoned.
You've checked all the systems in the Graveyard. You should do a thorough search of the Grave Digger's base on <destination> in case they left behind any clues.
A derelict Pelican is asking for assistance. They were attacked by Ka'het.
A derelict Ibis is asking for assistance. They were attacked by Ka'het.
A Quarg Tiamat is searching the system.
You find a derelict Ka'het. That's not so unusual. The Ka'het do fight amongst themselves.
You find a derelict Ka'het. That's not so unusual. The Ka'het do fight amongst themselves.
You find a derelict Albatross. It appears abandoned. This might be something to investigate.

You find rusting salvaging equipment strewn across a beach on one of the tropical islands. Labels on the machines indicate they were manufactured on Millrace and sold by the Syndicate. From the markings in the sand, something big was dragged out of the ocean. Whatever it was is no longer here.

children.key: The ship has been stripped of its outfits. There are no signs of violent conflict and no remains of the crew. When you check the logs, most of the data was erased, but from what remains it seems they were investigating something submerged under the waters of Retilie.

The Grave Digger base looks abandoned. But before you leave, something catches your eye: an empty box of House Unuk chocolate covered acorn cookies. You're certain those didn't exist back when you fought Lu Bu...

children.key: When you exit your ship, one of Taely's assistants enthusiastically greets you. "Our scan revealed you have Builder Anti-Missiles on your ship! If you'd like more, we have a surplus in our salvaged inventory." She leads you to a storage room at the back of the salvaged outfits area. Hidden under dusty tarps is a sizable stock of the turrets. "We salvaged these long ago, but we found them so inferior to the Point Defense Turrets that none of our pilots want to use them. We'll have them moved to the sales area by tomorrow."

You thank her for the information. When compared to the Point Defense Turret, the Builder Anti-Missile is an archaic relic. Even the simplest Anti-Missile Turrets produced by Lovelace Labs have automated targeting systems. But other than requiring a crew member to operate the weapon, by human standards it still provides reasonable protection for an anti-missile turret of its size.

description: Escort the <npc> to <destination> to outfit it for escaping the Graveyard.

values: Escort the <npc> to <destination> to outfit it for escaping the Graveyard.

children.key: The upper atmosphere is covered in thick clouds. As you descend, a fierce blizzard obscures visibility. Suddenly something emerges from the storm. A Vareti'het, rushing to escape the blizzard collides with the Dreaming Solstice! The Pelican is no match for the larger vessel and careens out of sight into the swirling snowstorm. The Vareti'het continues on, unconcerned, its only objective appears to be an escape from the harsh weather. It takes all your effort to keep the <ship> under control as you make your landing.
The Dreaming Solstice isn't responding to hails...

You immediately take the <ship> back into the icy winds and begin a search for the Dreaming Solstice. Ionic lightning strikes the <ship> several times, disrupting its power systems, yet you press on. From above, the Vareti'het makes an unexpected reappearance and opens fire! Other Ka'het emerge from the swirling mists and join the attack. The <ship> tumbles out of control towards the frozen rocks below. In your last moments before dying, you see the Vareti'het disappear into the clouds above like an angel of death that has collected its toll...

Hours pass as freezing winds whip against the hull of the <ship>. After a long night, the storm abates and you realize the <ship> is half buried in the snow. You are warming the engines in preparation for dislodging the <ship> from its icy tomb when a hail comes in. "<ship>, are you alright?" It's Rysandel. "<first>, I am glad you and your crew survived. We were not so fortunate. Can you pick us up? The Dreaming Solstice didn't make it through the storm. Half the crew perished in the crash."
"Thank you," Rysandel signs, a hint of sorrow in his motions. "<origin> is a harsh planet. I'm transmitting our location to you. We await your arrival."
As the <ship> takes flight, you scan the frozen wastes below. Another ship lies half buried in the snow some distance from Rysandel's location. It isn't the Dreaming Solstice...

After rescuing the survivors, you investigate this other ship. It isn't the missing Starling that Rysandel was looking for, but the frozen remains of humans wearing Remnant style clothing are preserved outside of the ship. They must have been caught in a blizzard like the one you endured. They and the ship they found must have been hidden beneath the snow for centuries. Rysandel sees to the burial of the dead while you work on gaining entry into the ship.

It's some kind of mining ship, but it appears to have been partially modified. A lot of the preliminary work to convert this vessel into a light warship has already been done. Perhaps desperate survivors during the collapse of the Builder's civilization were responsible. Or maybe it was the frozen Remnant found outside. The truth of this mystery is lost to the passage of time.
Rysandel approaches you. "With the Dreaming Solstice gone, we are at your mercy."
"I need someone to pilot this ship."

Rysandel looks doubtful. "We could do that. But captain <last>, how do you plan to get it out of the Graveyard? I don't see a Quantum Key Stone on it. We can salvage the one in the wreckage of the Dreaming Solstice, but we lack the tools to install it."
"Fly this ship for me and you'll see."
Rysandel smiles. "I guess I will be working with you from now on."
After docking the Rao'xeris onto <planet>, Rysandel and his crew use the outfitter facilities to install the Quantum Key Stone onto it. <npc> is now ready to leave the Graveyard.

You have damaged the property of the great and powerful Garuk'athar Ik'or Tch'ikag, the five hundred and fifty sixth Navarch of the Kalishik'utar armada."
