As you start to lose interest it utters "Ring! Riing! Riiing! Pugga, mugga dugga. Hugga bugga? Tugga yugga, wugga sugga. Click." The pug lowers its wrist and turns to you. "You're a long way from home human. Why are you here?"
"I used a Quantum Bloodstone and a wormhole opened."
"I want to explore this region of space."
The Pug sighs. "Oh, the stolen wormhole borer... That's interesting. So do you not have a Bloodstone to go back?"
"I want to explore this region of space."
The Pug shrugs. "That's not something we keep in stock. But there might be a way to make them. You might even find alternatives if you look hard enough."

"I want to know about the Quarg here."

name: Midnight Pug Cthogha Confrontation

values: Midnight Pug Cthogha First Contact: offered

children.key: As you take in the sights of the spaceport, a voice from behind you catches your attention. "Are you enjoying the show?" Turning around, you see a Pug holding a large box of popcorn. "Want some? It's got 'movie theater' butter. This was supposedly a popular snack with a segment of your species population a millenia ago." The Pug shoves a handfull of the popcorn into its mouth. "Mmm! Ths s vry tsty."
"You knew I'd lead the Quarg away."

The Pug grins. "We expected them to go home a long time ago. But the Quarg who we allowed to steal the wormhole borer didn't take the others with it. They refused to abandon 'their duty' to keep watch over Cthogha." The Pug munches on more popcorn. After swallowing it continues. "But you did great! You found the wormhole borer and figured out how to open a new one." It crunches more popcorn. "Even so, the Quarg were reluctant to do what needed to be done to acquire the keys to pass through the gate. To make matters worse, they became chummy with the robotic law mongers even after a few of them were tossed into Incarceration Cells." The Pug shakes its head. "But your arrival must have made their descendants homesick. Now that they're gone we don't have to worry about them interfering with our war plans!" The Pug reaches into the popcorn box. "Oops, I guess there's nothing left for you." It tosses the box aside which vanishes into nothingness.

"The Ignitia are on the cusp of making their own Jump Drives. That isn't our fault, in case you were wondering. This conflict was inevitable. Practically everyone on the Justicar side is stuffed into an Incarceration Cell. The best they can hope for is to be freed with the collapse of their robot overlords. If there are reasonable people among them, perhaps they'll realize that both sides have planets that they can't use but the other side can and build a peaceful future off of that." The Pug pauses before asking, "How does it feel, seeing one of our projects from this side?" You remember the Pug invasion at the end of the Free Worlds war.
The Pug laughs. For some reason the laughter is contagious and you start laughing yourself. When the laughter subsides, the Pug is gone.

You try. The Pug grabs your arm and flawlessly performs the karate move you once saw on a video long ago. You end up lying on the ground looking up at the sky. "You're too tense human. Relax. You need to be calm, like water." The Pug starts performing some martial arts maneuvers. It moves gracefully despite its awkwardly long limbs. "Wah tah!" You roll over to stand up. When you're back on your feet, the Pug is gone.

values: Midnight Pug Cthogha First Contact: offered

name: Quash: Humanika Infiltration 1
description: Take your passengers to <destination>. Then transport them to Trinket in the Sargas system. Payment is 400,000 credits.

values: Take your passengers to <destination>. Then transport them to Trinket in the Sargas system. Payment is 400,000 credits.

children.key: As you are walking through the spaceport, three men and a woman all wearing nondescript clothing appear out of nowhere and offer you 400,000 credits for discreet passage to <destination>. After they complete some business there, they'll need transportation to Trinket in the Sargas system.

Seeing you hesitate, they explain that their previous pilot was caught smuggling ringworld shavings, an illegal drug, and they need a replacement pilot for a job they couldn't refuse. Transporting them might be very dangerous. On the other hand, they're offering a small fortune...

As you approach <planet>, your passengers start unpacking and equipping some gear. They're all armed now. One of the men even has a sniper rifle. It's obvious they're up to no good. But it's too late to back out. Their leader, the one they refer to as "Commander," tells you to land at a specific site. You notice that this location is nowhere near the spaceport...

children.key: You land at the designated site, a parking lot of what appears to be a ruined building abandoned long ago. Commander tells you to wait for them. He promises that you'll get your 400,000 credits once you've safely delivered them to Trinket in the Sargas system. The four well armed passengers disembark from your ship, off to do whatever it is they came here for.
It's obvious they're up to no good and you want no part of that. You fire up your engines and head out, abandoning your passengers and their promised reward.
After an hour, Commander returns... alone and injured. "Go! The others are dead. Get us out of here!" You fire up your engines...

He hesitates a moment, then hands over the Sniper Rifle. "I guess you could also try selling this. That's the best I can offer." He departs, never explaining anything about what happened on Humanika or the mysterious Quarg he was cursing.

children.key: You are surprised to see a Quarg approaching you. "Greetings human. I am in need of transport. Can you help me? I can pay you 90,000 credits after we arrive."
"Welcome aboard. I'll do my best to get you where you're going."
"Sorry, I can't help you right now."
"My ship isn't outfitted to accommodate Quarg-sized passengers."
"What is a Quarg doing on a pirate world?"
"Ah, even a Quarg can fall victim to misfortune. But perhaps my fortunes will take a turn for the better."
"Do not concern yourself. I can manage some discomfort."
"I am glad to hear that. My name is Quash. I'm going to Skuld, in the Archipelago."
"My name is <first> <last>. I'm not familiar with those locations."
"Simply take me to Orbona. Once there the path forward will become clear."

name: Cartography: Quarg Hitchhiker 1.5
description: The path forward to <destination> has been revealed.

values: The path forward to <destination> has been revealed.

When you arrive in Orbona, Quash asks you to transmit a certain coded signal far beyond the edge of the system. Not long after, your navigational computer shows a hyperspace link to a new system has opened! "As promised, the path ahead is clear," says Quash.

children.key: You've visited systems that had more than one star, but what spreads out before you can only be described as a star cluster. You count four star systems in the immediate vicinity. There are intermittent flashes of light as their heliospheres collide, forming bursts of exploding plasma. Amazingly, people live here. There is a surprisingly high amount of traffic, with a variety of different ships moving between the various star systems. Three of the systems have habitable planets, and Quash directs you to land on one of them.

values: Quash says, "Meet me at landing pad Q in the spaceport after an hour to receive your payment. As for the transmission data that unlocks the path to Archipelago, feel free to use it as a bonus for a job well done."

name: Cartography: Quarg Hitchhiker 2

children.key: When you arrive at landing pad Q, you a greeted by a dreadful sight. The Carabao, known as the "cursed" city ship, is featured in many horror stories where the colonists die off one by one as the ship's automated systems accidentally kill them in grisly and gruesome ways.

Quash's voice booms from an external speaker. "I'm glad you finally arrived, Captain <first> <last>. I hope you had no trouble finding your way here. Please, come aboard my new ship. It's called a Carabao." A boarding ramp descends from an open entry hatch. The area within is dark, making it difficult to see the ship's interior from outside.
You tell Quash that it can keep its payment.

"Oh?" Quash responds. "Well, if you insist. Far be it for me to deny your generosity. It was a pleasure doing business with you, Captain <first> <last>. I look forward to employing your services again someday." The boarding ramp retracts into the Carabao and the hatch closes.

Soon after you enter, your eyes adjust to the low light. One corner of the room is occupied by an alien device that provides the only internal light source. On the floor is a pouch, a briefcase, and a series of bloodstains.

"Sorry about the mess." Quash's voice emanates from a speaker in the ceiling. "The business associate who helped me acquire this vessel chose to alter the terms of our agreement. He chose poorly. I'm certain you are a trustworthy business person who would not engage in such duplicitous behavior. Your payment of 90,000 credits is in the pouch on the floor. Go ahead, you've earned it."

As soon as you touch the briefcase, the entry hatch slams shut. "Tsk. tsk. Captain <first> <last>, I had hoped we could continue to do business in the future." The device in the corner of the room brightens with an eerie light. The heat in the room is also rising. "However, I can't have business associates who are unable to follow simple instructions." Your hair and skin are burning as you bleed out on the floor. Quash's words are drowned out by your screams. After a few moments, the room is dark and silent once again.

values: An unusual Quarg hitchhiker I met on a pirate world. Quash needed transportation to Skuld, another pirate world, in the Archipelago system. Quash has an unusual city ship, a Carabao. It has been featured in many horror stories which have the hapless colonists die gruesome deaths due to accidents caused by the ship's automated systems.

children.key: You scoop up the pouch and begin heading for the exit. "Fare well, Captain <first> <last>. It was a pleasure doing business with you. I look forward to employing your services again someday."

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Cartography: Quarg Hitchhiker 2

Due to your involvement in the archaeology discovery on Zug, the government of Poisonwood invites you to investigate a similar discovery we've uncovered." The message gives instructions for where to land on Poisonwood, but doesn't describe what was found there.

values: Acquired an obsolete star map during an information exchange regarding a derelict Coalition war ship found on Poisonwood. Someone with more knowledge regarding the movements of the stars might be able to figure out where the systems on this map are currently located.

children.key: The invitation provided instructions to a landing site far from the usual spaceport. As you descend, you see that they have dug out a tunnel into the side of a mountain. A woman meets you at the landing site. She introduces herself,"My name is Millie. I'm in charge of this excavation." Millie leads you towards the tunnel as she talks. "To be honest, we were hoping to lure Albert Foster out here by getting you involved. But it seems he is still busy with his work on Zug." Not far into the tunnel, you see what they are digging out of the earth.

The invitation provided instructions to a landing site far from the usual spaceport. As you descend, you see that they have dug out a tunnel into the side of a mountain. A woman meets you at the landing site. She introduces herself,"My name is Millie. I'm in charge of this excavation. You met my aunt, the governor of Poisonwood, some time ago." Millie leads you towards the tunnel as she talks. "To be honest, we were hoping to lure Albert Foster out here by getting you involved. But it seems he is still busy with his work on Zug." Not far into the tunnel, you see what they are digging out of the earth.
It's a spaceship. You've never seen one like this before, but the design resembles the style used by the Saryd of the Coalition.
It's a rare ancient Saryd warship. You've seen this design at least once before.

"It looks like the ship crash landed here ages ago. Most of the systems are ruined. It's a miracle that the hull is intact at all. The skeletal remains of the crew lead us to believe they may have resembled the centaurs from ancient mythology." She turns to you. "The only thing we managed to salvage is some system mapping data." She holds up a data chip. "From the look on your face, you know something about this ship. Care to share?"
You agree to tell her everything you know about the Coalition in exchange for the data chip.

children.key: It's been a while since you last visited the archaeological dig site and you are curious at how they have progressed in excavating the hull of that crashed ship. When you arrive, you find that they have excavated what remains of the ship, but have left it to languish exposed to the elements.

Millie arrives to greet you. "Welcome back, Captain <last>. We were hoping to find more buried beyond the ship, but this is all we've found for now. The local government has no plans to keep the wrecked hull. Things might've turned out differently if Foster had shown up, but all we have is you. Would you be interested in purchasing it? We estimate 22,000,000 credits is a fair price for an empty hull of this size and condition."
"Sure, I enjoy restoring old ships to working condition."
"Sorry, I'm not interested in an empty hull."
You fill out the forms and complete the transfer of ownership.

(Remember to visit the outfitter and make sure your new ship is properly outfitted for flight! You may need to import outfits from other worlds in order to make the ship spaceworthy. If so, press "i" to open the info screen and park the ship until you return with the necessary outfits.)

values: Acquired the hull of an old Coalition war ship that was found on Poisonwood. Restoring it to working condition will take considerable resources and effort.

name: Cartography: The Map (Coalition)

children.key: Do you want to show the members of the Coalition a copy of the obsolete star map and ask them what they know about it?

After asking around, you're directed to the astronomy department of a local educational center. "Strange, it is," comments a professor. "A Saryd map this is. Familiar with these stars we are not." They ask you for more information about how and where you obtained the map. After listening to your story, they come to a conclusion. "An exploratory mission, it probably was. Before returning, unfortunate crash they likely had." Without a point of reference to guide them, they are unable to extrapolate the current position of these star systems.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Cartography: The Map (Coalition)

name: Cartography: The Map (Quarg)

children.key: Do you want to show the Quarg a copy of the obsolete star map and ask them what they know about it?

Walking down the principal, alien-looking hall, you decide to stop one of the few Quarg you see there. "Hello, human. How may I be of service?" the Quarg says. You show it the star mapping data and ask what it knows about it. It leans forward to look and is momentarily stunned by what it sees on the star map. It closes its eyes as patches of skin all over the Quarg's body radically shift from the usual grey to blue and red, some spots mixing into purple. The moment passes and its appearance returns to normal. The Quarg opens its eyes and says, "That which was left behind. What was forgotten should remain forgotten. May it remain lost, never to be found." The Quarg stands tall and walks away, apparently unwilling to discuss the matter farther.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Cartography: The Map (Quarg)

name: Cartography: The Map (Remnant)

children.key: Do you want to show the Remnant a copy of the obsolete star map and ask them what they know about it?
After asking around, you are reminded that the Remnant's migration from human space was relatively recent compared to the time period the star map data was supposedly recorded.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Cartography: The Map (Remnant)

name: Cartography: The Map (Hai)

children.key: Do you want to show the Hai a copy of the obsolete star map and ask them what they know about it?

After asking around, a local observatory is recommended to you. The Hai astronomers you find greet you warmly and agree to look at your star mapping data. After a few hours of running a comparison search through their database, they conclude, ironically, that this star map data may be more recent than the charts they have from when the Hai occupied what is now human space. Although they weren't able to determine the current location of these systems, they share what they can about how the stars were aligned farther back in time.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Cartography: The Map (Hai)

Although they weren't able to determine the current location of these systems, they share what they can about how the stars were aligned farther back in time.

children.key: While walking around the spaceport, you notice a Quarg towering over the crowd. It spots you and approaches. As it gets closer you recognize Quash, the Quarg you transported to the Archipelago.
"Greetings, Captain <first> <last>," it says. "I see you have managed to find another hidden system."
"How many of these systems are there?"
"What brings you to Wang Xiang Tai?"
"There is a specific hidden system I am searching for. Perhaps you could help me once again."
"What do you need me to do?"
"I hope this won't involve anything illegal."
"I merely need transportation to the Underworld of the planet below. A simple task."
"What happened to the ship you had the last time we met?"
"I do not feel comfortable piloting a ship of that size through underground caverns..."
"Good point. So how much are you offering?"
"What makes you think I can do it?"

Quash gently pats you on the shoulder. "Have confidence in yourself. Other humans have spoken highly of your piloting skills. After our previous journey together, I have no doubt that reputation is well earned."
"Thanks. So how much are you offering?"

"I can share the knowledge I gain of the hidden system I am looking for. I'll add in the hyperspace link codes for Diyu if you don't already have them." A chance to uncover another hidden system isn't something to pass up on.

values: Bring Quash to an underground pirate hideout on <origin> to complete a trade. Then return it to <planet>.

children.key: Quash directs you to a certain canyon. In a deep secluded area surrounded by steep canyon walls, you find a tunnel large enough to squeeze your ship through...

You can't help but feel a tinge of claustrophobia as you navigate your ship through the narrow tunnels. The occasional stalactite pierces your shields and scrapes your hull. The damage is inconsequential, but you still cringe at the thought of the damage to the paint. After an hour the tunnel opens up into a large cavern that has several other tunnels leading away from it. You've finally reached your destination.

"Land here," Quash instructs. Soon after, a Hai shield beetle descends from a tunnel farther up. "Relax captain. These people have brought something for me. Please open the hatch so that I may meet them.

"You should stay here. Keep the ship's weapons powered up, in case I need backup." Quash disembarks the ship and heads out to meet the pirates. Despite having a Hai ship, they look like ordinary humans. They talk for a bit and one of them hands Quash something which it pockets. They talk for a while more before going their separate ways.

Suddenly the pirate ship opens fire, shooting Quash in the back! The ship is reorienting its guns towards you. It looks like they've decided your ship is an easy target. You'd better get out of here fast.
[MISSION FAILED] You have failed a key part of the Cartography plot. If life were a game, you could load a previous save file and try again, preferably with a more powerful warship.
Quash makes it safely back to the ship. "I suggest we leave while everyone is still pretending to be civilized."

You've managed to defeat the White Rabbit. Quash asks that you return to <destination>.

children.key: You find the landing pad where Quash's ship is docked. The Quarg comes out to meet you and hands over a data chip. "A small system near Gacrux."
"Is this the system you were looking for?"
"No. But I know where to find that data. Would you be interested in escorting me there?"
"Sure. I'd also like to learn the location of the system you are searching for."
"Sorry, I have other things to do."
"And these other things are more important than uncovering secret systems and planets that may be unknown to the rest of humanity?"
"Very well. Go on. Be on your way now. Shoo." The Quarg turns to leave.
"Wait. Fine, I'll join you on your journey."
The Quarg walks away. Wherever it's final destination is, you're not ready to follow it there.
"Good. Are you familiar with the Coalition? Our destination is The Ring of Friendship, a former Quarg ringworld."
"Will the Heliarchs allow a Quarg to land?"

values: [MISSION FAILURE] You have failed as important part of the Cartography mission chain. If life were a game, you could load a save file and try again.

Escorted Quash's ship, the Halcyon, to the Ring of Friendship in Coalition space. Amazingly, the Heliarch allowed Quash to land. Quash seems to have made some sort of deal with the Heliarch and we parted ways while Quash works with them.

The Heliarch refer to Quash as 'The Outcast'. Apparently, Quash is some sort of criminal amongst the Quarg. Considering that the previous two times I've met Quash were on pirate worlds, I shouldn't be surprised.

children.key: Surprisingly, the Heliarchs allow Quash to land. You land your own ship at the adjacent landing pad and watch as a delegation greets Quash. Three Heliarch translators greet it in a language you do not recognize. There is some argument and negotiation, then Quash boards his ship and begins to take off.
Meanwhile, you have your own Heliarch delegation ready to welcome you. A Saryd addresses you. "Greetings human. Why The Outcast, do you travel with?"
"Yes," replies a Kimek. "Not welcome amongst its fellow Quarg, The Outcast is. Of many crimes, The Outcast is guilty."
Upon reflection, you recall that both times you encountered Quash were on pirate worlds. Perhaps Quash wasn't so out of place there after all.
An Arach speaks up. "Beware human. Though cast out from its own society The Outcast is, for good reason the Quarg must have."
"Why do the Heliarch tolerate The Outcast's presence?"
"Why is The Outcast not welcome among the Quarg?"
The Kimek answers, "Knowledgeable The Outcast is. Of the ringwords. Of the Quarg. Of the space beyond. Too useful, the services it offers, to not employ."
The Saryd shrugs. "Unknown their reasons are. Ancient, the hostilities between them are. Even before united, the Coalition were, did the Quarg hunt The Outcast when pass through our space it did."
You thank the Heliarchs before boarding your ship to follow Quash. Before launching, you find that Quash has already sent you a message:

"The Heliarch have requested I lend them my expertise regarding some minor technical matters on the Ring of Wisdom. This may take a while. I'll contact you when I am finished. In the meantime, have you visited the Quarg ringworld to the west? I've attached the map data if you haven't. It's quite a sight!"

children.key: The architecture of the station reminds you of Quarg designs you've seen before. Quash easily locates the station's control room. All of the data displays are in a language you are unfamiliar with. Quash reaches for the control panel...

Quash answers while gesturing at a data display. "This Quarloque is networked with others in the nebula. They are generating gravitational distortions that make it difficult to detect this nebula and dive deeper within. I'm going to deactivate them."
"I'm not sure that's a good idea."
Quash turns towards you. "The Quarloques were placed here to prevent anyone from seeing what is hidden within the nebula. Doesn't that pique your curiosity?"
"I'd like to explore the rest of the nebula first."

Quash backs away from the control panel. "Why do humans always choose to do things the hard way? The gravity distortions may make it difficult to dive deeper into the nebula. Take care not to crash your ship into a clump of dark matter..." Quash returns to the Halcyon.
Quash backs away from the control panel. "I... sense that we have done this before. Could this be a time loop? Strong gravitational distortions could cause such a phenomenon."
"But the date and time seem correct."

The Quarg looks at the Celestial Compass. "Our spacial coordinates are also correct. Perhaps what I'm experiencing are memories from an alternate timeline. I believe humans call this Deja Vu. Do you still want to leave the Quarloques active?"
"Yes, I'd like to explore the rest of the nebula first."

This is the first time you've seen a Quarloque being deactivated, but somehow the process seemed familiar enough that you're certain you could repeat it.

children.key: This frozen planet has been separated from its home system and floats free in the empty void. Although the world is uninhabited, there are Quarg ruins here. Most of the buildings have been demolished by some unknown force. As is typical for a Quarg world, the air is too thin for human comfort.

You see the Halcyon parked at one of the spaceport landing pads. Attempts to hail it results in no reply. Before you can finish putting on an environmental suit, Quash has already left the Halcyon and entered the nearby ruin. It's as if the enigmatic Quarg forgot that you were accompanying it.

A few rusting derelict Quarg ships covered by thick frost occupy some of the other landing pads. Most show signs of combat damage. The corpses nearby give the impression that they were frantically trying to repair one of these ships when something caused an abrupt and violent end to their lives. You're uncertain how many centuries they've been here, but the cold has preserved them well enough for you to discern twisted horrifying expressions on their faces.

Overhead, flashes of lightning from the nebula above serve as the main source of lighting on the planet's surface. The eerie glow occasionally flickers as activity shifts among the clouds, causing shadows cast by the ruins to dance about wildly. The ringworld shard seems to hover over the horizon like a tombstone for this dead world.

The entrance leads to a network of tunnels. As you make your way deeper into the facility, you find the air is warmer and some of the power systems are still operational. A strange light in the chamber ahead beckons you forward.

The large chamber has some kind of containment device on a pedestal in the center. It appears to be made of the same material as a Jump Drive. The device is broken, shards of it scattered across the floor. The reflections of light in the broken shards draw your attention to something moving near the ceiling above.
You sense a familiar feeling, like a half forgotten dream beckoning to you from under your hazy subconsciousness...

With the way it acts, you're certain this is an alien lifeform. It looks translucent, as if it consists of a hazy mist. The entity seems to be aware of your presence and you suspect it has been observing you for some time. Slowly, it starts to descend.
"Back away from the entity, Captain <first> <last>." Quash enters the chamber and gives you a stern warning. The mysterious entity hesitates, seeming to study the actions of its two guests.
(Do as Quash says. Back away from the entity.)
(Ignore Quash and beckon the entity towards you.)
You back away from the entity. As you do, Quash steps forward and stretches its arms wide. The entity regards the both of you and flies towards Quash!
You shoot the entity but the bullets have no effect. It envelopes Quash and the Quarg bellows in agony. As it writhes about, the Celestial Compass falls onto the floor and rolls towards you.
(Wait to see what happens to Quash.)

You fire your gun at Quash! Several bullets dig into its flesh. Quash screams and drops the Celestial Compass onto the floor where it rolls towards you. Then the entity envelopes Quash and the Quarg bellows in agony.

You snatch up the compass and run. As you flee through the empty passages back to your ship, the alien sound of Quash's tortured wails echo behind you. Boarding the <ship>, you get back into orbit and are deciding your next course of action when a fleet of Quarg warships arrives. They hail you.

They hail you.

Before the words leave your lips, the Halcyon launches. Most of the Quarg fleet moves to intercept. The old city ship is no match for them. Once the Halcyon is completely destroyed, the Quarg hail you. "Human. Has The Outcast's grip on your mind been broken? Are you in control of yourself?" It waits expectantly for you to answer.

name: Midnight Pictograph 1
description: Transport some ancient Earth artifacts to <destination>. Do not, under any circumstance, look inside the crate. Payment is <payment>.

values: Transport some ancient Earth artifacts to <destination>. Do not, under any circumstance, look inside the crate. Payment is <payment>.

children.key: When you return to your ship you find a strange woman with unkempt hair and soda pop spectacles tapping her foot as she waits impatiently. Gripped in her hand is a clipboard which she glances at occasionally. Upon spotting you, she rushes over and asks with a nasal voice, "Are you Captain <first> <last>?"

"I'm a researcher specializing in archaeological pre-history. You've been highly recommended by my colleagues at <planet> and I'd like for you to transport some sensitive artifacts recently recovered from the west Saharan marshes to the station in <system>.
"Is the pay going to be the same as before?"

"It'll be ten times what he offered. But there's a catch. Absolutely no peeking at the artifacts! The crate must remain sealed at all times." She seems determined to make sure you don't look at the contents.

She seems taken aback before stammering out a response, "Oh, uh... They're, uh, extremely sensitive. Any exposure to normal air will damage them. Yeah, that's it..." She doesn't sound too confident with that statement.
"What? Why not? I'm offering ten times what was paid last time. Ten!"
She scowls and scribbles something on her clipboard before walking away.

"You will? That's great! I'll have the crate brought here within the hour. Also, I'm coming along, so keep a bunk open for me. My name's Tart Concord." Tart scribbles something on her clipboard and walks away. This could be an interesting trip."
Tart double checks the crate before retiring to her bunk. She says, "Remember, no peeking at what's inside! These artifacts are sensitive. Sensitive!"
You're almost at Alexandria. Tart appears to be asleep. Do you dare peek inside the crate?
Are you sure? This will be your last chance...

Just as you pry the lid off, Tart screams from the entrance to the cargo bay, "What are you doing!?!" You drop the lid haphazardly back onto the crate as she rushes over and nervously asks, "Did you see? Did you see?"

There is a momentary pause as she registers your response in her brain. She quickly adjusts the lid to seal the crate back up. "Whew, that was a close call!" She smiles in relief then suddenly frowns. "Captain <last>, I'm very disappointed in you. Please get us to Alexandria so we can safely unload these artifacts someplace safe. And don't you dare try to open the crate again! Hmph." She insists on standing guard over the crate until you land.

She sighs. "I suppose what was seen can't be unseen. As you probably know, the west Sahara wasn't always a jungle marsh. Centuries ago it was dry desert. But thanks to long term erosion, the sand dunes have slowly washed away. A recent typhoon finally uncovered ancient ruins that pre-date the Pyramids. That much was reported in the news." She slides the lid off the crate. "This, however, has been kept secret.

"A stone tablet bearing a pictograph from a human civilization so ancient we don't know its name." It appears to depict ancient humans kneeling before a figure of some importance. "What do you make of it?"
"Is it shooting lightning from its hand?"
"What's the red thing over its head?"
"Alright, I suppose you have a point."

"I thought your involvement with Albert Foster's archaeological discovery on Zug might have granted you some insight. Are you sure you don't have any impressions on this?" she gestures at the pictograph.

"It might be lightning or it might be symbolic of 'magic'. If we were to show primitive humans a Laser Rifle, they might see it as having the ability to shoot lightning... Hmm." She scribbles something on her clipboard. "Does anything else stand out to you?"

"It could be a symbol for the sun or some sort of celestial entity associated with the figure standing beneath it... Hmm." She scribbles something on her clipboard. "Does anything else stand out to you?"

"That certainly is eye catching. It clearly depicts that figure as non-human. When one also considers its taller stature... Hmm." She scribbles something on her clipboard. "Does anything else stand out to you?"
Tart looks over the notes she wrote on her clipboard. "Captain <first>, do you suppose the figure the humans are kneeling to could be a Quarg?"

Tart looks relieved. "Thank you. I happen to think so too. The red marking above its head may be symbolic of the Quarg coming down from space. But this is still only speculation. And there are some who would refuse to even consider the possibility that the Quarg might have visited prehistoric humans and meddled in our ancestor's affairs. The potential social upheaval that could result from this theory getting out might be catastrophic."
She scribbles something on her clipboard. "I suppose it is... Thank you for sharing your impressions with me."
"May I take a photo of the pictograph?"
Tart's response is swift and sure. "Absolutely not!" As she reaches for the lid, you instinctively glance at the nearest cargo bay security camera...

Tart secures the lid back onto the crate. "Please keep the existence of this artifact a secret. Until Alexandria is able to determine what this pictograph truly represents, we would prefer it not be exposed to wild speculations from the general public." She insists on standing guard over the crate until you land.

name: Midnight Pictograph 2

children.key: Do you want to try selling the Ancient Pictograph to "Fine Art and Cultural Treasures"?

You enter the shop and see that he has another customer, a figure in a dark cloak. Though her face is obscured, from what you can see of her figure, she appears to be a woman. Upon your entrance, she retreats to a back room while the clerk turns his attention towards you. "Welcome back! How can I help you today?"
"Maybe I should come back when you aren't busy..."
"Don't worry about her. Tell me, what brought you here today?"
You tell him about the photo of the Ancient Pictograph. "You're in luck. I know just the person who might be interested in this." He turns towards the back room. "Greythatch!"
The woman from earlier peeks out from the back room. "This had better be good." Lowering her hood she asks,"What's so important you felt the need to call out my name?"
"Sorry," apologizes the clerk, "But you have to hear this!" Graythatch waits patiently while you repeat your story about the Ancient Pictograph.
After you finish your story she mulls it over. "Sounds ridiculous. I don't suppose you'd be willing to show me this photo of an alleged unique artifact?" What will you do?
She scoffs. "Yeah, figures. Don't waste my time on nonsense." Greythatch leaves and the shop clerk decides to close up early.
You try to show her the photo, taking care to obscure it as best as you can from any security cameras the "Fine Art and Cultural Treasures?" might have hidden away. Upon seeing the photo, she gasps.

A smirk slowly crawls across the shop clerk's face. "Well, what do you think? The info we heard about Tart Concord going to Earth only to immediately turn around and haul something back to Alexandria seems to line up with this story about an Ancient Pictograph being discovered at around the same time."

"But if this is real, that would mean..." Her words trail off. She looks at you, "The Quarg will probably freak out if they know you have this photo. Let me take it off your hands for, say, eight hundred twenty five thousand."

"Isn't it obvious?" Greythatch whispers, "That tall figure flinging lightning over the crowd is definitely a Quarg. Look at its legs." Regardless of if that's true or not, there's still the issue of whether or not you'll sell the photo.

Greythatch grimaces, then pulls her hood back over her head. "Suit yourself. It's just a blurry photo." Although most of her face is obscured, you can see that she's frowning. She leaves the shop and the clerk decides to close up early.
Greythatch swallows. "Fine. But make sure you delete any copies you have left. If you backstab me, I'll make sure to tell the Quarg about you!"
You agree to her terms and transfer your only copy of the photo to her in exchange for <payment>.

children.key: At the spaceport bar some Hai freighter pilots are exchanging stories. They invite you to join them and share your experiences flying beyond Hai space. You start with some stories from the early days when you were just starting out. The tale of your first encounter with pirates prompts another pilot to relate his own experience meeting the Unfettered for the first time. Another pilot offers to buy you a drink and asks about your experiences flying outside of human space. You begin with the tale of how you found Hai space. This gets a few giggles from the crowd. The night wears on as more stories are told and more drinks are poured. Eventually, you mention the abandoned Hai systems to the far west near Terminus.
"You've been to the Ancestral Lands?" they ask.

You tell them about the current state of those worlds. The Hai listen intently, occasionally asking questions. The barkeep announces that the bar is closing as you finish your tale. Finishing your drinks, the other pilots thank you for sharing your stories and wish you a good night.

You find Nanachi, the Hai pilot who you helped start out, at a spaceport cafe. She's reading a copy of "Journey to the Southwest" when she notices you and waves you over to join her. She tells you about her experiences as a captain. You also tell her about how your life has been ever since you last met, of your adventures and how far you've come.

When you mention that you've been to the ancient Hai worlds near Terminus, she becomes especially attentive. She asks several questions and eagerly listens to your answers. Eventually, the conversation moves on to other topics. You keep swapping stories for hours, until the cafe is ready to close.

name: Vault Weapon Quash 2
description: Two Quarg weapons were among the items stolen from Farpoint's evidence vault. Search the pirate systems for them.

values: Two Quarg weapons were among the items stolen from Farpoint's evidence vault. Search the pirate systems for them.

children.key: You are lead to an underground interrogation room where a familiar face awaits. "Welcome Captain <last>, I've been expecting you." You never thought you'd meet Raven again. "Our operatives have determined that you successfully recovered some of the weapons that were stolen from this facility's evidence vault."
"Just lucky to be in the right place at the right time."
"We are hoping you could put that luck to work for us."

"While we managed to find the collaborator who made the heist possible, the Republic's own recovery efforts have not been as productive. And so we've decided to reach out to you for assistance. Specifically, for two Quarg weapons that are of particular interest." She shows you data on them: a Quantum Phase Pistol and a Graviton Generator. "As you can see, the power of these weapons far exceeds the ones you've retrieved so far. And that doesn't even begin to address the diplomatic issue that could arise if the Quarg find out we've been keeping them here."
"How did the Navy get their hands on these?"
"What can you tell me about the Quantum Phase Pistol?"
"What can you tell me about the Graviton Generator?"
"What diplomatic concerns are there with the Quarg?"
"What's in it for me if I help you?"
"Alright, I'll help track down these weapons."
"Thank you for agreeing to help. I wish you luck in your search. Remember, the existence of these weapons is top secret. Take care not to mention them in any communications."

"Like the other exotic stolen weapons, they were confiscated from pirates during the early days of the Republic. The pirates claimed that these weapons were sold to them by a rogue Quarg named..." She pauses to look through some notes. "Quiche? That must be a typo. Well, I suppose that's not important. These events took place centuries ago and likely have no bearing on the current situation."

"The data indicates that once this weapon locks onto a target, the energy projectiles it fires will home in on their target, phasing though any matter blocking its path. Very suitable for assassinations."
"This device creates miniature black holes. A personal weapon of mass destruction is not to be taken lightly."
"The Quarg do not approve of humans using their technology. There are unconfirmed reports of Quarg using violence against humans violating this taboo."
"We are willing to overlook the other stolen weapons that have found their way into your possession..."

description: The Covert mining cartel was probably behind the assassination plot. Head to <destination> to investigate.

values: The Covert mining cartel was probably behind the assassination plot. Head to <destination> to investigate.

children.key: Korban is scheduled to attend a rally being held at a plaza. It's some sort of historical site, with buildings over 1,000 years old. The crowd is already large. Nearby is a bridge and a library.
(Survey the area from a grassy knoll.)

The candidate this rally supports hasn't arrived yet, but there are already thousands of people here. Korban is nowhere to be seen, but a VIP like him may be part of the candidate's entourage. Any of these people could be the assassin. You need a better vantage point...
The crowd is even thicker now. Any of these people could be the assassin. You need a better vantage point...

While nearby, the bridge is some distance away from the stage where the candidate and his entourage will be standing. But it's difficult to hide here. A sniper using the bridge would be easy to spot. No one else is here at the moment.
When you return to the bridge, onlookers have gathered on the side facing the plaza. None of them appear to be armed.
The library is a tall building. Several dark windows face the plaza. A sniper could be hiding in any one of them. The door is locked...

You've spent hours searching the area with nothing to show for it. Standing on a grassy knoll, you are surrounded by onlookers who arrived too late to get closer to the stage. The candidate's entourage has arrived and Korban is among them.

While you are trying to find the assassin, an energy blast flies down from one of the library windows and kills Korban! Security returns fire as the crowd panics and starts stampeding! Some are running in your direction and you are knocked down by the rushing throngs. You try to get back up but thousands of feet are bludgeoning you to death. Your search ends here...
You spot some movement in the upper windows...

You start running but you don't make it in time. An energy blast flies down from the library window and kills Korban! Security returns fire as the crowd panics and starts stampeding! Some are running in your direction and you are knocked down by the rushing throngs. You try to get back up but thousands of feet are bludgeoning you to death. Your search ends here...

You aim a shot at the window and fire! The crowd screams and runs away from you. Security has their own guns out, but realizing you weren't aiming at the stage, makes no move to return fire. Korban sees you and nods. You quickly run towards the library, finding the door unlocked. Stepping into the building, you run into the shooter!
(Do this karate move I saw in a video one time.)

Before you can get into a proper stance, the assassin fires with the Quantum Phase Pistol. You react by diving behind a book case, but the energy bolt phases through the shelf and slams into you! You hear the security team fighting the assassin as your consciousness drifts into oblivion.
You are quicker on the draw. The assassin is lying on the ground, a pool of blood forming from the wound you put into his shoulder. Taking the pistol he was wielding, you ask:

The assassin spits at you. Rally security arrives with Korban. Alastair says, "We meet again Captain <last>. It seems I am in your debt. This assassin was likely hired by the Covert mining cartel. We've always been at odds, even after I resigned." Alistair's eyes linger on the alien pistol gripped in your hand, but says nothing. Looking down at the assassin he continues, "We'll handle the rest. Syndicate Security and Republic Intelligence will have a lot of questions for this one."
Having retrieved the Quantum Phase Pistol, it's not clear where to search next. With no other leads on the Graviton Generator, you consider heading to Covert.

values: Saved Alistair Korban from an assassination attempt on Earth.
You spot the remains of a freighter adrift. The hull appears to have imploded. Check the vessel before landing on Covert.
This ship belonged to the Covert mining cartel. The cargo bays that haven't been crushed by whatever caused the implosion are empty and all crewmembers are dead.

children.key: The attack on the Underdark is the hot topic of conversation at the spaceport bar. As the story goes, a few months ago the Covert mining cartel got ahold of an alien device that could quickly convert large amounts of coal into diamonds. The cartel employee responsible for safeguarding the device stabbed the cartel in the back and has become a pirate warlord. It turns out the device can be used as a powerful weapon, and the Underdark was its latest victim. The cartel has placed a hefty bounty on his ship, the Diabolos. While it has already made several attacks on cartel ships in Gienah, they must be using another pirate outpost as their base of operations.

The Diabolos is surrounded by a fleet of other pirate ships. The alien device its captain stole from the mining cartel must have helped him to quickly gain a large following. Capture the ship to get ahold of that device!
When the dying captain fell in battle, he dropped the Quarg Graviton Generator. It lies just out of his reach, but he still spends the last of his strength in a futile attempt to reach it.

You've confirmed that the device stolen from the mining cartel is actually the Quarg Graviton Generator stolen from Farpoint. Before deciding what to do with it, you might consider returning to <origin> and collecting the bounty on the Diabolos.

This is probably the safest course of action. As long as the Quarg don't catch you with them, everything should be fine...
You've decided to keep the weapons for yourself. They are powerful, but dangerous. If the Quarg ever catch you with them, things could turn ugly.

name: Midnight Lost Orphan Atrocity: Quarg

children.key: Your ship loses all power immediately upon touching down on the landing pad. As you walk around to try and find the problem, you pass by your hatch. You find that it is already opened with dozens of Quarg coming in, all clad in elegant full-body armor suits.

You stretch out your arms, preparing to wield the terrifying power of Midnight's Lost Orphan... But it's not there! The power, the presence, of the entity is gone! The Quarg are speaking to you, but it's hard to focus on their words as the realization that the Orphan abandoned you settles in.
"<first> <last>, you are found to be in illegal possession of Quarg equipment. Our devices are precious and ours alone. Though it is regrettable, we must-"

Before the Quarg finishes its sentence one of the other Quarg falls to the floor and begins moaning in agony! Some point their weapons at you while the others stare in shock at the scene before them. The skin of the Quarg who spoke to you earlier takes on a reddish purple tinge as it raises its voice and points at you, "The entity! Stop them!" But by this point the attention of all the other Quarg has shifted to the one that was writhing on the floor.

It calmly stands up. Spreading its arms, it gasps. "I have been chosen! The power... The power is mine to wield!" The blood vessels of you and the other Quarg suddenly burst as your blood flows backwards! Convulsing in pain, you collapse to the floor. While your life drains away, the Orphan's new host begins a fresh journey of galactic atrocities.

Before the Quarg finishes its sentence a nearby door opens. The skin tone of several of the Quarg standing nearby shifts to a mix of purple and red. Oddly, you don't recall what room that door leads to. Several Quarg glare as you step closer to look in. Beyond the doorway is some sort of device cobbled together from stolen Quarg technology. You don't remember for certain what it does, but your gut reaction is that this is some kind of weapon designed to cause mass destruction on a galactic scale...

Before the Quarg finishes its sentence a nearby door opens. The skin tone of several of the Quarg standing nearby shifts to a sickly pale yellow as they recoil from whatever lies beyond. Curiously, you can't seem to recall what room that door leads to and step closer to look in. There, an unfortunate Quarg lies on an operating table with it's body splayed open. The organs of the still living Quarg glisten under a bright surgical lamp as they shudder, exposed for all to see. Equally disturbing are the body parts of other alien species unnaturally grafted onto its body...

Before the Quarg finishes its sentence the floor panel it is standing on suddenly collapses, dropping it into a hidden compartment below. Strangely, you don't remember having such a compartment on the <ship>. Your thoughts are interrupted by an unsettling alien sound coming from the hole. You and the other Quarg who didn't fall in peer into the gap to see the first Quarg who addressed you earlier is waste deep in the blood spattered corpses of several sentient species, both human and alien. The disturbing sound reverberating through the chamber is the Quarg's anguished wailing...

Before the Quarg finishes its sentence one of the nearby ceiling tiles falls away and the rotting decapitated head of a Quarg tumbles out. Several more severed body parts pour out after it as blood starts seeping from the seams between the tiles. You have no idea how they got there...

They don't allow you to get as much as a word out before one of the guards has locked your arms behind your back, completely halting your attempts to fight back with surprisingly little effort. You are brought before something akin to a Quarg jury, where you are found guilty of intergalactic atrocities you don't remember committing. At the end of it all, they sentence you to life imprisonment.

You spend the rest of your days in the same cell, which although large and comfortable, quickly proves plain and dull. You're kept in very good health and are well fed, but the Quarg do not allow you to leave the cell and seldom entertain your attempts at striking conversation. You get few visitors and can only wonder what life would've been like had you the chance to live out all these years in freedom, the captain of a starship.

children.key: You locate the warehouse that was indicated in the message and land near it. On the way down, you notice several nearby hobos huddled by bonfires. It's difficult to see, but you are certain that they are armed with weapons.
You decide that the presence of the armed hobos is a risk you're unwilling to bear and abort the landing.

You make sure the gun at your hip is fully loaded before opening the cargo bay doors. A bald man in a gaudy suit waves at you and holds up a data pad. "Simply confirm payment on this data pad and it's all yours!"
"What, exactly, am I buying?" you ask.

"Behold!" he gestures towards the warehouse. As he speaks, the door to one of the docking bays slides open and inside is a power system. "The Quantum Vacuum Battery! Looted from a derelict Quarg vessel, it eventually found its way into our inventory."
By the time he finishes his sales pitch, a cargolift has positioned itself to load the bulky outfit onto your ship.
The salesman holds the data pad out expectantly.

He puts away the data pad. "Unfortunately, it appears we were unable to reach an agreement. Thank you for your time. However, I suggest you depart immediately." The armed hobos are no longer warming themselves by the fires and are instead trudging their way towards the warehouse. You decide to follow the man's suggestion.
"Congratulations on your purchase captain. I'm sure you won't regret it. You'll hear from us again if we happen to acquire any more unique merchandise that might interest you."

name: Midnight Gorgon Angry Squirrels - Phalanx Grenades

values: Midnight Gorgon Angry Squirrels - Phalanx System: failed

children.key: The Unfettered weapons developer Go Foo Ku has been experimenting with Phalanx Systems. Do you want to check his progress?

As you approach his lab, Go Foo Ku suddenly runs out of the front door. At first, you get the impression that he's come out to greet you. However, his panicked expression and dive for cover tell a different story. He narrowly avoids a beam that shoots out from the lab. Fortunately, you seem to be out of range. A few moments later, the light show ends and Go Foo Ku stands up. After dusting himself off, he notices you. "Welcome back monkey! Today is a lucky day for you. My newest prototype is finished! Come, have a look."

The device Go Foo Ku presents resembles a minaturized Phalanx System. "Phalanx Grenade!" Go Foo Ku beams with pride. "Instead of exploding, it sprays the enemy with bursts of laser fire until its charge runs out. You could also set it as a trap to defend against boarders, but its charge doesn't last long. What do you think? Do you want to buy a set of ten for one million credits?" These might be powerful weapons, but if the Quarg catches you with them, they won't be happy.
"I don't want to anger the Quarg."
Go Foo Ku looks disappointed. "Silly monkey! I thought you had more courage in you." He begins packing the grenades away.
Go Foo Ku ignores your response and quietly finishes packing the grenades away and you leave.

name: Grave Digger: Stolen Kestrel

values: The prototype Kestrel I helped Tarazed develop was stolen last night. The Wayfarer authorities are still searching for the thief.

children.key: The spaceport is bustling with activity. Tarazed security technicians are checking the security systems at each landing pad. Pilots are being asked to wait with their ships until the checks are complete. As you look about the port you spot Charles Atinoda supervising a squad of guards. On second thought, it looks more like the guards are questioning him. He looks tense and frustrated.
After the guards are done with him, he notices you and waves as he approaches. "Captain <last>, welcome back! Too bad it isn't under better circumstances."

"Someone stole the prototype Kestrel from its storage hangar last night. The same one you previously fought against, with some minor upgrades. The hangar security systems were damaged and the entire squad of guards who had been assigned to protect the ship were killed by the thieves. Whoever did this must be highly skilled professionals."

Charles sighs. "I was suspected because I had developed a habit of taking the prototype out on test flights... during my weekends off. And, well..." he looks down dejectedly. "There was some concern that I might not have properly reactivated the security systems when returning the ship to its hangar."
You can see that Charles is genuinely saddened by the theft.
"That prototype was my dream ship, <first>. The thief didn't just steal a ship. He stole my dream."

name: Grave Digger: Void Rifle

children.key: As you land you notice Plume pacing back and forth at the spaceport. As you complete your landing he notices you and waves.
"Welcome back Captain <last>. Have you met Captain Lu Bu? He arrived here from the old worlds like you did and started working with us as well."
The name doesn't sound familiar at all.

"He is a competent captain and has done good work fighting the Korath. His ship, the Grave Digger, is a prototype Kestrel outfitted with exotic devices. But I do not like his attitude. He recently returned from an expedition to visit the Void Sprites with one of their tentacles! Not only did he jeapardize our future research by risking the wrath of the Archons, he did not even store the severed appendage properly! There are bloodstains on my desk that I have not been able to clear out!" Plume shudders in disgust.
"Do you think he will attack the Void Sprites again?"
"What kind of person would harm those magnificent creatures?"
You remember your last visit with the Void Sprites; an amazing memory you won't soon forget.
"A normal man might fear the wrath of the Archons. But he is not a normal man."
Another researcher motions for Plume's attention. "Looks like I have to get back to work. Thanks for your time <first>. Beware of Lu Bu. That man will likely betray the trust of our people."

values: Another human has found his way into Remnant space. Captain Lu Bu seems to be the culprit behind the theft of the stolen Kestrel prototype from Wayfarer. According to Plume, Lu Bu is a vicious warrior who has no qualms with regard to harming the Void Sprites. If I ever run into him, I doubt we'd get along.

name: Grave Digger: Penguin

children.key: As you land you notice Taely at the spaceport looking up at the sky in the direction of arriving flights. As you complete your landing she makes a welcoming gesture.
"Welcome back Captain <last>. Have you met Lu Bu, captain of the Grave Digger? He arrived here from the old worlds like you did and started working with us as well."
The name doesn't sound familiar at all.
"He is a competent captain and has done good work fighting the Korath. His ship, the Grave Digger, is a prototype Kestrel outfitted with exotic devices. But I do not like his attitude.
"Frankly, I am starting to suspect the blood test was wrong. If not for those test results, I would assume he was descended from an Alpha."

"And now, I wonder if I made a mistake. He recently returned from an expedition to visit the Void Sprites with some fascinating genetic samples. This proved useful in finalizing development of a new ship. Yesterday I let him take the prototype out for a test flight. But something about his demeanor gives me the impression he will not be returning with it anytime soon."

A dock worker motions to Taely while pointing to a broken jump drive being unloaded at the adjoining landing pad. She gestures back. "Thank you for your time <first>. Beware of Lu Bu. That man will likely betray the trust of our people," she signs before running off to supervise their latest acquisition.

values: Another human has found his way into Remnant space. Captain Lu Bu seems to be the culprit behind the theft of the stolen Kestrel prototype from Wayfarer. After talking with Taely, I get the impression Lu Bu may even have an arsenal of stolen technology. If we ever crossed paths, he might find my ship a tempting target.

"What, exactly, am I buying?" you ask.

"Behold!" he gestures towards the warehouse. As he speaks, the door to the warehouse swings open and the dock workers are wheeling out several shipping crates. "Interesting. Could we take it to study? We will provide you with fair compensation."

You have a damaged jump drive that the Remnant might be interested in. Do you want to seek out someone to give it to?
You find a Remnant director and inform them about the damaged jump drive that you have.

"Excellent!" he glances at his data pad. "There are several teams working on aspects of the jump drive, and the team with the highest priority for this one is on <planet>. I will notify them to expect you."
He considers this, and sings, "If you wish. Our offer stands, whenever you choose to return."

When you arrive on <planet> there is a team of engineers and mechanics waiting for you, along with a flatbed freight truck. Once you open the cargo doors they quickly free the damaged jump drive from its moorings and load it delicately onto their truck. The lead engineer comes over to hand you <payment>. "Thank you for providing this."
"I will keep a lookout for more."
"Aren't you going to replace it with a hyperdrive?"

The engineer looks at you incredulously. "You mean you were actually trying to use this drive?" He shakes his head in disbelief. "You are lucky you managed to get this far, then. It is surprising that they exist at all, so it is too much to expect them to work too. If you need a replacement drive, there are plenty available in the outfitter."

"Next time you find one of these drives, the landing scans will trigger the system to display a message on the job board listing where it needs to be delivered. A word of warning though; I strongly recommend not trying to use these drives - they may disappear at the most inconvenient of times, and there will not always be an outfitter on hand." He turns and heads off with the rest of the team, turning briefly to give you friendly wave as they disembark.

name: Hunting Beelzebub: Prefect Perfid
description: Visit <destination> to work with Lieutenant Paris of Deep Security on tracking down Beelzebub.

values: Visit <destination> to work with Lieutenant Paris of Deep Security on tracking down Beelzebub.
Beelzebub was formerly Prefect Perfid of the Remnant. He is considered a "Deserter" who has abandoned the Remnant to live the life of a pirate.
Taely has made Modified Inhibitors available at Remnant outfitters. Rather than simply slowing a pursuer while making an escape, this weapon is more suited to entrapping prey.

children.key: You are greeted by a Remnant security force when you exit your ship. They indicate that your participation in a meeting regarding the recent technology sample you delivered is required. After a short walk through the spaceport you find yourself at a firing range where Taely is demonstrating the Modified Inhibitor to Prefect Chilia and Torza.
Torza is the first to respond, signing, "This came from a human pirate ship?"
Taely signs, "Yes. <first>, what was the name of the pirate you were hunting?"
Not knowing the hand gestures for his name, you clearly state:
"Beelzebub," Chilia attempts to mimic your vocalization. He signs,"Were there not some surveillance teams looking into a pirate by that name?"
Torza signs, "Yes, but they have not been able to locate him. It is as if he knows our tracking methods."
Taely interjects, signing, "Whoever made this is intimately familiar with our technology."
"Made? You mean it was not stolen?"

"There can be no doubt," Taely signs. "The serial numbers do not match anything that has passed through our outfitters. Every attribute matches the Inhibitor Cannon other than the firing synchronizer. Our Inhibitor Cannons are designed so a ship can fire a volley and flee while the target is inhibited. With the synchronizer gone, a battery of Modified Inhibitors fires in a steady stream. This setup is ideal for immobilizing and entrapping, a strategy fit for someone who has no intention of fleeing the target: a pirate. This was made by someone with a precise understanding of not only how the Remnant Inhibitor Cannon works, but how the Remnant use it and why that is not ideal for how a pirate would use it."
"It must be 'him'," Chilia signs. There is a sense of sadness in his gestures.
"You mean to suggest," Torza signs. There is hint of disbelief in his gestures.
Taely signs her response, "Your 'Beelzebub' is probably Prefect Perfid, the Deserter."

Chilia begins to sing a sad song. It tells the tale of a Remant Prefect who lead a surveillance mission in human space. When confronted by pirates, the Prefect decided to fight rather than flee. After capturing the pirate ship, he chose to remain behind instead of returning to Remnant space.
Torza punches a wall then signs, "He should never have been allowed to remain there."

Chilia responds, signing "Our people are not prisoners. It is rare, but occasionally one of us chooses to live amongst the ancestral humans." Chilia turns to you. "Captain <last>. Prefect Perfid, Beelzebub, has abandoned life as a Remnant to live as a pirate. We leave his fate in your capable hands." That almost sounds like an assassination order.

While Chilia was singing earlier, Taely was preparing the Modified Inhibitor for transportation to your ship. She signs, "I have instructed our outfitters to supply you with more of these if you request them. Perhaps they will be useful when you confront Beelzebub."
If you're going to hunt down Beelzebub, it might be a good idea to team up with Lieutenant Paris of Deep Security. He should be on <destination>.

values: Search the nearby systems for the Ember Nightmare, then return Paris to <destination>.

children.key: As your ship descends through the atmosphere, you receive a transmission with instructions for the rendezvous. A hidden cave entrance, maze-like caverns, and a large underground chamber are typical scenery for deals in The Underworld. You've parked your ship, but the other party hasn't arrived. Suddenly, a pair of interceptors fly in and open fire!

Following the two Hawks, a Sparrow appears and shoots one down! The other Hawk turns and gets a hit on the Sparrow before crashing into a cavern wall. The Sparrow lands nearby and hails you, "Got room for a passenger? I'll sleep on the floor if I have to." It's Tom! He leaps from the burning Sparrow and runs towards your ship as the flames consume what's left of the wrecked interceptor.
You've barely closed the hatch after he's onboard when another pair of Hawks arrive. "I think we need to get back into space. We're a sitting duck down here," Tom suggests. You're inclined to agree.

You receive a hail. "Did you think I wouldn't notice you snooping around my business? This is a fitting place for you to pass on to the next life." The transmission came from a ship that looks like a heavily modified Albatross. The red glowing lights nestled within the shadows of the ship match the description of the Ember Nightmare, Beelzebub's ship. The Ember Nightmare jumps away as a fleet of dark warships and interceptors swarm around you.
Paris growls, "Forget these guys. We need to chase after Beelzebub!" He must have fled to one of the nearby systems...

values: The Ember Nightmare is here and it's not alone.

name: Sheragi Shenanigans: Sapphire Shield 4
description: Escort the Sapphire Shield to <destination>, where Dr. Stumpernickle will open an account for you.

values: Escort the Sapphire Shield to <destination>, where Dr. Stumpernickle will open an account for you.

children.key: As you walk into the spaceport, you note a fervor spreading through the crowds. Apparently, the Sapphire Shield landed an hour ago. No sooner do you learn this when a well dressed man leading an entourage of similarly dressed individuals addresses you.

"Captain <first> <last>! I am Dr. Wesley Stumpernickle, owner of the Sapphire Shield. The captain of my ship informed me that you took an interest in its systems. As the owner of the Emerald Sword, the only other Sheragi ship to have been found, I would like to hear your opinion on the Sapphire Shield. Why not join me on my ship, where I can give you a tour?"

While Wesley is talking, a crowd of onlookers has gathered to watch the confrontation of sword and shield. Hiding in the crowd is Desyo, wearing a hooded cloak. She hasn't approached you, probably concerned that her status as an alien might be exposed, but she starts gesturing with hand signals once you make eye contact. Clearly, she wants to tell you something. But you have no idea what those signals mean.

As you arrive at the Sapphire Shield, the entourage of well dressed merchants accompanying Wesley depart for their own ships. They seemed disappointed that there wasn't a public spectacle between the owners of the sword and shield. Now that you're able to talk in private, Wesley asks, "What did you learn?"
"I'm fairly certain the Sapphire Shield is a fake" you bluff.

"That's an outrageous accusation," retorts Wesley. "We painstakingly reconstructed the vessel from Sheragi ship parts salvaged in an asteroid field using scans of the Emerald Sword as a guide. While we may have gotten a few things wrong, I assure you we spared no effort to making the Sapphire Shield as close to accurate as possible!"
"I'm having the scans analyzed, but haven't gotten the results back yet," you tell the truth.
"I guess it's only a matter of time until you learn the truth then. Only the hull has been reconstructed from genuine Sheragi ship parts. The outfits are just reproductions."
That's probably what Desyo was trying to tell you. Still... "You can't really call that an accurate representation of a Sheragi ship."
Wesley sighs. "Three thousand a month. That's all I can afford. Please keep quiet about this."

You refuse to accept the bribe. As you turn to leave, Dr. Stumpernickle shoots you in the back! "Sorry, Captain <last>. But the costs for salvaging the Sapphire Shield are eating me alive. If word gets out that the ship is a fake, I could lose the Paradise planet tour gig, and that would be the end for me."
"The Sapphire Shield is a fake," you publicly accuse Dr. Stumpernickle! "I have scanner data that proves it"!

"That's... that's an outrageous accusation," retorts Wesley. "We painstakingly reconstructed the vessel from Sheragi ship parts salvaged in an asteroid field using scans of the Emerald Sword as a guide. While we may have gotten a few things wrong, I assure you we spared no effort to making the Sapphire Shield as close to accurate as possible!"
You respond, "You can't really call that an accurate representation of a Sheragi ship!"
The crowd is eating up this confrontation as the harsh words give way to foul language. Eventually, Dr. Stumpernickle storms off back to the Sapphire Shield.
As the crowd disperses, Desyo approaches you. "That was a surprise," she says. "Now that the truth is out, I wonder if people will still be lining up to see his ship."
The next day, news broadcasts briefly mention the accusations.
"Follow me to Alexandria and I'll set up an account for you."

description: Infiltrate the counterfeiter's manufacturing facility on <planet> to steal their prototype and computer data.

children.key: You receive a message bearing the symbol of familiar stylized reptilian eye. "You seem to be hunting pirates armed with a certain type of weapon. Information on where those weapons are coming from can be yours, for a mere five million credits."
You remember the last time you dealt with this information broker. The information you purchased was expensive, but accurate. What will you do?
"Do you not recall my policy on the price? It is non-negotiable. You will pay my price or I will rescind my offer. The choice is yours."

You hear laughter. "I shall enjoy watching you stumble blindly about the galaxy in search of what could have been handed to you." The communication cuts off, leaving only the slowly fading afterimage of the stylized reptilian eye.

The image of the reptilian eye is replaced with a map of the galaxy. It slowly zooms in to the south, then the Men system, and finally Smuggler's Den. "You'll find what you're looking for in one of the manufacturing facilities." The map zooms in to a specific part of the old space station. "Their Particle Waveform Cannons are made to order. If you steal their prototype and data file, they will not be able to manufacture more. The facility is lightly defended, but the station is not. Oh, I would advise against informing your Quarg friend, unless you want to see everyone on the station die."
You remember your meeting with Yarthis. From its demeanor, the Quarg probably would destroy the station just to stop the counterfeiter.

"See you, Captain <last>. Remember I always do." The communication cuts off, leaving only the slowly fading afterimage of the stylized reptilian eye. You notice that no money has been withdrawn from your account... yet.

values: Mammon has sold me information regarding the counterfeiters distributing fake Sheragi outfits. I'll have to pay the information broker back eventually for this valuable lead.
Mammon offered me information regarding the counterfeiters distributing fake Sheragi outfits. I declined the offer. Hopefully I can track down the source on my own before the Quarg get involved.
You've arrived at <planet>. Head for the spaceport at night when you're ready to infiltrate the counterfeiters facility.

description: Destroy any counterfeiters armed with the Fake Sheragi Cannons and deliver the prototype and data files to <destination>.

children.key: You observe the entrance to the the manufacturing facility indicated by your information broker. As the evening hours roll in, you see a man lock up the facility. You remember him from Dr. Stumpernickle's entourage. Perhaps he was the source for the Sapphire Shield's outfits as well. After a moment, he's gone and the area is deserted.
There's a chain with a combination padlock. Very low tech.
(Just use your trusty pocket laser razor.)
You try to figure out the combination, but fail...
The chain falls away, rattling loudly through the silence of the deserted sector...
The door itself has an electronic security seal. Far more challenging than the padlock.

values: How to Hack a Science Drone For Fun and Profit

children.key: You try to hack the electronic seal, but fail...
There is a loud clang as the electronic seal unlocks. The door slowly slides open, granting you access to the facility.

The "manufacturing facility" is little more than a workshop. A Fake Sheragi Cannon dominates one side of the room, while an unfinished cannon occupies the opposite side of the chamber. The complete cannon is probably the prototype.

Looking around the room, you see a computer, a There May Be Riots poster, a magazine with the Sapphire Shield pictured on the cover, a print out of Albert Foster's interview on the Emerald Sword, and a Subsi Subsidurial Plushie.
When you try using the computer, it asks for a password...
T H E R E M A Y B E R I O T S
S A P P H I R E S H I E L D
A L B E R T F O S T E R
E M E R A L D S W O R D
The password you entered didn't work...
You get into the computer's data files. After searching, you find the prototype blueprints for all the fake Sheragi outfits. You download a copy and delete the originals.
The prototype has been disassembled and stored in your cargo bays. It's time to leave. Bring both your cargo and the blueprint data to <destination>.
You decide to brute force your way in. An entire box of grenades does the job, but you're certain someone must have heard the blast. The remains of the door lie open before you...
You have the Quantum Key Blade...

Taking the orbital direction of the space station into account, you activate the Quantum Key Blade and put yourself out of phase with the rest of reality. You drift through the bulkhead into the room beyond.

values: A fleet of pirate ships is heading right for you. Some are armed with the fake cannons You might have done something to attract the counterfeiter's attention while you were in their workshop.
That's the last of their ships armed with the fake cannons. That should prevent them from making new blueprints.
There may still be counterfeiters armed with Fake Sheragi Cannons or the prototype is on one of your escorts that hasn't arrived in the system.

children.key: You present Yarthis with the prototype of the Fake Sheragi Cannon and the blueprints used by the counterfeiters. With this, the counterfeiters should no longer be able to manufacture these fake Sheragi outfits. The Quarg is satisfied with the results of your investigation.

After asking at several shops, one seems to recognize what you have. "That is a rare artefect from the days of our Predecessors, i'faith! I could tell thee of that armour. But first, I pray thee, do us a favour..." The shopkeeper reveals two intricately carved sculptures. "Privily set thou these twain at the spaceports upon, then hie thee back hither. Shouldst thou perform this task for me, I shall grant thee the knowledge and aid thou dost crave to make use of that armour." name: Midnight Successor Shadow Cloak
description: The Shadow House is searching for an object in Predecessor space. "Thou shalt know it when thou canst not see it." Find this object and deliver it to <destination>.

values: The Shadow House is searching for an object in Predecessor space. "Thou shalt know it when thou canst not see it." Find this object and deliver it to <destination>.

children.key: As you walk through the station, the equipment hums to life. A successor in black clothing appears at the entrance to the shipyard. "Hark, alien! The graven images do work as 'twas aforethought. As I did avow, I shall tell thee of the Predecessor's harness."
"Why did you tell me about Shadow House?"

"This armour's make is a tech that were lost in th' chaos when our kin did flee the space o' our Predecessors. To employ't, certain arts must be applied besides the wonted process f'r configuring modern armours. We hast the means here to perform this feat. Alas, we cannot ourselves forge the stuff. Shouldst thee find more o' this matter, bring it hither to has't installed on modern Successor warships.

"I speak for House Sado, whose name hath been forgot long ere our kind didst meet with thine. Shadow House might well be a name fit enow to call us by, methinks. Our numbers be but scant, yet through the ages we have laboured from the murk to guide, with subtle hand, the course of our folk."

"We have need o' thee. There be an object we desire, which may be found within the stead o' our Predecessors. Thou shalt know it when thou canst not see it. Find this object, and bring it unto us. Until then, we have other, smaller tasks, which we shall entrust thee with. Thine assistance in these matters shall be rewarded."
"What if I tell the High Houses about you?"

The Shadow House agent shudders, flashing shades of yellow while making a noise that seems like laughter. "Then shall thee be put to death. We have insidiated all other Houses, with at least one of our agents. These are dedicate to ensure the House of Shadows remaineth but a tale amongst the common sort."
The agent slithers away into the shadows, leaving you to explore the station on your own.

_internalId: Lost In Midnight/Lost-in-Midnight::Midnight Successor Shadow Cloak

children.key: A Shadow House agent emerges from the shadows. "Thou hast found the thing. We may not see't, yet know we 'tis there."
"Yes, I am here to deliver it to you."
"It's mine. I have no intention of handing it over."
